JTAG Interface (Rear Board)

Detail Value
Label P1_JTAG
Type 20-pin shrouded IDC (2x10, standard ARM JTAG)
Location Immediately left of LPC2361 QFP-100
State Populated with pins

Standard 20-pin ARM JTAG pinout:

  • Odd pins: VTref, nTRST, TDI, TMS, TCK, RTCK, TDO, RESET, DBGRQ, DBGACK
  • Even pins: All GND (except pin 2 = nSRST)

Note: UART0 pins (P0.2/TXD0 = LQFP pin 98, P0.3/RXD0 = LQFP pin 99) are NOT on the JTAG header. The earlier claim that they are "separate pads near the QFP" has no photo or citation and is UNVERIFIED (audit S09, E-03); the Phase 0 continuity check settles it.

LPC2361 pin numbers from the data sheet (docs/DATASHEETS.md (b), Rev. 03, Table 3): P0.2/TXD0 = pin 98, P0.3/RXD0 = pin 99, P0.15/TXD1 = pin 62, P0.16/RXD1 = pin 63. Pins 97 and 96 are VSS and VDD(3V3), never UART pins: a probe or wire placed there lands on ground or the 3.3 V supply. The stock MIDI UART is UART3 per the firmware disassembly (6N138 output to pin 85, P4.29, UNVERIFIED). Which UART pins are free on the board is UNVERIFIED until the continuity check.

KEYBOARD Connector (Rear Board Back)

White FPC connector labeled "KEYBOARD" on rear board solder side. Adjacent test point pads for keyboard scanning signals (TP5-TP20 range visible, associated with DAC and key scanning).

Matches firmware/pico/config.py and docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md section 1. Board: Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350). Nothing here uses wireless.

Phase 0 Bench-Validation Wiring

The two Phase 0 diagrams, schematics/phase0_wiring_schematic.svg and schematics/phase0_breadboard.svg (not embedded in this file), show the same Phase 0 circuit two ways:

  • Schematic (phase0_wiring_schematic.svg) — flat view, elbow-routed nets, useful for understanding what connects to what.
  • Breadboard layout (phase0_breadboard.svg) — top-down view with the Pico straddling the centre channel and jumper paths colour-coded; useful for actually wiring it on the bench.

Phase 0 covers: one OLED on SPI0 (the 0.91″ strip OLED is dropped). Main OLED baseline (owner ruling, 2026-10-17): the owner's 1.3″ 7-pin SPI module, write-only (SCK GP2, MOSI GP3, DC GP4, RES GP5; the CS lead goes to the GND rail, PROVISIONAL, BT-14), powered from the Pico 3V3 pin. GP11 (gate input) is not used in Phase 0. Controller UNVERIFIED (SSD1306 or SH1106: read the module); module pin order UNVERIFIED (common order GND, VCC, D0 = SCK, D1 = MOSI, RES, DC, CS). The 4-pin I²C 1.3″ module is in a TD-3 and not available. Driver: display.py (OLED_SPI) · KY-040 rotary encoder · tap button · RGB LED (3× 220 Ω) · clock IN/OUT (1 kΩ inline; CLOCK IN is loop-back only, no external signals: no CD4049UB on the bench). Power comes from USB; +3V3 and GND are bridged to both top and bottom breadboard rails so peripherals can pull from the closer side.

Free GPIO

3 free pins; GP2 and GP3 (SPI main OLED) and GP11 (gate input) are not free (owner rulings, 2026-10-17):

GPIO Pin# Type Note
GP26 31 ADC0, not fault tolerant PWM slice 5A shared with GP10
GP27 32 ADC1, not fault tolerant —
GP28 34 ADC2, not fault tolerant —

GP6, GP7, GP16, GP17, GP18, GP19 and GP20 are NOT free: they are the aux outputs and clock divider outputs above. No fault-tolerant pin is left: GP11 took the gate input (DECIDED-PROVISIONAL, BT-14; fallback GP27/GP28 with the BT-5 leakage check or a series diode / 3V3 buffer, connection map section 12G). No I²C bus is used on the expander. An I²C display alternative would need GP4/GP5, which are OLED DC/RES, so it requires re-pinning. GP23, GP24, GP25 and GP29 are RP2040-internal and not exposed on the header.

I²C1 EFFIGY / Daisy Seed Expansion — SHELVED

SHELVED (2026-10-17): the EFFIGY pairing is kept as an idea for another project and is not part of this build. No rear JST-XH header is fitted; GP2 and GP3 are now the main OLED's SCK and MOSI and GP11 the gate input (table above).

USB-MIDI (micro-USB)

Pico enumerates as a USB-MIDI class device over its micro-USB port via TinyUSB. Orthogonal to the LPC2361 bridge — gives the DAW/computer a MIDI port named "Macrobrute Pico". Firmware hook: firmware/pico/usbmidi.py (to be implemented).

Important: Pico does not drive 5-pin DIN MIDI at 31250 baud. The stock DIN jack goes to the LPC2361 via 6N138 optocoupler (unchanged).

                   │

                   │

Tap button GP12: Same RC filter.

8 body-contact circuit bends for the Arturia MicroBrute, optimized for high-impact live performance. Touch brass bolts on the panel to modify sound in real-time via body capacitance and resistance.

Touch Mod Table

# Name PCB Point Safety R Effect Intensity Risk Utility
1 Pitch Shimmer R309 area (near blue trimmers, rear board) 10k Analog pitch vibrato/detune via body capacitance 4/5 1/5 5/5
2 Metalizer Crunch C111 (wavefolder stage 3) 4.7k Sweeps harmonic folding intensity 5/5 2/5 5/5
3 Filter Wah Filter CV input area (Steiner-Parker cutoff) 22k Manual filter sweep, overrides LFO 4/5 2/5 5/5
4 Brute Distortion Feedback path (Brute Factor circuit) 15k Variable feedback: clean to aggressive self-oscillation 5/5 3/5 5/5
5 Envelope Decay ADSR decay timing cap area 33k Pluck-to-swell morphing, changes decay time 3/5 1/5 4/5
6 Dual Harmonic Morph C107 + C106 (wavefolder stages 1 & 2, two bolts) 10k each Cross-coupled folding stages, touch both for complex harmonics 5/5 2/5 5/5
7 LFO Speed Throb LFO timing resistor network 47k Manual tremolo/vibrato speed control 3/5 1/5 4/5
8 Metalizer Feedback Gate Metalizer output to input (series connection) 1k Touch closes feedback loop: harsh harmonic chaos 5/5 4/5 5/5

Recommended top 6 for panel: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 (all rated 5/5 utility)

Wiring Diagram

Each touch bolt:

MicroBrute PCB point ──[safety R]──┬── Brass bolt (panel mount)
                                    │
                            (body contact)
                                    │
                                   GND (via skin resistance ~10k-1M)

For dual-point bends (mod 6), two separate bolts wire to different circuit points. Touching both simultaneously creates cross-coupling through your body.

For feedback gate (mod 8), the circuit is:

Metalizer output ──[1k]── Brass bolt A
                            │
                     (touch to close)
                            │
Metalizer input  ──[1k]── Brass bolt B

Test Protocol

  1. Build the touch test board (schematics/touch_test_board.svg)
  2. Wire each channel to the MicroBrute via clip leads (non-destructive)
  3. Probe dry-fingered at 50% touch pressure — document effect onset
  4. Increase to full pressure for dynamic range
  5. Repeat with slightly damp finger to map moisture sensitivity
  6. Record 10-second audio clip per mod (baseline + touch effect)
  7. Rate musical usefulness vs stability/predictability
  8. Select top 6 for permanent panel installation

Safety Notes

  • All points connect to signal-level circuits (max +/-12V), not power rails or CPU
  • Higher risk mods (4, 6, 8) involve feedback coupling -- test thoroughly

with dry fingers before wet-touch experiments

  • Moisture increases body conductivity: effects become stronger and less

predictable with damp fingers

  • Optional: add 100pF cap in parallel with safety R to limit HF transients
  • B1M pot in series allows variable touch sensitivity (use during testing)

Panel Installation

After testing, select 6 mods for permanent panel bolts:

  • Drill 6x 6mm holes in bottom-left panel area (below mod wheel)
  • Insert brass M3 bolts from outside, nut on inside
  • Solder wire from bolt to safety resistor to PCB point
  • Label each bolt on panel (PITCH, CRUNCH, WAH, DISTORT, HARMONIC, GATE)
  • Spacing: 18-20mm horizontal between bolts to avoid accidental multi-touch

▶ Reader Roadmap docs/MACROBRUTE_README.md

A 1900 KB manual is a lot of doc. Here's how to triage it depending on where you're standing right now.

What this project is

The MACROBRUTE turns a stock Arturia MicroBrute into a deeply modified, expander-paired hybrid synth:

  • Inside the MicroBrute: a small buffer-only breakout board that taps the

existing test points and adds jacks and touch bends. It is powered only from the synth (TP70/TP71/TP72). The Pico is not inside the MicroBrute. Optionally, a custom firmware on the stock LPC2361 to add a sequencer + arpeggiator over the existing engine.

  • Outside the MicroBrute: a Eurorack expander module (17 HP or about 20 HP,

width open) that hosts the Raspberry Pi Pico, display and controls, and pairs to the synth over 2× DB-9 on the MicroBrute rear panel (left of Pitch/Gate), exposing waveform outs, CV ins and utilities: slew limiter, LFO, S&H, firmware clock dividers and aux outs. Noise, mult and attenuverter stay out.

The endgame is two boxes that talk to each other — the synth keeps working stock if the expander is unplugged.

Reading paths

→ If you have never seen this project (10 min)

Read in this order — these are the only docs you need to get the shape:

  1. This page — you're here.
  2. MACROBRUTE_INDEX.md (Section 1) — the master index, project

status, and "key decisions" table.

  1. MACROBRUTE_MOD_SELECTION.md (Section 2) — the 14 curated mods +

6 touch bolts, with rationale.

  1. MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md (Section 2) — 7-phase roadmap from

bench validation to firmware load. Skim the phase headers, ignore the detail.

  1. Skim a couple of schematic SVGs to get a feel for the visual style:

Interconnect Wiring (Section 4) and System Architecture (Section 3).

That's it for the orientation pass. Don't try to read top-to-bottom.

→ If your MicroBrute is on the bench and you want to start (today)

Skip the planning docs and do Phase 0 bench validation first. It's non-destructive, takes a weekend, and uses ~$30 of parts.

  1. Section 2 → Phase 0 starter BOM — the minimal kit (Pico, one

OLED, KY-040 encoder, breadboard, jumpers, RGB LED, a handful of resistors and 3.5 mm jacks). Check the Have column first; order only what is missing.

  1. Section 1 → "Phase 0 Bench Validation" section of the build plan —

the wiring + flash + test procedure.

  1. Section 4 → Phase 0 Breadboard Layout SVG — what the wired-up

breadboard should look like, with every jumper colour-coded.

  1. firmware/pico/ — copy main.py, config.py, and the peripheral

modules onto the Pico. Then run test_hw.py for per-peripheral diagnostics (OLED draws a frame, encoder reports clicks, RGB LED cycles, etc.).

If Phase 0 works on the bench, you're ready for Phase 1 (the breakout board build). If anything is flaky on the bench, fix it there — it will be 10× harder to fix once it's inside the MicroBrute.

→ If you're picking this up mid-build

Find the most recent phase you finished, then:

  • MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md — re-read just that phase + the next one.
  • MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md (Section 3) — the canonical wiring

reference. Cross-check anything you wired against this.

  • MACROBRUTE_TROUBLESHOOTING.md (Section 9) — common pitfalls

organised by phase.

  • Section 5 → Breakout Board — re-check stripboard layout + track

cuts before you power up.

If you've been away for >2 weeks: also re-read the Key Decisions table in MACROBRUTE_INDEX.md — pin assignments and connector choices have been deliberately frozen, but it's worth double-checking nothing in your notes contradicts the canonical map.

Skill prerequisites

You'll be comfortable if you have:

  • Through-hole soldering at 1.5 mm pad pitch (DIP-8 / DIP-14 ICs).
  • Basic multimeter use — continuity, DC voltage, resistance.
  • Breadboarding — comfortable wiring jumpers from a schematic.

Helpful but not required:

  • Reading schematics (the manual has both schematic and breadboard views

side-by-side for the touchier circuits).

  • Python + MicroPython basics (Pico firmware is hackable but works as-is).
  • ARM-bare-metal C (only if you want to touch the LPC2361 firmware

itself — most builders never will).

If you've never soldered DIP packages: do the touch-test board first (schematics/touch_test_board.svg). It's 10 cm × 5 cm, ~30 minutes of soldering, and gives you a working circuit-bend rig at the end.

Time + cost expectations

Phase Calendar Active hours Out-of-pocket
Phase 0 — bench validation 1 week 4–8 h ~$30 starter BOM
Phase 1 — breakout board 2 weeks 12–20 h ~$60 (board parts + ICs)
Phase 2 — internal wiring 2 weeks 8–14 h ~$15 (wire + connectors)
Phase 3 — panel mods (irreversible) 2 weeks 10–18 h ~$40 (jacks + toggles + bolts)
Phase 4 — expander build 4 weeks (parallel) 20–35 h ~$80 (panel + parts)
Phase 5 — system integration 2 weeks 6–12 h ~$10 (DB-9 cable)
Phase 6 — custom LPC firmware (optional) open-ended 10+ h $0

Total: ~$250 of parts spread over ~12 weeks of evenings/weekends. The project is deliberately incremental — it works at every phase boundary, so you can stop at any point and still have a usable instrument.

What's locked vs. still in flux

Locked (don't propose changes here without strong reason):

  • 2× DB-9 connector as the MB ↔ expander interface (confirmed by the owner; HD-15 was rejected;

see Key Decisions in the Master Index for why).

  • Pico GPIO assignments — firmware/pico/config.py is canonical; see

schematics/pico_pinout.md and the connection map. 3 pins are free (GP26-28); GP2 and GP3 are the SPI main OLED, GP11 the gate input.

  • Power scheme — split: the expander runs from the rack only, the

breakout from the synth only; only ground is shared over the DB-9. No supply rail and no I²C cross the cable.

Still in flux (your input welcome):

  • Expander size — 17 HP or about 20 HP, open until the owner measures

the blank.

  • The main OLED chip marking and pin order (1.3" 7-pin SPI baseline, SSD1306 or SH1106)

and the DB-9 count are for the owner to confirm (BF Q22, Q9). The board is a Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350).

  • LPC bridge UART (UART1 is the working assumption, UNVERIFIED until the

Phase 0 continuity check).

  • Resonance vactrol — owned, but the part number and LED rating are unread.
  • Whether the 9th touch bolt (envelope retrigger, M11) makes the cut.
  • Final mix of 6 panel touch bolts from the 8 documented bends.
  • Whether the optional LPC2361 custom firmware ships with v1.

When in doubt, treat anything in the Master Index → "Key Decisions" table as locked, and anything labelled TBD or maybe elsewhere in the manual as open.

Where to find things at a glance

The sidebar groups sections into three clusters:

  • PLAN (0–3) — what you're building, why, and in what order. Read

these first.

  • BUILD (4–8) — every wiring diagram, stripboard, and panel cut.

Reference during construction.

  • REFERENCE (9–12) — IC pinouts, test points, glossary,

troubleshooting, mod catalog, research notes, legacy archive.

If a doc isn't in any of those: it's an internal .md not surfaced in the rendered manual. Browse docs/ directly.

Key Decisions (authoritative)

Decision Choice
Connector 2× DB-9 (18 pins total) on the MB rear panel, left of Pitch/Gate — CONFIRMED by the owner; VGA HD-15 rejected. DB-9 B = UART TX/RX, Filter CV, VCA CV, grounds; no supply, no I²C
OLED 1.3" 7-pin SPI (chip SSD1306 or SH1106 and pin order UNVERIFIED: read the module) on SPI0: SCK GP2, MOSI GP3, DC GP4, RES GP5, CS tied to GND (PROVISIONAL, BT-14) — main display on the expander panel (owner ruling, 2026-10-17; larger than the 0.96" cutout, bears on the open width). The 0.91" strip OLED is dropped; the 1.3" 4-pin I²C module is in a TD-3, not available. Alternatives only (I²C needs re-pinning): 0.96" SSD1306 (owner to confirm), 16×2 1602 I²C LCD.
MIDI path Pico ↔ LPC2361 UART bridge over Pico UART0 (GP0/GP1) @ 115200 baud, DB-9 B pins 1 and 6; LPC UART1 (P0.15/P0.16, pins 62/63) UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity check. No direct 31250-baud MIDI from Pico.
Analog utilities Slew limiter, LFO, Sample & Hold (LF398, not owned) on the expander; CD4066 and CD4024 are dropped (S&H uses the LF398; the owned CD4051 has no role in the decided design)
EFFIGY pair Shelved
RGB LED (common cathode) GP8=R/clock, GP9=G/gate, GP10=B/mode. Replaces 3 discrete LEDs.
CD4049UBE Expander clock IN/OUT buffers on Pico 3V3 (not on the gate path; the gate uses a 22k/33k divider, BF 3.5)
Touch mods 6 body-contact bends (PITCH, CRUNCH, WAH, DISTORT, HARM, GATE), selected from 8 tested
Panel jacks 3 (VCF insert, Metalizer insert, VCA CV in)
Panel toggles 3 (Envelope bypass, Metalizer boost, VCA drone)
Expander size OPEN: 17 HP or about 20 HP (repo panel file 87 × 128.5 mm, UNVERIFIED)
JF-33 delay Moved to spinoffs/jf33-eurorack/ — not part of canonical MACROBRUTE
DSO138 oscilloscope Moved to spinoffs/dso138-desktop/ — desktop scope, not a module
Power Split: expander from the rack only, breakout from the synth only; signal ground only via DB-9

2. Architecture
▶ Complete Connection Map docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md

Every signal, mod, bend, and wire in the system. This is the master wiring reference for building, debugging, and expanding.

Design sources (2026-10-17): owner decisions in docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md section 1a, datasheet facts in docs/DATASHEETS.md, and the back-feed and hum design note docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-backfeed-hum-design.md (cited below as "BF"). Nothing is built yet: every value here is a design value, and anything marked UNVERIFIED waits for a bench check or an owner answer.

Connector: 2× DB-9, CONFIRMED by the owner (2026-10-17; the VGA HD-15 line in a pasted inventory was an error; HD-15 rejected — shorts pins 6-8 to GND). Both mount on the MicroBrute rear panel, left of Pitch/Gate (owner decision a). Panel dimensions, free area and depth: UNVERIFIED until the owner measures (audit E-20, E-21). DB-9 mounting-hole spacing 24.99 mm (Spectrum Control cut-out, DATASHEETS (g)); flange size of the owner's part UNVERIFIED. Power: split. The expander is powered only from the Eurorack rack; the MicroBrute-side breakout is powered only from the synth (TP70/TP71/TP72). No supply rail crosses either DB-9 cable; only ground is shared. OLED: one 1.3" 7-pin SPI 128×64 main display on the expander (owner ruling, 2026-10-17), write-only on Pico SPI0: SCK GP2, MOSI GP3, DC GP4, RES GP5 (section 1); the module's CS pin is tied to GND, no GPIO (PROVISIONAL, BT-14; section 12G). Chip UNVERIFIED (SSD1306 or SH1106: owner to read the module, BF Q22). Module pin order UNVERIFIED (common order GND, VCC, D0 = SCK, D1 = MOSI, RES, DC, CS: read the silkscreen). Powered from the Pico 3V3 pin, 3V3 logic; current draw UNVERIFIED. Driver: firmware/pico/display.py (OLED_SPI, SPI0 at 8 MHz); for SH1106 set OLED_CHIP="SH1106", OLED_COL_OFFSET=2. A 1.3" module is larger than the 0.96" panel cutout, which bears on the open expander width (17 vs about 20 HP stays OPEN). The owner's 4-pin I²C 1.3" module is wired into a TD-3 and is not available. Alternatives only: the 0.96" SSD1306 (may not have arrived, owner to confirm) or another I²C module; an I²C display would need GP4/GP5, which are DC/RES here, so it requires re-pinning and is not a drop-in. The 0.91" strip OLED is dropped (decision c). No I²C is used on the expander, and none crosses the DB-9 cable. MIDI path: Pico UART0 ↔ LPC2361 UART bridge @ 115200 baud (LPC side: see section 5.4). LPC firmware relays as internal MIDI SysEx. No direct 31250-baud MIDI from Pico. Firmware: Pico MicroPython (14 modules + _effigy_constants.py generated from EFFIGY's C header; the EFFIGY pairing is SHELVED, section 5.6), LPC2361 ARM7 (stock + planned bridge extension). Board: Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350).

1. Pico GPIO Allocation

Canonical source: firmware/pico/config.py. Update this table AND that file together.

GPIO Pico Pin Function Direction Notes
GP0 1 UART0 TX → LPC2361 OUT 115200 baud, DB-9 B:1, 1kΩ series on the expander board (BF 3.1). Design rule: GP0 stays an input until GP1 reads high (firmware rule, not yet implemented)
GP1 2 UART0 RX ← LPC2361 IN 115200 baud, DB-9 B:6, 1kΩ series on the expander board. Fault-tolerant pin (BF 3.1)
GP2 4 OLED SCK (SPI0 SCK) OUT Main OLED D0, on the expander only (short on-board run). Module pin order UNVERIFIED
GP3 5 OLED MOSI (SPI0 TX) OUT Main OLED D1. Write-only display: no MISO, no pull-ups
GP4 6 OLED DC OUT Main OLED data/command select
GP5 7 OLED RES OUT Main OLED reset (active low)
GP6 9 Aux output 3 OUT Programmable: tap-div / euclidean / random / passthrough / PWM-CV
GP7 10 Aux output 4 OUT Programmable, same modes as GP6
GP8 11 RGB LED R · Clock tick OUT PWM, owned exclusively by leds.LEDManager
GP9 12 RGB LED G · Gate active OUT PWM
GP10 14 RGB LED B · Mode OUT PWM (1 kHz), slice 5A
GP11 15 Gate input (Pico mirror of DB-9 A:1) IN GATE_IN. From the MicroBrute CD40106 stage output through the 22k / 33k divider (BF 3.5). Fault-tolerant pin. PROVISIONAL (BT-14): the OLED CS pin is tied to GND so GP11 can take this input; see section 12G for the fallback
GP12 16 Tap button IN Pull-up; short = tap tempo, long-hold = manual gate
GP13 17 Encoder switch IN Pull-up, short = select, long = back
GP14 19 Encoder CLK (A) IN Pull-up, IRQ on both edges
GP15 20 Encoder DT (B) IN Pull-up
GP16 21 Clock divider out 1 OUT Firmware-driven, default ÷2 (configurable)
GP17 22 Clock divider out 2 OUT Default ÷4
GP18 24 Clock divider out 3 OUT Default ÷8
GP19 25 Aux output 1 OUT Programmable (PWM-capable)
GP20 26 Aux output 2 OUT Programmable
GP21 27 Clock input IN Pull-down, external sync IRQ; fed through the CD4049UB buffer (section 4)
GP22 29 Clock output OUT Master clock (plain GPIO from a Timer) through the CD4049UB buffer to the expander CLK OUT jack (section 4)
GP26 31 ADC0 (free) IN Not fault tolerant, diode to IOVDD (Pico datasheet p20). PWM slice 5A shared with GP10 (section 12C)
GP27 32 ADC1 (free) IN Not fault tolerant
GP28 34 ADC2 (free) IN Not fault tolerant
3V3 36 3V3 out PWR Main OLED (draw UNVERIFIED) + encoder
VSYS 39 +5V input PWR From rack CP1A +5V via a Schottky OR diode + bulk + 100nF (section 10)
GND 3,8,13,18,23,28,33,38 Ground — To the expander star point (rack 0 V at the 16-pin header), not to TP72 (BF 4.1)

Free pins: 3 — GP26, GP27, GP28 (ADC-capable, not fault tolerant). GP2 and GP3 (SPI main OLED) and GP11 (gate input) are not free (owner rulings, 2026-10-17). The I²C0 bus speed question (400 kHz in code against 100 kHz in older docs, audit S05) is moot: the display is SPI. Allocated in config.py: GP0, GP1, GP2, GP3, GP4, GP5, GP6, GP7, GP8, GP9, GP10, GP11, GP12, GP13, GP14, GP15, GP16, GP17, GP18, GP19, GP20, GP21, GP22. GP23, GP24, GP25 and GP29 are RP2040-internal and not exposed on the Pico header. Rule (BF 5): any input that can see a cable or jack signal while the Pico may be unpowered goes on a fault-tolerant pin (GP0-GP22), not on GP26-GP28.

Tap button modes: short press (< 400 ms release) → tap tempo. Held press (≥ 400 ms) → manual gate (RGB-G LED full-bright while held; gate signal also goes to LPC bridge as a synthetic note-on/off pair).

RGB LED color semantics:

Channel Pin Meaning
Red GP8 Brief flash on each clock tick
Green GP9 Solid while gate is high (manual or external)
Blue GP10 Mode indicator (the old "paired with EFFIGY" meaning is shelved)

Mixed colors arise naturally — yellow = clock + gate, cyan = gate + mode, magenta = clock + mode, white = all three.

USB-MIDI: Pico micro-USB enumerates as a USB-MIDI class device via TinyUSB (firmware/pico/usbmidi.py). Orthogonal to the LPC bridge — gives the host DAW a "Macrobrute Pico" MIDI port. Pico does NOT drive 5-pin DIN MIDI; that stays on the stock 6N138 → LPC2361 MIDI UART path inside the MicroBrute (UART3 per the firmware disassembly, audit S06; the 6N138-to-pin-85 route is UNVERIFIED, audit E-02). USB ground rule (BF 4.3): no USB cable on the Pico while the expander is rack-powered and the DB-9 cables are connected; flash and debug with the DB-9 cables unplugged. Runtime USB-MIDI with the cables connected needs a USB isolator, which is not owned (BF Q17).

2. DB-9 A — Outputs (MicroBrute → Expander)

From BF section 2.3. A has 8 signals and 1 ground, so no pin can be interleaved; the order is kept. Connector face (insert numbering; neighbour geometry UNVERIFIED until BF BT-7):

   top row     [1 GATE]-[2 PITCH]-[3 ENV]-[4 LFO]-[5 MIX]
   bottom row        [6 VCF]-[7 SAW]-[8 SQUARE]-[9 GND]
Pin Signal MB Source Buffer Series R (MB board) Protection / Notes Wire Color
1 Gate Out TP83 2× CD40106 in series (keeps TP83 polarity) 1kΩ at the CD40106 output Expander: 22k / 33k divider into Pico GP11 (fault tolerant; PROVISIONAL (BT-14), 12G); gate jack tapped before the divider. Provisional (BF 3.4, 3.5) White
2 Pitch CV Out Rear panel jack Stock pitch buffer 220Ω (new; was "direct") Low-impedance source UNVERIFIED (E-16) Yellow
3 Envelope Out Mod matrix / TP5 TL07x follower 1kΩ after the feedback tap Source choice UNVERIFIED (audit N23) Orange
4 LFO Out Mod matrix TL07x follower 1kΩ after the feedback tap Source TP21 meaning UNVERIFIED (E-17) Green
5 VCO Mix Out TP30_MIXER_OUT TL074 follower 1kΩ in, 1kΩ out — Blue
6 VCF Out TP19 TL074 follower 1kΩ in, 1kΩ out — Purple
7 Saw Out TP94 TL074 follower 1kΩ in, 1kΩ out Peak level UNVERIFIED (E-19) Red
8 Square Out TP93 TL074 follower 1kΩ in, 1kΩ out Peak level UNVERIFIED (E-19) Brown
9 GND TP72 — — TP72 star and expander star Black

Expander side of A: lines 2-8 go to panel jacks with no expander IC on them. If any A line is later normalled into an expander circuit (slew, S&H), it enters through at least 100kΩ (BF 3.6). The r5 re-order of A stays an owner option, decided by the BT-9 crosstalk check (BF Q14).

Gate level note (Provisional, BF 3.5): the CD40106 gate output (5V) reaches the Pico only through the 22k / 33k divider on the expander (about 2.95 V high at a 5.0 V CD40106 supply). No 5 V net touches a Pico GPIO. The CD4049UBE is not used on the gate path, because its datasheet says its inputs clamp to VCC (TI SCHS046L p17).

3. DB-9 B — Digital + Essential CV (Expander ↔ MicroBrute)

From BF section 2.2. DB-9 B carries UART TX, UART RX, Filter CV, VCA CV and grounds only. No supply rail and no I²C on this cable. Rule applied: the UART pair at one end, each CV pin surrounded only by ground pins, no CV pin next to a digital pin.

Connector face (insert numbering; neighbour geometry UNVERIFIED until BF BT-7):

   top row     [1 UART TX]-[2 GND]-[3 VCA CV]-[4 GND]-[5 FILTER CV]
   bottom row        [6 UART RX]-[7 GND]-[8 GND]-[9 GND]
Pin Signal Direction Series R Protection / Notes Wire Color
1 UART TX (Pico GP0 → LPC RXD1, section 5.4) Expander → MB 1kΩ at the Pico (expander board) + 1kΩ at the LPC (MB board) GP0 high-impedance until GP1 reads high (BF 3.1). LPC UART choice UNVERIFIED (audit B01) White
2 GND — — Guard; TP72 star and expander star Black
3 VCA CV In (to TP10) Expander → MB 10kΩ at the expander output + 100kΩ on the MB board BAT85 to +12V_BRK and from -12V_BRK at the node after the 100kΩ; 1 nF to GND Purple
4 GND — — Guard Black
5 Filter CV In (to TP26) Expander → MB 10kΩ at the expander output + 100kΩ on the MB board As pin 3 Blue
6 UART RX (LPC TXD1 → Pico GP1, section 5.4) MB → Expander 1kΩ at the LPC (MB board) + 1kΩ at the Pico (expander board) GP1 is a fault-tolerant RP2040 pin (BF 3.1) Yellow
7 GND — — Guard Black
8 GND — — Guard Black
9 GND — — Star return Black

Freed pins: against the old map (1 TX, 2 RX, 3 SDA, 4 SCL, 5 Filter, 6 VCA, 7 +12 V, 8 -12 V, 9 GND), the two I²C pins and the two rail pins are freed and all carry ground (BF 2.2). Series resistors sit on the board side of each connector (solder cup or first board pad), never in the cable. Whether the synth's own 220kΩ / 100kΩ sit after TP26 / TP10 is UNVERIFIED (E-18); the extra 100kΩ may reduce CV depth (BF 3.3, bench check BT-4; fallback 47kΩ).

Migrated to MB panel (no longer in DB-9 B):

Original DB-9 signal Where it goes now
Resonance CV In New 3.5 mm jack on MB panel — wires internally to a TL072 voltage-to-current stage → vactrol LED on breakout (audit S37; sense resistor depends on the owned vactrol's LED rating, UNVERIFIED, BF Q2)
Sync In Use existing MB back-panel Sync In jack — no new drilling
Gate In Use existing MB back-panel Gate In jack — no new drilling
Ext Audio In Use existing MB back-panel Audio In jack — no new drilling

Cable spec: two shielded 9-conductor cables (not ribbon), one per connector. Maximum length: 1 m working figure, UNVERIFIED until BF BT-6 (cable capacitance) and BT-1 (UART edges). Braid bonded at the MicroBrute end only (section 11). A molded off-the-shelf cable bonds the braid at both hoods and must be modified or built (BF 4.2).

Crosstalk mitigation: (1) shielded cables, braid at the MB end only; (2) each CV pin on B has only ground neighbours; (3) the series resistors in the table below; (4) both cables bundled and short. Pin-number order alone does not separate lines: on a D-sub, pin 6 sits between 1 and 2, 7 between 2 and 3, 8 between 3 and 4, 9 between 4 and 5 (audit S42, BF 2.1).

5.4 LPC Bridge Wiring (replaces direct MIDI)

The bridge is the only description of the LPC side of the UART in this document; other sections refer here.

Pico speaks a custom framed protocol over its UART0 at 115200 baud to the LPC2361's UART1: P0.15 / TXD1 (LQFP pin 62) and P0.16 / RXD1 (LQFP pin 63) (LPC2361 data sheet Rev. 03, Table 3, p6). UNVERIFIED pending the Phase 0 continuity check (audit section 4 item 7): the stock firmware uses SSP0/SPI, which shares these pins, so they may be wired to something on the board. Do not write "confirmed" until that check passes. Fallback only if those pins are taken: the ISP UART (UART0, LQFP pins 98/99), with the ISP conflict handled. Pins 96 and 97, given in older drawings, are VDD(3V3) and VSS (data sheet p12): never probe or wire there.

The lines cross DB-9 B pins 1 and 6 (section 3), with the Pico on the expander, not inside the MicroBrute case. The LPC firmware (modified via .mbf re-encryption) translates protocol messages into internal MIDI SysEx, avoiding the 31250-baud MIDI path entirely. The UART wires are installed in Phase 3 but unused until the Phase 6 bridge firmware (audit N17).

From To Notes
Pico GP0 (UART0 TX) 1kΩ → DB-9 B:1 → 1kΩ → LPC2361 P0.16 / RXD1 (pin 63) No divider, no level shifter (both 3.3 V)
LPC2361 P0.15 / TXD1 (pin 62) 1kΩ → DB-9 B:6 → 1kΩ → Pico GP1 (UART0 RX) GP1 fault tolerant
Shared GND DB-9 B:2, B:4, B:7, B:8, B:9 TP72 star (MB) and expander star

Protocol frame: 0xAA · msg_type · counter · payload_len · payload[…] · xor_checksum

The XOR checksum is the bitwise XOR of all bytes from msg_type through the last payload byte (excluding the leading 0xAA and the checksum itself). Receivers compute and verify; bad frames are silently dropped. Both sides (firmware/pico/midi.py and firmware/lpc2361/include/pico_comm.h) implement identical framing.

The protocol document docs/MACROBRUTE_EFFIGY_BRIDGE.md and firmware/pico/effigy_bridge.py are archived as they are.

10. Expander (Eurorack — width OPEN: 17 HP or about 20 HP)

The expander hosts the Pico, the user interface (main OLED + encoder + tap button + RGB LED), the I/O between MicroBrute and the rack, and three analog utilities: slew limiter, LFO and Sample & Hold. The LFO and the S&H are standalone rack utilities: no synth cabling, rack power only (decided 2026-10-16). Noise, mult and attenuverter stay out.

Width: OPEN until the owner measures the blank (decision e). 17 HP (the repo panel file is 87 mm, with mounting holes 79 mm apart, both UNVERIFIED against the A-100 spec; audit S53, E-22) or about 20 HP (101.3 mm; audit S54). Plan both layouts. Depth behind the panel UNVERIFIED (E-23).

Power (rack only): Behringer CP1A 16-pin bus: -12 V @ 1 A on pins 1-2 (red stripe), GND on pins 3-8, +12 V @ 1 A on pins 9-10, +5 V @ 0.5 A on pins 11-12, pins 13-16 not used (CP1A QSG p15, p20; DATASHEETS (f)). The +5 V budget is 0.5 A shared with every other +5 V module in the rack. Whether the owner's bus slot carries +5 V: UNVERIFIED (BF BT-12). Pico VSYS takes rack +5 V through a Schottky OR diode (valid per Pico datasheet p21-p22): 1N5817 is a 20 V / 1 A part and is not owned; an owned 1N5819 (40 V, x10, UNVERIFIED part) or an owned BAT85 can stand in (BAT85: about 4.2 V at 100 mA, inside VSYS 1.8-5.5 V; BF 1.2). Provisional; using 1N5819 here would free a BAT85.

11. Ground Strategy

Single rule (BF 4.1): exactly one ground connection between the synth and the rack — the cable ground conductors (A:9; B:2, B:4, B:7, B:8, B:9), all running between the same two star points.

  • MicroBrute star: TP72. Every cable ground pin and the breakout ground go to TP72 by their own

short wires, not through the breakout's ground strip (audit N13). The breakout takes power only from TP70 / TP71 / TP72.

  • Expander star: where rack 0 V enters at the 16-pin header. Every cable ground pin, the Pico

GND and all expander circuit grounds meet there.

  • No other synth-to-rack path: no separate clock cable (section 4), no chassis or panel bond

between the two cases, no USB on the Pico while the cables are connected (section 1, BF 4.3).

  • Shield (BF 4.2): each cable's braid is bonded to its connector shell at the MicroBrute end

only, and that MB-side panel shell is wired with a short lead to TP72. At the expander end the braid is cut back and insulated inside the hood, and the expander panel connector's shell is isolated from the aluminium panel with insulating shoulder washers. The shield never carries signal return. Shell-to-panel continuity: UNVERIFIED (E-15, BT-8).

  • Both cables are bundled and kept short so the small loops between the ground conductors stay

small. Adapter earth status (class II or not) is UNVERIFIED (audit N06).

  • No capacitor in series with any ground pin. The old "100 nF in series with DB-9 GND" fix

removes the DC ground reference for CV, gate and UART (audit S23) and is withdrawn.

Fallback ladder (owned parts only, in order of cost; BF 4.5). Do each step only if hum or noise is still measured after the previous one (BT-9):

  1. No parts: confirm the baseline. USB unplugged; no clock cable; cables bundled and short; both adapters on the same mains strip; measure with each cable unplugged in turn to locate the loop.
  2. No parts: re-wire any ground that does not go to its star by its own lead; confirm no case-to-case contact.
  3. No parts: swap the shield bond to the expander end and compare; keep whichever measures lower (the swapped expander shell gets a short lead to the expander star; compare the MB shell lead to TP72 in place and removed).
  4. Owned resistor kit plus two BAT85 (conditional): on the expander, break the ground bundle from the expander star with 10Ω, bypassed by 100 nF in parallel and two anti-parallel BAT85. Keeps the DC reference. All 10 owned BAT85 are allocated, so this step needs two freed (audit C12, BF Q3). Recheck BT-2, BT-3, BT-5 afterwards.
  5. Owned TL072 and resistors: dedicate one B ground pin (for example B:8) as a no-current ground-sense wire from TP72 and use it as the reference of difference-amplifier receivers on the expander's audio inputs. Needs matched resistors (1 % parts not owned, BF Q5).
  6. Owned isolation transformer (46.9/82.4Ω windings) on the single worst audio line only, after its characterisation (E-29). It passes no DC, so never on CV, gate or UART.

PWM slice note (audit S02): RP2040 PWM slice = (GP >> 1) & 7, channel = GP & 1. GP26 is slice 5 channel A, the same channel as GP10 (LED_MODE, 1 kHz): GP26 cannot be used as a PWM DAC while GP10 drives the mode LED. GP27 is slice 5 channel B and would be tied to GP10's 1 kHz slice frequency. GP28 is slice 6 channel A, the same channel as GP12 (channel = GP & 1, slice = (GP >> 1) & 7), so the two share one duty value if both are ever PWM; GP12 is a plain input (tap button), so GP28 is usable as PWM while it stays that way. A pin used as PWM cannot also be read as ADC. A Pico PWM output reaching the MicroBrute would also need a cable pin, and DB-9 B has none free for signals (section 3).

▶ What You're Building docs/MACROBRUTE_VISION.md
Expander Finished Panel
The expander, finished (width open: 17 or about 20 HP). Visualization of the assembled module, labelled by signal type: blue = audio, gold = CV, green = gate/clock, lavender = pot/switch. The faux OLED frame shows the kind of UI the firmware draws (BPM, sequencer state, level meters). For drilling dimensions see panel/expander_17hp.svg.
Microbrute Finished Panel
STALE (to be redrawn, see roadmap batch B): the strip OLED is dropped and the expander width is open (17 or about 20 HP). MicroBrute panel additions in their final positions. Stock controls are ghosted for spatial reference — the old drawing adds a strip OLED (now dropped), 8 new 3.5 mm jacks (4 inserts + 4 Phase-2 mod jacks), 5 SPDT toggles, and 6 brass touch bolts plus a GND return bolt. Color coding matches the expander mockup. For drilling dimensions see panel/microbrute_panel_template.svg.

Two mockups of the finished hardware, so you have a target image in your head before you read another 1900 KB of detail. The expander (17 or about 20 HP, open) (panel) and the modified MicroBrute (additions in their final positions) — rendered as they'd look assembled.

These are visualizations, not drilling templates. For 1:1 mm drilling guides, see panel/expander_17hp.svg and panel/microbrute_panel_template.svg.

The expander module (17 or about 20 HP, open)

The expander is a self-contained Eurorack module that pairs to the modified MicroBrute over a 2× DB-9 cable. It hosts the main 1.3″ 7-pin SPI OLED (chip UNVERIFIED), the rotary encoder, the tap button, the RGB status LED, all clock I/O, the analogue slew limiter, a standalone LFO, a standalone Sample & Hold, the firmware clock dividers and the four firmware-assignable aux outputs. Its width is open (17 HP or about 20 HP) until the blank is measured.

Power comes from the Eurorack bus (the CP1A; it needs ±12 V and +5 V from the rack, since the Pico runs from bus +5 V) — the synth's stock power is untouched, and no supply rail crosses the DB-9 cable; only ground is shared.

The modified MicroBrute panel

The synth keeps every stock control. The mod adds: two DB-9 connectors on the rear panel, left of the Pitch/Gate section (dimensions still to be measured), a row of new 3.5 mm jacks for the panel inserts and the Phase-2 mod additions, five SPDT toggles down the right side, and six brass touch bolts along the front edge for circuit bending. The seventh "GND" bolt provides the always-touched return path. The 0.91″ strip OLED idea is dropped.

If you unplug the breakout, every stock control still works exactly as Arturia shipped — the mods are in addition to, not instead of.

Grounding Strategy

From BF 4.1-4.3 and connection map section 11.

  • Exactly one ground connection between synth and rack: the cable ground conductors (A:9;

B:2, B:4, B:7, B:8, B:9), all running between the same two star points.

  • MicroBrute star: TP72. Every cable ground pin and the breakout ground go to TP72 by their own

short wires, not through the breakout's ground strip.

  • Expander star: where rack 0 V enters at the 16-pin header.
  • Shield: MB end only (above); the shield never carries signal return.
  • No USB on the Pico while the cables are connected (USB ground loop, BF 4.3).
  • Never create ground loops: no chassis or panel bond between the two cases, no clock cable,

no capacitor in series with any ground pin (audit S23).

  • Hum fallback ladder (owned parts only): connection map section 11, BF 4.5.
BUILD
3. Power
▶ Circuit Design Review schematics/CIRCUIT_REVIEW.md
LED Driver Array
Eight-channel LED driver array (2 N3904 saturated switches) for panel indicators. Each channel takes a Pico GPIO and sinks up to 20 mA from the +5 V LED rail.
Full Vactrol Driver
Complete vactrol-based VCA/filter modulator including the 2 N3904 LED driver, vactrol (VTL5C3 or LED+LDR DIY), and the load-side coupling.
CV Input ESD Protection
Panel-jack ESD/static protection — 1 nF cap to ground + BAT54S series for the touch plates, plus ferrite beads on every audio output for RF rejection.
CV Input Protection Circuit
CV input protection topology that scales across all the expander's CV inputs — uses the same BAT54S clamp + 1 kΩ series pattern as the breakout, but with attenuator pots before the clamp for level control.
CD4051 Analog Multiplexer
CD4051 8-channel analog multiplexer wiring: address pins, common Z, eight Y channels, VEE tied to GND for unipolar operation. Used to multiplex touch plates and any spare CV inputs.
Buffered Multiple (1→3)
Buffered 1×3 multiple: TL072 unity-gain followed by three 1 kΩ output isolators. Useful for splitting one CV/clock to multiple destinations without loading the source.
Manual Gate Button
Front-panel manual gate button — momentary SPST, debounced through a CD40106 Schmitt trigger so the gate output is clean even under fast taps.

Systematic review of all circuit designs for correctness, safety, and reliability.

Updated against the project audit (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md) and the back-feed and hum design note (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-backfeed-hum-design.md, "BF"). Nothing is built; a "CORRECT" status below means the reasoning checks out on paper, not a bench result. Sections 6 and 8 cover dropped circuits; sections 11-12 cover the JF-33 spinoff.

1. Breakout PCB — Power Supply

Issue: Diode direction for -12V

Status: CORRECTED (audit B15, S74; the old text here said both "cathode toward the load" and "anode toward load")

  • One rule: on +12 V the diode anode faces TP70 and the cathode the breakout rail; on -12 V the

cathode faces TP71 / the -12 V source and the anode faces the breakout rail (the load).

  • Check: in normal operation current flows from the breakout -12V_BRK rail into TP71, so the diode

conducts anode (rail) to cathode (TP71). A positive voltage on TP71 reverse-biases it and is blocked.

  • Part: owned BAT85 per rail, or a 4.7-10 Ω series resistor instead: OPEN (owner), audit conflict

C12; an owned 1N5819 (40 V) per rail is a third option. The 1N5817 is not owned and is a 20 V part (docs/DATASHEETS.md (e)); the owned 1N5819 serves wherever a 1N5817 was drawn.

Issue: Pico power from +5V rail

Status: REMOVED (audit S12, B09)

  • The Pico is on the expander and takes rack +5 V through a Schottky OR diode into VSYS

(connection map section 10). Nothing on the breakout takes 5 V from the synth; no synth 5 V or 3V3 is tapped.

  • The breakout's only 5 V is a local 78L05 from +12V_BRK for the CD40106 gate stage (Provisional,

BF 3.4).

Issue: Ferrite bead values

Status: REMOVED

  • Ferrite beads are not owned and are omitted (BF 1.5). Bulk is 2-4 owned 10 µF / 63 V per rail

(BF 1.4); where extra filtering is wanted, 10 Ω + 10 µF.

2. Output Buffers (TL074)

Issue: Input bias path

Status: CORRECTED (audit N11)

  • TL074 non-inverting followers need a DC bias path on the input.
  • MicroBrute test points are DC-coupled; the bias resistor only defines the input when a tap lead

is disconnected.

  • Decision: 1MΩ to GND (replaces 10MΩ: an open input floats less and picks up less mains hum).

Issue: TL074 output current

Status: CORRECT, cable figure corrected

  • Output into the cable through a 1kΩ isolation resistor placed after the feedback tap (stable

arrangement, audit R3-15 / N09). Maximum peak output ±12 V min into 10 kΩ at ±15 V supplies (TI SLOS080W p15).

  • Cable capacitance is UNVERIFIED (the old "~20pF/m" is low; 50-100 pF/m is more usual, audit

R3-14). Working cable length 1 m, UNVERIFIED until BF BT-6 measures the cable.

Issue: TL074 slew rate vs audio bandwidth

Status: CORRECT

  • TL07xC slew rate: 8 V/µs min, 20 V/µs typ (TI SLOS080W p16; the old "13 V/µs" was not from this sheet)
  • For 10Vpp at 20kHz: required slew = 2π × 20000 × 5 = 0.63V/µs
  • 8 V/µs >> 0.63 V/µs — no slew limiting in the audio band

Issue: Input common-mode range

Status: OPEN (audit N10)

  • Linear input range is about 4 V inside each rail (SLOS080W p11, p15), about ±8 V here. Saw and

square peaks are UNVERIFIED (E-19): scope TP94 / TP93 / TP30 / TP19 and add a 2:1 divider if peaks exceed about ±8 V.

3. Gate Buffer (CD40106)

Issue: Input can never read low

Status: CORRECTED (audit B14, Provisional per BF 3.4)

  • The old stage put a 10kΩ pull-up to +5V on pin 1 with TP83 (100kΩ source) through 10kΩ. With

TP83 low the pin sat at 5 V × 110k / 120k = 4.58 V, above VT+, so the input read high in both states.

  • New stage: TP83 → 10kΩ → pin 1, 1nF to GND at the pin, no pull-up; pin 2 → pin 3 (second

inverter, so A:1 follows TP83 polarity, audit S33); pin 4 → 1kΩ → DB-9 A:1; unused inputs 5, 9, 11, 13 to GND (audit S34). VDD = +5V_LOC from a local 78L05.

Issue: Input voltage range and threshold

Status: OPEN (E-09)

  • CD40106 input abs max -0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V, ±10 mA (TI SCHS097F p4).
  • VT+ at VDD 5 V: 2.2 / 2.9 / 3.6 V min / typ / max (p5-p6). TP83 must exceed 3.6 V high for a

guaranteed trigger. TP83's level is UNVERIFIED; scope it first (BF BT-5). If it is 3.3 V logic the stage must be redesigned: OPEN (owner), BF Q15 (no synth 3V3 tap, audit B09).

  • The old "10kΩ+10kΩ divider" suggestion is withdrawn: halving the input would make triggering

less certain, not more.

Issue: Output level and the Pico

Status: CORRECTED (BF 3.5, Provisional)

  • 0 / 5 V gate through 1kΩ. On the expander the gate jack is tapped before a 22kΩ / 33kΩ divider

that feeds a fault-tolerant Pico GPIO at about 2.95 V high. No 5 V net reaches a GPIO. The CD4049UBE is not used on the gate path (its inputs clamp to VCC, TI SCHS046L p17).

4. Vactrol Driver

Issue: Transistor driver works as a switch

Status: WRONG — withdrawn, replacement TO DESIGN (audit S37, R3-12)

  • The old circuit (TL072 → 1kΩ → 2N3904 base, LED in the collector) had no collector supply as

drawn. With LED + R from +12 V to the collector, the LED current is fixed at about (12 - 2 - 0.2) / 1k ≈ 9 mA once the base passes about 0.8 V: on/off, not a continuous resonance control. The base had no protection against negative TL072 swings.

  • The earlier "Final value: 1kΩ confirmed" and "base current 4.3 mA, saturated: CORRECT" entries

are withdrawn.

  • Replacement: a linear voltage-to-current stage, TO DESIGN: an op-amp stage (+IN = CV; output →

LED anode; LED cathode → R_sense → GND; R_sense node → -IN; I = V_CV / R_sense) or an op-amp driving an owned transistor (2N3904 etc., kit contents UNVERIFIED) as a current sink. R_sense depends on the owned vactrol's LED rating, unread (OPEN (owner), BF Q2). CV comes from the new MB panel jack, not DB-9 B pin 3 (now VCA CV).

Issue: Vactrol response asymmetry

Status: BY DESIGN

  • LED on-time: ~1-5ms, LDR off-time: ~5-50ms (typical vactrol figures; the owned part is

UNVERIFIED)

  • This asymmetric response is musically useful (natural attack/release)
  • For faster response: use photodiode instead of LDR (but loses

the musical character)

5. CV Input Protection (DB-9 B Filter CV and VCA CV)

Issue: Clamp voltage, series resistor and back-feed

Status: CORRECTED (audit B17, S39; BF 3.3)

  • The old entry (1kΩ series, BAT54S to ±12 V, "±12.3 V, 12 mA, within absolute max") is withdrawn,

and so are the other drawn versions (±5 V clamp with a -5 V rail that does not exist; BAT54S to +5 V / GND "-0.3 / +5.3 V"). A +5 V / GND clamp would clip legitimate CV into the synth's ±12 V summing node; 1kΩ lets milliamps into the unpowered breakout rails.

  • One circuit per line (B:3 VCA CV → TP10, B:5 Filter CV → TP26): 10kΩ at the expander output,

cable, 100kΩ on the MB board, then BAT85 to +12V_BRK and from -12V_BRK (two owned BAT85 per line), 1nF to GND, then the injection point.

  • Synth off, expander on: at most (10 - 0.24) / 110k ≈ 89 µA into the unpowered rail. Bounded,

not zero (acceptance BF BT-3).

  • CV depth with the extra 100kΩ: UNVERIFIED (E-18, BT-4); fallback 47kΩ.

6. Noise Generator

DROPPED (archive). The noise generator is out of the expander scope (audit section 1, S59); the rack's existing noise module covers it. Kept for reference only.

Issue: 2N3904 selection

Status: CORRECT with note

  • Not all 2N3904s avalanche at the same voltage
  • Typical B-E breakdown: 6-8V
  • With 2x 470kΩ from +12V: junction sees ~9.4V (divider with ~1MΩ total)

→ should exceed breakdown

  • If no noise: Try different 2N3904 samples or increase bias voltage

(single 220kΩ instead of 2x 470kΩ)

Issue: Noise level

Status: CORRECT

  • Gain of 47x (4.7MΩ/100kΩ) gives ~5-8Vpp output
  • Adequate for Eurorack (~10Vpp standard, noise is typically quieter)

7. LFO

Issue: Integrator output swing

Status: CORRECT

  • TL072 saturates at approximately ±(Vcc-1.5V) = ±10.5V
  • Schmitt trigger: NON-INVERTING (triangle → 50kΩ → +in, 100kΩ from output → +in, -in to GND);

thresholds at ±Vsat × 50k/100k = ±Vsat/2 ≈ ±5.25V. The earlier inverting version (triangle on -in) latched at a rail because the integrator already inverts (fix round 1).

  • Triangle amplitude: peak-to-peak = 2 × 5.25V ≈ 10.5Vpp
  • Eurorack compatible (10Vpp standard)

Issue: Square output level

Status: CORRECT

  • Raw square: ±10.5V (~21Vpp) — TOO HOT for Eurorack
  • Voltage divider (1.8kΩ + 3.3kΩ) scales to ±3.6V (~7.2Vpp)
  • Correction: For ±5V standard, use 2.2kΩ + 3.3kΩ:

Vout = ±10.5 × 3.3/(2.2+3.3) = ±6.3V — still slightly hot

  • Better: 3.3kΩ + 3.3kΩ: ±5.25V — closer to standard
  • Recommendation: Use 3.3kΩ + 3.3kΩ divider, then a 1kΩ series output resistor (audit N14).

Issue: Rate range

Status: CORRECTED (audit S60, S61)

  • With thresholds at ±Vsat × R1/R2 the triangle travels 2 × Vsat × R1/R2 per half-period at

slope Vsat / (RC), so T = 4RC × R1/R2 = 2RC for R1/R2 = 1/2; Vsat cancels (derived, not measured; E-27). Derivation in expander_circuits.md section 1.

  • R = 1MΩ pot + 10kΩ, C = 1µF: slow end T ≈ 2.0 s (about 0.5 Hz); pot at 0: T = 20 ms (about 50 Hz).

The old "0.04-40 Hz" was wrong.

  • The 10kΩ series resistor is mandatory: at pot = 0 it is the only thing limiting the current from

the Schmitt output into the integrator.

  • Parts: 1µF film and 1MΩ pots are not owned (BF Q6); an owned 100kΩ pot makes the range about 10×

faster.

  • Open: the connection map and BF 1.1 name a CD40106 as the LFO Schmitt, while this review and

expander_circuits.md use the second TL072 section. Which one is used is OPEN (owner); the range above assumes the TL072 version.

8. Clock Divider (CD4024)

DROPPED (archive). Clock division is done in Pico firmware (GP16-18); the CD4024 is not owned (audit S59, BF 1.1). Kept for reference only. The expander's Clock IN uses 100kΩ + a CD4049UB buffer on Pico 3V3 instead (BF 3.7).

Issue: 5V logic with Eurorack levels

Status: CORRECT

  • Input conditioning via 120kΩ + 100kΩ divider: scales 10V → ~4.2V
  • CD40106 Schmitt trigger at +5V cleans signal
  • Output 1kΩ series resistors protect against shorts

Issue: Reset pin

Status: CORRECT

  • Pin 2 (RST) pulled LOW via 10kΩ → counter runs freely
  • Optional momentary button to +5V for manual reset
  • Add 100nF cap across reset button for debounce

9. Sample & Hold (LF398)

Issue: Hold capacitor selection

Status: CORRECTED (audit S63, B13; datasheet TI SNOSBI3C, docs/DATASHEETS.md (a))

  • Hold capacitor: 10 nF polystyrene or polypropylene film (0.01 µF is the characterised value,

p7). Not owned: buy with the LF398 (BF Q1).

  • Low dielectric absorption: polystyrene, polypropylene or Teflon; mica and polycarbonate are not

nearly as good (p15). The owned 1 nF ceramic is not used here.

  • NEVER use electrolytic (leakage)
  • Leakage into the hold capacitor: 30 pA typ, 200 pA max (LF398-N, 25 °C, p7). Droop with 10 nF:

about 3 mV/s typ, 20 mV/s max (derived as I / C, not a TI figure). The old "3 pA / 1 nF = 3 mV/s" used a wrong leakage figure.

  • Hold step 1 mV typ, 2.5 mV max at 0.01 µF (p7); acquisition to 0.1 % about 20 µs at 0.01 µF.

Issue: Pinout and trigger

Status: CORRECTED / TO DESIGN

  • PDIP-8 pinout (p3): 1 V+, 2 OFFSET ADJUST, 3 INPUT, 4 V-, 5 OUTPUT, 6 Ch, 7 LOGIC REFERENCE,

8 LOGIC. There is no "IN-" feedback pin; the three older pinouts in the repo are wrong (B13).

  • Sample when LOGIC is high relative to LOGIC REFERENCE, hold when low (p14). Logic threshold

1.4 V typ (p5); logic edges need at least 1 V/µs (p15); the logic-to-reference differential limit is printed on p4. Trigger conditioning from a rack gate is required (audit S65): TO DESIGN.

  • Owned-parts alternative to buying the LF398: a CD4051 channel as the switch, a TL072 follower and

the same 10 nF film cap (expander_circuits.md section 2b). It cannot run from ±12 V (CD4051 V+ to V- 20 V abs max); charge injection UNVERIFIED. LF398 stays the default.

10. Slew Limiter

Issue: TL072 rail-to-rail behavior

Status: NEEDS ATTENTION

  • Datasheet: at ±15 V the common-mode range is ±11 V min, -12 to +15 V typ (TI SLOS080W p15),

so about ±8 V min on ±12 V rails.

  • Recommendation: For full ±10V range, consider:
  1. TL062 (lower power but same range) — NOT better; not owned
  2. Add 10kΩ input attenuator (halve signal to ±5V) — simple fix
  3. Use OPA2134 (rail-to-rail output, wider input) — not owned
  • Simplest fix: Accept ±8V range (adequate for most CV signals)
  • Parts: 1N4148 steering diodes are owned (owner, kit contents UNVERIFIED); 1MΩ pots are not (BF Q6).

11. JF-33 Anti-Latch-Up

Issue: Timing

Status: CORRECT

  • RC = 100kΩ × 1µF = 100ms
  • BC337 reaches saturation at ~3-5τ = 300-500ms
  • PT2399 datasheet requires >100ms startup delay
  • 300ms provides adequate margin

Issue: BC337 saturation voltage

Status: CORRECT

  • BC337 Vce(sat) ≈ 0.3V at 100mA
  • At ~5-10mA collector current (PT2399 pin 6): Vce(sat) < 0.1V
  • Negligible effect on delay time control accuracy

12. JF-33 Delay Time CV

Issue: Emitter resistor value

Status: CORRECTED

  • Originally showed 220Ω → max 22.7mA (WOULD DESTROY PT2399)
  • Corrected to 1kΩ → max 5mA (within PT2399 safe operating range)
  • PT2399 datasheet: pin 6 current range 50µA to 5.4mA
  • At 1kΩ emitter R: 0-5V CV → 0-5mA → full delay range covered

Issue: 1N4148 protection

Status: CORRECT

  • Diode prevents reverse current if CV goes negative
  • Cathode to pin 6, anode to ground
  • Also protects 2N3904 collector from reverse bias

13. Power Distribution

Issue: Reverse polarity protection

Status: CORRECTED

  • Two separate supplies (split power): the breakout from TP70 / TP71 / TP72, the expander from the

rack 16-pin header. No supply crosses the DB-9 cable.

  • Series Schottky per rail on the expander header (justified against reverse insertion, audit N04);

on the breakout a BAT85, an owned 1N5819 or a 4.7-10 Ω resistor per rail (OPEN (owner), C12). 1N5817 is not owned (20 V part); owned BAT85 is used (BF 1.2). -12 V diode: cathode to the source, anode to the rail.

  • Ferrite beads not owned (omitted); bulk 2-4 owned 10µF / 63 V per rail instead of 47µF / 100µF.

Issue: Power budget

Status: NOT VERIFIED (audit S18, H5). The old table (TL074 × 3, CD4024, LF398 ~5 mA, 6 LEDs, 78L05, "Total +12V ~102mA") matched neither board and is withdrawn.

  • Datasheet figure: TL07x quiescent current 1.4 mA typ, 2.5 mA max per amplifier (TI SLOS080W

p16). LF398 supply current is not quoted in docs/DATASHEETS.md (E-06).

  • Reviewer estimates, UNVERIFIED until recomputed: breakout about 35 / 60 mA typ / worst on +12 V;

expander about 25-55 mA on +12 V and 75-150 mA on +5 V (r2).

  • Rack: CP1A gives +12 V 1 A, -12 V 1 A, +5 V 0.5 A shared with every module (CP1A QSG p20).

Synth rail capacity for the breakout load: UNVERIFIED (E-04).

Summary of Corrections Needed

Several items above stay OPEN or TO DESIGN; nothing here is bench-verified.

4. Breakout Board
▶ Internal Breakout PCB — Schematic schematics/breakout_pcb.md
Output Buffer Board
Per-channel output buffer (TL072 unity-gain) used on every audio path that leaves the MicroBrute via DB-9 A — input impedance > 100 kΩ, output series 1 kΩ for cable drive.
Gate Buffer
Gate buffer using a CD40106 Schmitt trigger for clean rising edges to the expander's clock divider and any external trigger inputs.
Vactrol Driver
Vactrol driver (2N3904 + LED + LDR pair). Used for soft-knee filter modulation from external CVs — slow attack/release, naturally smooth.
CV Input Protection
Per-channel CV input protection (BAT54S Schottky to ±12 V rails + 1 kΩ series). Clamps any input to ±12.3 V; series resistor limits fault current to ~12 mA.
MACROBRUTE — Breakout Board Stripboard Layout
Physical layout of the breakout stripboard — IC positions, power rails, decoupling caps, and where each I/O wire enters/exits.
Power Distribution
STALE (to be redrawn, see roadmap batch A): decided design has NO supply on the cable, only shared ground, and no I²C; see connection map sections 2-3. Power distribution across the breakout PCB and expander — Eurorack ±12 V bus, 78L05 local +5 V regulator, decoupling caps per supply pin pair, ferrite-bead noise rejection on the +5 V branch.
Output Buffer Board
Sub-section of the breakout dedicated to the audio output buffers (TL074 quad). Shows where each channel sits relative to power rails and connectors.
Power Regulation Diagram
Split power chain. The expander runs from the Eurorack rack (CP1A) only; the MicroBrute breakout is powered from the synth test points TP70, TP71 and TP72 only. DB-9 A and B carry signals and grounds, with no supply on the cable. Unmeasured currents are tagged UNVERIFIED; nothing is built.
Pico Power Protection
Pico VSYS protection from the rack +5 V: series Schottky D1 (drawn as the owned 1N5819, OWNER-CONFIRM) → 2-4x 10 µF/63 V bulk → 100 nF → Pico VSYS (pin 39). Design values only, nothing built; unmeasured figures are tagged.

Mounts inside MicroBrute. A buffer-only board powered from the synth (TP70 / TP71 / TP72): output buffers, gate conditioner, CV-input clamps, the vactrol driver (TO DESIGN) and the DB-9 connections. The Pico, OLED, encoder, tap button and RGB LED live on the expander, not here (connection map section 9; audit S12).

Status: design values only, nothing is built. Values come from the back-feed and hum design note (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-backfeed-hum-design.md, "BF" below) and the audit (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md). Items marked Provisional follow the audit recommendation and wait for the owner. Anything not proven by a datasheet is UNVERIFIED.

Power Supply (from MicroBrute rails)

The breakout takes power only from TP70 / TP71 / TP72. No supply crosses the DB-9 cable, and no synth 5 V or 3V3 is tapped (TP56 is "per original doc" only, TP141 is the 5 V precision reference, P4 pin 5 is the LPC's own +3V3ARM; audit B09).

MicroBrute +12V (TP70) ──[D1 BAT85: anode at TP70, cathode at rail]──┬── +12V_BRK
                                                                     │
                                                     2-4× 10µF/63V ──┤── 100nF at each IC V+ pin
                                                                     │
                                                                    GND (TP72 star)

MicroBrute -12V (TP71) ──[D2 BAT85: cathode at TP71, anode at rail]──┬── -12V_BRK
                                                                     │
                                                     2-4× 10µF/63V ──┤── 100nF at each IC V- pin
                                                                     │
                                                                    GND (TP72 star)

+12V_BRK ── 78L05 pin 3 (INPUT) ; pin 2 (COMMON) ── GND ; pin 1 (OUTPUT) ──┬── +5V_LOC (U3 CD40106 only)
                                                                          100nF
                                                                           │
                                                                          GND
  • Diode rule (one rule, audit B15): on +12 V the anode faces TP70 and the cathode the rail; on

-12 V the cathode faces TP71 / the -12 V source and the anode faces the breakout rail (load). Either way the diode conducts in normal operation and blocks a reversed supply.

  • Rail protection part: OPEN (owner), audit conflict C12. Option 1: one owned BAT85 per rail as

drawn (uses 2 of the 10 owned BAT85; BF 1.2). Option 2: a 4.7-10 Ω series resistor per rail instead, which frees two BAT85 for hum-ladder step 4 (BF 4.5, Q3). Option 3: an owned 1N5819 (40 V / 1 A Schottky, 0.60 V max at 1 A, docs/DATASHEETS.md (e); owned x10 (owner, kit card contents UNVERIFIED)) per rail, same orientation rule; this also frees two BAT85. The 1N5817 in older drawings is a 20 V part (not 40 V) and is not owned; the 1N5819 serves where the docs wanted a 1N5817.

  • BAT85 drop: 400 mV at 10 mA, 800 mV at 100 mA (BAT85 p2-p3), so the rails sit roughly 0.4-0.7 V

inside ±12 V at the expected load. Breakout load and synth rail capacity are UNVERIFIED (audit E-04).

  • Bulk: 100µF parts are not owned; use 2-4 owned 10µF / 63 V in parallel per rail (BF 1.4).

Ferrite beads are not owned and are omitted (BF 1.5).

  • +5V_LOC (Provisional, BF 3.4): owned 78L05 from +12V_BRK, for the CD40106 only. TO-92 pinout

1 OUTPUT, 2 COMMON, 3 INPUT (TI SLVS010X p3; the owned parts' maker is unknown, so check the marking). The TI sheet states no external capacitor is needed for stability (p1); the 100nF is local decoupling. Dropout 1.7 V typ, quiescent 3.8 mA (BF 3.4).

Output Buffer Board (TL074 #1 — 4 channels)

Buffers waveform test point taps. Unity-gain voltage followers prevent loading the MicroBrute's internal circuits.

                    +12V_BRK
                       │
                 ┌─────┤
                 │   ┌──┴──┐
  TP94 (Saw) ────┤   │     │
       via 1kΩ   ├───┤+ TL074├──┬──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 7 (Saw Out)
                 │   │  A   │   │
                 │   └──┬──┘   │
                 │      │       │
                 └──────┼───────┘ (feedback: op-amp output pin → inverting input,
                        │          taken BEFORE the 1kΩ output resistor)
                    -12V_BRK

  TP93 (Square) ──1kΩ──┤+  TL074 B├──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 8 (Square Out)
  TP30 (VCO Mix)──1kΩ──┤+  TL074 C├──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 5 (VCO Mix Out)
  TP19 (VCF Out)──1kΩ──┤+  TL074 D├──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 6 (VCF Out)

Each channel:

  Test Point ──[1kΩ]──┬──[TL074 +in]
                      │
                     1MΩ to GND (bias)

  TL074 out pin ──┬── TL074 -in   (feedback at the output pin)
                  │
                [1kΩ]  (output isolation, outside the loop)
                  │
               DB-9 A pin

Component values per channel:

  • R_series: 1kΩ (input protection / isolation)
  • R_bias: 1MΩ to GND (replaces 10MΩ: an open input floats less and picks up less hum; audit N11)
  • R_output: 1kΩ after the feedback tap (stable into the cable; audit S36, R3-15)
  • C_decouple: 100nF ceramic per supply pin

Input level: the TL074 linear common-mode range is about 4 V inside each rail (TI SLOS080W p11, p15), so about ±8 V on these rails. Saw / square / mix / VCF peaks are UNVERIFIED (audit N10, E-19): scope TP94 / TP93 / TP30 / TP19 first and add a 2:1 input divider if peaks exceed about ±8 V.

Gate Buffer (CD40106 Schmitt Trigger)

Provisional (audit recommendation, owner has not confirmed; BF 3.4 and 3.5). TP83 has 100kΩ source impedance. The old 10kΩ pull-up to +5V is removed: with TP83 low it held pin 1 at about 5 V × 110k / 120k = 4.58 V, above VT+, so the input could never read low (audit B14).

  TP83 (Gate) ──[10kΩ]──┬─── U3 pin 1 (input A)        no pull-up
                         │
                        1nF (owned; at the pin)
                         │
                        GND

  U3 pin 2 (output A) ──── U3 pin 3 (input B)          second inverter: A:1 follows TP83 polarity
  U3 pin 4 (output B) ──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 1 (Gate Out)

  U3 pins 5, 9, 11, 13 (unused inputs) ── GND          (audit S34)
  U3 pin 14 VDD = +5V_LOC (78L05)
  U3 pin 7  VSS = GND
  100nF decoupling VDD to VSS

Expander side of A:1 (BF 3.5, Provisional): A:1 → gate jack (tapped here) → 22kΩ → node → 33kΩ to GND; node → Pico GP11, a fault-tolerant GPIO (GATE_IN; PROVISIONAL (BT-14): the OLED CS pin is tied to GND so GP11 can take this input, CM 12G). High level 5 V × 33k / (1k + 22k + 33k) = 2.95 V. No 5 V net reaches a Pico GPIO. The CD4049UBE is not on the gate path: it sits on the expander as the clock buffer (BF 3.7).

Output: 0 / +5V_LOC gate through 1kΩ. Open item: the CD40106 needs TP83 above VT+ (2.2 / 2.9 / 3.6 V min / typ / max at VDD 5 V, TI SCHS097F p5-p6). TP83's level is UNVERIFIED (E-09); if it is 3.3 V logic this stage must be redesigned (OPEN (owner), BF Q15; no synth 3V3 tap allowed). RC at pin 1: (100k + 10k) × 1 nF ≈ 0.11 ms.

Envelope & LFO Taps (from mod matrix)

These signals are available at the front panel mod matrix connections. Buffer with U2 TL072 (not a second TL074; connection map section 9).

  Envelope (mod matrix / TP5) ──[10kΩ]──┤+ TL072 A follower├──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 3
  LFO (mod matrix)            ──[10kΩ]──┤+ TL072 B follower├──[1kΩ]── DB-9 A pin 4

The 1kΩ sits after the feedback tap (audit S36, R3-15). Source choice for the envelope (TP5 vs mod matrix) and the meaning of TP21 are UNVERIFIED (audit N23, E-17).

Triangle Buffer (with 2x Gain)

Research confirmed TP124 (triangle) is inherently quieter than other waveform outputs. Instead of a unity follower, use a non-inverting amplifier with 2x gain to match levels with saw/square. The output goes to a body jack: DB-9 A has no free pin (connection map section 5.1; audit S35).

  TP124 (Triangle) ──[1kΩ]──┬── TL072 section (+in)
                             │         │
                            1MΩ       out ──┬── [1kΩ] ── body jack
                             │              │
                            GND       -in ──┴── 100kΩ (Rf, feedback from the output pin)
                                       │
                                     100kΩ (Rg, to GND)

  Gain = 1 + Rf/Rg = 1 + 100k/100k = 2x
  Gain accuracy follows the resistor-kit tolerance (1 % parts are not owned, BF Q5).

Op-amp sections: U2 (TL072) has two sections but four jobs (env, LFO, triangle, vactrol driver). U1/U2: TL074C or TL072IP, both owned (×4 / ×6); final op-amp count and split chosen at breakout layout (audit S17 / C10).

LED Drivers — removed

Removed (audit S12, R3-17): the RGB LED and its drive are on the expander (Pico GP8-10, connection map sections 1 and 10), so nothing on the breakout drives an LED. (The 2N3904 is now owned, but that does not change where the LED lives.)

Vactrol Driver (Resonance CV) — TO DESIGN

Finding (audit S37, R3-12): the old drawing used a TL072 driving a 2N3904 base through 1kΩ with the vactrol LED in the collector. As drawn no supply reached the collector; with the sensible reading (LED + R from +12 V to the collector) the LED current is fixed at about (12 - 2 - 0.2) / 1k ≈ 9 mA once the base is above about 0.8 V, so the vactrol works as an on/off switch, not a continuous resonance control. The base had no protection against negative TL072 swings, and the CV came from DB-9 B pin 3, which is now VCA CV (BF 2.2). The old circuit is withdrawn.

Replacement: a linear voltage-to-current stage, TO DESIGN until the vactrol marking is read. Constraints (r3 R3-12, BF 1.1, Q2):

  • Topology: either an op-amp stage (TL072 section, +IN = CV, output → vactrol LED anode, LED

cathode → R_sense → GND, R_sense node → -IN, so I_LED = V_CV / R_sense) or a transistor current sink driven by the op-amp with emitter feedback. The owner has 2N3904 / 2N3906 / S8050 / S8550 (owner, kit card contents UNVERIFIED), so either is possible; the choice is TO DESIGN. A bare saturated switch (the old circuit) is not acceptable.

  • R_sense depends on the owned vactrol's LED forward-current rating: the vactrol type and marking

are unread (OPEN (owner), BF Q2). No value is given here until then.

  • CV source: the new 3.5 mm resonance jack on the MicroBrute panel (connection map section 3,

"Migrated to MB panel"), not the DB-9. Input protection on that jack: series resistor plus clamps to ±12V_BRK as for the B CV lines (below); values TO DESIGN.

  • Negative CV must not reverse-bias the LED: an anti-parallel diode across the LED (r3 suggested a

BAT85, all 10 of which are allocated, BF 1.2; an owned 1N4148 (owner, kit card contents UNVERIFIED) can serve).

  • Op-amp section: assigned with the op-amp split at breakout layout (C10).
  • LDR side: the vactrol LDR in parallel with RP13 (resonance JFET path), as in the old docs;

UNVERIFIED against the synth schematic.

CV Input Protection (DB-9 B inputs)

One circuit for both B CV lines (audit B17, BF 3.3). Lines: B:3 VCA CV → TP10 and B:5 Filter CV → TP26 (BF 2.2). The expander adds 10kΩ at its op-amp output; the MB board adds:

  DB-9 B pin 3 or 5 ──[100kΩ]──┬────────────── to injection point (TP10 for B:3, TP26 for B:5)
                               │
                               ├── BAT85 anode at node, cathode to +12V_BRK
                               ├── BAT85 anode at -12V_BRK, cathode at node
                               └── 1nF (owned) ── GND
  • The clamps hold the node within about one BAT85 drop of the breakout rails. The old ±5 V clamp,

the "-0.3 V / +5.3 V" BAT54S clamp and the 1kΩ / "±12.3 V, 12 mA" text are withdrawn: a +5 V / GND clamp would clip legitimate CV into the synth's ±12 V summing node, and 1kΩ lets about 4-10 mA into the unpowered breakout rails (audit B17, S39). BAT54S is not owned; BAT85 is (two per line).

  • Back-feed (BF 3.3): with the synth off and the expander on, at most (10 - 0.24) / 110k ≈ 89 µA

flows into the unpowered breakout rail. Bounded, not zero; acceptance is BT-3 (unpowered rails below about 0.3 V).

  • CV depth: whether the synth's own 220kΩ (TP26, R67) and 100kΩ (TP10, R25) sit after these points

is UNVERIFIED (E-18); the extra 100kΩ may cut depth (BT-4). Fallback 47kΩ, then repeat BT-3.

  • 1nF with 100kΩ gives a 0.1 ms time constant (about 1.6 kHz corner).

The UART lines (B:1 TX, B:6 RX) go from the DB-9 B cups through the MB-side 1kΩ resistors to the LPC (connection map section 5.4); they do not use the breakout's op-amps. The LPC pins (UART1, LQFP 62 / 63) are UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity gate G1.

Pico H Mounting — removed

Removed (audit S12, R3-18). The Pico, OLED, encoder, tap button, RGB LED and clock I/O are on the expander (connection map sections 1, 4 and 10). No Pico header, VSYS path or 3V3 rail on the breakout.

PCB Size Estimate

  • ~60mm x 40mm (fits inside MicroBrute near digital board); the stripboard version is

90 × 50 mm (breakout_stripboard.md). Free space inside the synth is UNVERIFIED.

  • Single-sided perfboard adequate
  • Mount with VHB tape or M2 standoffs

▶ Breakout Board — Stripboard Layout schematics/breakout_stripboard.md
MACROBRUTE — Breakout Board Stripboard Layout
Physical layout of the breakout stripboard — IC positions, power rails, decoupling caps, and where each I/O wire enters/exits.

Mounts inside MicroBrute. Houses analog buffers, gate conditioning, CV-input clamps, the vactrol driver (TO DESIGN) and the power input. Powered from the synth only (TP70 / TP71 / TP72). The Pico is on the expander, not on this board (audit S12).

Board: 90 × 50mm stripboard, 20 rows × 28 cols, 2.54mm pitch (as drawn by tools/generate_layouts.py → breakout_layout.svg, "LAY" below; the old "35 columns" figure was wrong, audit B16) Tracks: Horizontal copper strips (left → right) View: All diagrams show COMPONENT SIDE (top view, looking down)

Build status: do not build from this page or from LAY yet. LAY is the reference geometry (audit R3-08, conflict C14), but it still carries the defects listed under "LAY defects" below, and the netlist on this page changes several circuits (gate stage, LED drivers removed, vactrol driver TO DESIGN). Hole-level positions for the changed parts are TO DESIGN when the layout is regenerated in a later diagram batch.

For pin-by-pin DIP layouts during the build, see ic_pinout_reference.md (pin tables checked against the datasheets). For the spatial component placement, see the MACROBRUTE — Breakout Board Stripboard Layout and Zone Layout SVGs in this section, with the caveat above.

Track Cuts (Copper Side)

Every DIP IC needs a track cut between its left and right pin columns to prevent shorting opposite pins. Use a 3mm drill bit twisted by hand or a proper stripboard track cutter.

The old placement on this page (U1 at cols 5/8, U2 at cols 18/21 on rows 6-9, cuts only at cols 6-7 and 19-20) shorted nets: rows 6-9 had no cut between col 8 and col 18, so U1 pin 14 (OUT_D) met U2 pin 1 (OUT_A), U1 pin 13 met U2 pin 2 and U1 pin 12 met U2 pin 3 (audit B16). On row 9 U1 pin 11 (V-) met U2 pin 4 (V-), the same net and harmless. The placement below is LAY's, which has no such short.

U1 — TL074 at rows 6-12, left col 10, right col 13

Row Cut At Left Pin Right Pin Why
6 cols 11, 12 1 OUT_A 14 OUT_D Different outputs
7 cols 11, 12 2 -IN_A 13 -IN_D Different feedback
8 cols 11, 12 3 +IN_A 12 +IN_D Different inputs
9 cols 11, 12 4 V+ 11 V- CRITICAL: V+ vs V-
10 cols 11, 12 5 +IN_B 10 +IN_C Different inputs
11 cols 11, 12 6 -IN_B 9 -IN_C Different feedback
12 cols 11, 12 7 OUT_B 8 OUT_C Different outputs

Further LAY cuts: col 15 on rows 6, 8, 10, 12 (IC right pins vs headers); col 20 on rows 8, 10 (output headers vs right-side input resistors); cols 6 and 22 on rows 8, 10 (input 1kΩ in series).

U2 — TL072 at rows 15-18, left col 22, right col 25

Row Cut At Left Pin Right Pin
15 cols 23, 24 1 OUT_A 8 V+
16 cols 23, 24 2 -IN_A 7 OUT_B
17 cols 23, 24 3 +IN_A 6 -IN_B
18 cols 23, 24 4 V- 5 +IN_B

Further LAY cuts: col 26 on row 15 (V+ vs the A:3 header); cols 19 on rows 17, 18 and col 21 on row 18 (input 10kΩ in series; V- vs the LFO input).

U3 — CD40106 at rows 13-19, left col 5, right col 8

Row Cut At Left Pin Right Pin

15 cols 6, 7, 9 3 IN_B 12 OUT_F

18 cols 6, 7, 9 6 OUT_C 9 IN_D
19 cols 6, 7, 9 7 VSS 8 OUT_D

Col 9 isolates the right-hand pins from the area to the right. Row 13 also has a cut at col 4 (TP83 series 10kΩ).

  • Row 3, cols 3 and 6: +12V input pad (col 1) → D1 → series element → +12V rail.
  • Row 4, cols 3 and 6: same for -12V. In LAY D2 is drawn in the same direction as D1, which is

backwards for -12V (audit B15): see the power table below.

the synth and there is no Pico on this board.

LED Drivers — removed

Vactrol Driver — TO DESIGN

The old 2N3904 driver is withdrawn: it switched the LED on/off at about 9 mA instead of giving a continuous control, and took CV from DB-9 B pin 3, which is now VCA CV (audit S37). Replacement: a linear voltage-to-current stage (op-amp, or op-amp plus an owned transistor), CV from the new MB panel jack. R_sense waits for the vactrol marking (OPEN (owner), BF Q2). Constraints are listed in breakout_pcb.md, "Vactrol Driver".

CV Input Clamps (DB-9 B:3 VCA CV, B:5 Filter CV)

Per line (BF 3.3): DB-9 B cup → 100kΩ → node; node → BAT85 (anode) to +12V_BRK (cathode); BAT85 anode at -12V_BRK, cathode at node; 1nF node to GND; node → TP10 (B:3) or TP26 (B:5). Position TO DESIGN.

Build & Test Order

  1. Solder DIP sockets (U1, U2, U3) — do NOT insert ICs yet
  2. Make all track cuts — verify each with multimeter continuity
  3. Power section: Solder D1, D2 (check D2: cathode on the -12V header side), the bulk and

decoupling caps, and the 78L05

  1. Test power: Apply +12V/-12V only, measure at IC socket pins:
  • U1 socket: pin 4 = +12V_BRK, pin 11 = -12V_BRK, verify NO short between them
  • U2 socket: pin 8 = +12V_BRK, pin 4 = -12V_BRK
  • U3 socket: pin 14 = +5V_LOC, pin 7 = 0V
  1. Insert U1 (TL074): Solder feedback jumpers, input/output resistors,

bias resistors. Test each channel with a signal source.

  1. Insert U2 (TL072): Same process for aux buffers.
  2. Insert U3 (CD40106): Solder gate conditioning components.

Test with manual gate (touch the 10kΩ input end to +5V_LOC); scope TP83 high and low first (BF BT-5).

  1. CV clamps: Solder the 100kΩ / BAT85 / 1nF networks; check the clamp diode orientation.
  2. Vactrol driver: TO DESIGN; build and test on the bench before installing.
  3. Connector headers: Solder J_IN, J_OUT, J_CV_IN last.
