Makefile

# MACROBRUTE Firmware Makefile

# Project
PROJECT = uberbrute
VERSION = 0.1.0

# Toolchain
CC = arm-none-eabi-gcc
AS = arm-none-eabi-as
LD = arm-none-eabi-ld
OBJCOPY = arm-none-eabi-objcopy
SIZE = arm-none-eabi-size

# Directories
SRC_DIR = src
BUILD_DIR = build
INC_DIR = include

# Source files
SRCS = $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.c) \
       $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/**/*.c)
ASMS = $(wildcard startup/*.s)

OBJS = $(SRCS:$(SRC_DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o) \
       $(ASMS:%.s=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)

# Flags
CPU = -mcpu=arm7tdmi
CFLAGS = $(CPU) -mthumb-interwork -g -O2 -Wall
CFLAGS += -I$(SRC_DIR) -I$(INC_DIR)
CFLAGS += -DDEBUG_LEVEL=2

LDFLAGS = $(CPU) -mthumb-interwork
LDFLAGS += -T linker/lpc2361.ld
LDFLAGS += -nostartfiles
LDFLAGS += --specs=nano.specs

# Targets
.PHONY: all clean flash monitor

all: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).hex $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).bin
	@$(SIZE) $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).elf

$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).elf: $(OBJS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^

$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).hex: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).elf
	$(OBJCOPY) -O ihex $< $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).bin: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).elf
	$(OBJCOPY) -O binary $< $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(SRC_DIR)/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: startup/%.s
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(AS) $(CPU) -o $@ $<

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)

flash: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT).hex
	./tools/flash.sh $<

monitor:
	./tools/monitor.sh

# Debug build
debug: CFLAGS += -DDEBUG_LEVEL=3
debug: all

# Release build (no debug)
release: CFLAGS += -DDEBUG_LEVEL=0 -Os
release: all

docs/debugging.md

# MACROBRUTE Debugging Guide

## Printf Debugging

This firmware uses printf-style debugging over UART. No JTAG required.

### Hardware Setup

Connect your USB-TTL adapter:

| USB-TTL | LPC2361 (MicroBrute) |
|---------|---------------------|
| TX | P0.3 (RXD0) - Pin 99 |
| RX | P0.2 (TXD0) - Pin 98 |
| GND | GND |
| 3.3V | DO NOT CONNECT |

### Serial Settings

- Baud: 115200
- Data: 8 bits
- Parity: None
- Stop: 1 bit
- Flow control: None

### Viewing Debug Output

Linux:

./tools/monitor.sh

or

minicom -D /dev/ttyUSB0 -b 115200


Windows:
- Use PuTTY
- Select COM port
- Set baud to 115200

### Debug Levels

Set in `config.h`:

#define DEBUG_LEVEL 2


| Level | Output |
|-------|--------|
| 0 | None (production) |
| 1 | Errors only |
| 2 | Errors + Info (recommended) |
| 3 | Everything (very spammy) |

### Debug Macros

DBG_ERR("Something broke: %d", error_code); // Level 1+ DBG_INFO("State changed to: %s", state); // Level 2+ DBG_VERB("Processing byte: 0x%02X", byte); // Level 3 only


### Example Output

================================ MACROBRUTE v0.1.0 MicroBrute Expansion Firmware ================================ Compiled: Mar 21 2026 15:30:00 Debug level: 2

[INF] Init: System clock... [INF] Init: Debug UART... [INF] Init: GPIO... [INF] Init: Timer... [INF] Init: DAC... [INF] Init: Keyboard... [INF] Init: Sequencer... [INF] Sequencer: init 64 steps [INF] Sequencer: ready [INF] Init: Clock... [INF] Init: MIDI... [INF] === INIT COMPLETE === [INF] State: BOOT -> IDLE


### Debugging Tips

1. **Startup hangs?** Check which init message was last printed
2. **MIDI issues?** Enable level 3, watch for `[VRB] MIDI byte:`
3. **Sequencer problems?** Call `sequencer_print_state()` from main loop
4. **Timing issues?** Add heartbeat prints with loop counter

### Common Issues

**No output at all:**
- Check TX/RX wiring (they're crossed)
- Verify baud rate matches
- Make sure UART init runs before first printf

**Garbled output:**
- Wrong baud rate
- Wrong crystal frequency in config.h

**Missing messages:**
- Check DEBUG_LEVEL is high enough
- Printf buffer might be full (add small delays)

docs/isp-flashing.md

# ISP Flashing Guide

## Overview

The LPC2361 can be programmed via UART using In-System Programming (ISP).
This doesn't require a JTAG debugger.

## Hardware Setup

Same wiring as debug UART, plus ISP enable:

| USB-TTL | LPC2361 |
|---------|---------|
| TX | P0.3 (RXD0) - Pin 99 |
| RX | P0.2 (TXD0) - Pin 98 |
| GND | GND |

**ISP Enable:** P0.14 must be LOW during reset to enter ISP mode.

## Entering ISP Mode

1. Power off MicroBrute
2. Connect P0.14 to GND (jumper wire)
3. Power on MicroBrute
4. LPC2361 is now in ISP bootloader

## Flashing (Linux)

Install lpc21isp:

sudo apt install lpc21isp


Flash:

lpc21isp -control firmware.hex /dev/ttyUSB0 115200 12000


Or use the provided script:

./tools/flash.sh build/uberbrute.hex


## Flashing (Windows)

Use Flash Magic (free):
1. Download from flashmagictool.com
2. Select LPC2361
3. Set COM port and baud (115200)
4. Set crystal to 12000 kHz
5. Browse to .hex file
6. Click Start

## After Flashing

1. Remove ISP jumper (P0.14 to GND)
2. Reset or power cycle MicroBrute
3. New firmware runs

## Troubleshooting

**"No response from device":**
- Check wiring
- Verify ISP jumper is connected
- Try lower baud rate (38400)

**"Verify failed":**
- Flash might be protected (CRP)
- Try full erase first

**CRP (Code Read Protection):**
- If CRP is enabled, you can only do full erase
- Full erase wipes everything including CRP
- Then you can flash new firmware
▶ Custom Firmware Modification Plan docs/MACROBRUTE_FIRMWARE_MOD_PLAN.md

Overview

With the .mbf encryption cracked, we can create modified MicroBrute firmware and flash it via the standard MIDI SysEx update process. This document plans what modifications are worth pursuing and how they integrate with the broader MACROBRUTE project.

Flash Budget

Region Size Usage
Bootloader (0x0000-0x1FFF) 8 KB NXP ISP — do not touch
Stock firmware (0x2000-0xEDB7) 51 KB Application code (v1.0.4.114)
Free flash (0xEDB8-0x1FFFF) 68 KB Available for custom code
Total app space 120 KB 43% used, 57% free

68KB free is more than the stock firmware itself. We could nearly triple the codebase.

Re-encryption Pipeline

To flash modified firmware:

1. Modify .bin (ARM binary)
2. arm-none-eabi-objcopy -I binary -O ihex --change-addresses 0x2000 mod.bin mod.hex
3. Prepend: key string (24 bytes) + null byte (0x00) + Intel HEX text
4. XOR-encrypt with key "ArturiaminiBruteFirmware", start index 4
5. Flash via MicroBrute Connection or direct MIDI SysEx (28-byte packets)

A tools/mbf_encrypt.py tool will automate steps 3-4.

Safety Measures

  • Always preserve the vector table (first 0x54 bytes)
  • Never modify addresses below 0x2000 (bootloader)
  • Keep a stock .mbf backup — can always re-flash via MIDI SysEx
  • Test on breadboard LPC2361 first if available
  • Worst case: ISP recovery via PL2303HX on UART0 (P0.2/P0.3, P2.10 LOW)

Modification Tiers

Tier 1: Binary Patching (Low Risk)

Modify existing firmware bytes without adding new code. Safest approach.

Mod What Risk Benefit
Parameter range extension Patch min/max values in param tables Very low Wider bend range, extended swing
Default value changes Change power-on defaults Very low Custom startup state
DAC curve tweaks Modify pitch CV lookup values Low Custom tuning tables
MIDI channel defaults Change default MIDI channels Very low Convenience

Tier 2: Code Injection (Medium Risk)

Add new code in free flash space, patch jump targets to redirect execution.

Mod What Risk Benefit
Pico UART bridge Add a UART handler (UART1, P0.15/P0.16, UNVERIFIED) for Pico ↔ LPC2361 communication Medium Real-time parameter control from Pico
Extended SysEx Add custom SysEx commands beyond Arturia protocol Medium PC/DAW control of hidden parameters
Debug output Enable UART serial output of internal state Medium Live debugging during development
Custom sequencer modes Add Euclidean, probability, ratchet to built-in seq Medium-High Musical features

Tier 3: Major Rewrite (High Risk)

Replace significant sections of firmware.

Mod What Risk Benefit
Alternative tuning systems Replace pitch calculation with microtonal support High Microtonal synthesis
Custom oscillator modes Modify waveform generation parameters High New timbres
Full sequencer rewrite Replace stock sequencer with custom engine High Advanced sequencing

Priority Modifications for MACROBRUTE

Given the project goals (semi-modular expansion, Pico digital brain, high-impact sound-shaping focus):

1. Pico ↔ LPC2361 UART Bridge (Tier 2, HIGHEST PRIORITY)

Why: The Pico currently can only send SysEx to the MicroBrute via MIDI. A direct UART link between Pico (GP0/GP1, UART0) and LPC2361 (UART1: P0.16/RXD1 = pin 63, P0.15/TXD1 = pin 62, UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity check; the earlier UART0 choice is withdrawn because UART0 is the ISP port) would enable:

  • Real-time parameter reads (not just writes)
  • Low-latency bidirectional communication
  • Custom binary protocol (faster than SysEx)
  • State synchronization between Pico display and MicroBrute

Implementation:

  1. In Ghidra: locate the UART init code. The stock MIDI UART is UART3 (init at 0x3D88, base 0xE007C000); the earlier "UART0 init around 0x3EA8" was a literal-pool word, not code (audit S06). Confirm nothing writes UART1 registers via a computed base
  2. Find an unused IRQ slot in the VIC for the chosen UART
  3. Add ring buffer + simple command parser in free flash
  4. Connect to existing parameter structures
  5. Pico side: firmware/pico/lpc_comm.py already designed for this

Risk mitigation: UART0 is the ISP programming port and stays out of the bridge unless the UART1 pins turn out to be taken (they share pins with SSP0/SPI, which the stock firmware uses). Our code must NOT interfere with ISP mode (P2.10 LOW at reset). Only activate UART bridge after boot, when P2.10 is HIGH.

2. Debug Serial Output (Tier 2, HIGH PRIORITY)

Why: Understanding the firmware's runtime behavior before making bigger changes.

Implementation: Redirect C++ runtime error handlers (SIGPVFN, SIGRTMEM at 0xC7E4) to output via UART0. Add lightweight printf-like output for key events.

3. Extended SysEx Commands (Tier 2, MEDIUM PRIORITY)

Why: Allow Pico to query current parameter values, not just set them.

Implementation: Hook the existing SysEx dispatcher, add new command codes:

  • 0x80+: Query parameter value (response with current state)
  • 0x90+: Dump all parameters
  • 0xA0+: Trigger sequencer events

4. Parameter Range Extension (Tier 1, LOW PRIORITY)

Why: Some parameters have artificially limited ranges (e.g., bend range 1-12, swing 50-75). Extending these could unlock new musical territory.

Implementation: Binary patch the bounds-checking constants in the param table area.

Ghidra Analysis Roadmap

Before any modifications, we need a thorough Ghidra analysis:

Phase 1: Structural Mapping

  1. Load firmware/MicroBrute_Firmware_Update_1_0_4_114.bin as ARM:LE:32:v4t, base 0x2000
  2. Install SVD-Loader with LPC23xx SVD
  3. Mark vector table at 0x2000, handler pointers at 0x2020
  4. Auto-analyze, then manual pass on unresolved functions
  5. Label all peripheral register accesses (use our peripheral map)

Phase 2: Function Identification

  1. UART init — stock MIDI is UART3 (init at 0x3D88, base 0xE007C000); the old "UART0 init around 0x3EA8" entry is a literal-pool word (audit S06). Check UART1 (base 0xE0010000) for computed-base use
  2. SPI handler — around 0x4348 (MCP4728 DAC communication?)
  3. Timer0 handler — around 0x3F70 (tempo/sequencer timing?)
  4. SysEx parser — search for 0xF0 handling in UART/MIDI receive path
  5. Parameter store — find read/write functions for SysEx param codes
  6. DAC output — trace MCP4728 I2C writes for pitch CV
  7. GPIO handlers — button/LED control at 0x669C

Phase 3: Modification Points

  1. Map the SysEx command dispatch table
  2. Find free VIC interrupt slots for the chosen bridge UART (UART1, UNVERIFIED)
  3. Identify safe hook points for code injection
  4. Document all discovered function signatures

Integration with MACROBRUTE Build Plan

Build Phase Firmware Mod Integration
Phase 0 (Toolchain) Install arm-none-eabi-gcc, Ghidra. Write mbf_encrypt.py
Phase 1 (Pico bring-up) Test Pico firmware on breadboard, ready for UART bridge
Phase 2 (Internal wiring) Wire the LPC UART pins (UART1 P0.16/P0.15, pins 63/62, UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity check) to the breakout PCB → DB-9 B:1/B:6 → Pico GP0/GP1 (installed, unused until Phase 6C)
Phase 3 (Panel) No firmware changes needed
Phase 4 (Expander) No firmware changes needed
Phase 5 (Integration) Flash custom firmware with UART bridge, test Pico ↔ LPC2361 comm
Phase 6A (RE) Ghidra analysis, identify modification points

Recommended Order

  1. Ghidra analysis (can do now, no hardware needed)
  2. Write mbf_encrypt.py (can do now)
  3. Binary patch: debug serial output (first custom firmware test)
  4. UART bridge (after Ghidra identifies safe hook points)
  5. Extended SysEx (after UART bridge working)
  6. Parameter tuning (after understanding param table format)

Risk Assessment

Risk Likelihood Mitigation
Brick during flash Low Stock .mbf backup, ISP recovery via PL2303HX
Corrupt parameter EEPROM Low Parameters are reset on firmware update
Break MIDI functionality Medium Test SysEx before/after modification
Break audio output Medium Preserve DAC init and output path code
ISP bootloader damage None Bootloader is at 0x0000, we only write 0x2000+

The ISP bootloader cannot be damaged by flashing custom firmware through the normal update process — it only writes to the application area (0x2000+).

Files

File Purpose
tools/mbf_decrypt.py Decrypt .mbf → .hex → .bin
tools/mbf_encrypt.py Encrypt .bin/.hex → .mbf (with --verify round-trip)
tools/test_mbf_decrypt.py Automated test suite (52 tests: cipher, decrypt, encrypt, round-trip)
tools/ghidra_label_firmware.py Ghidra script: labels vectors, peripherals, known code locations
firmware/*.mbf Stock firmware backups (v1.0.4.114, v1.0.3.2)
firmware/*.bin Decrypted ARM binaries (gitignored, regenerate with decrypt tool)
docs/research/mbf_analysis.md Full technical analysis of cipher and firmware

▶ Comprehensive Build Plan docs/MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md
Phase0 Wiring Schematic
Flat schematic, power-rail style. Pico centre-right, +3V3 rail along the top, GND rail along the bottom. One 1.3" 7-pin SPI OLED sits on SPI0, write-only (GP2 SCK, GP3 MOSI, GP4 DC, GP5 RES); its CS pin goes to the GND bus, PROVISIONAL (BT-14), and GP11 (the gate input) is unused in Phase 0. UNVERIFIED: the chip (SSD1306 or SH1106) and the module pin order, so read the module first. Most Pico signal pins have their Y aligned with the matching peripheral pin so signal wires are straight horizontal lines. CLOCK IN is loop-back only, no external signals (no CD4049UB on the bench). MISSING (not owned, Q12): the RGB LED and the tactile button, and the half-size breadboard. UNVERIFIED: the RGB lead order R-K-G-B. Inline 220 Ω (RGB anodes) and 1 kΩ (clock series) resistors are drawn on their wires. Read this diagram to understand what connects to what before looking at the breadboard view.
Phase0 Breadboard
Top-down breadboard layout. Same circuit as the schematic above, drawn the way it physically sits on a half-size breadboard. The Pico straddles the centre channel; the single 1.3" 7-pin SPI OLED sits off the board, drawn flipped with its header toward the board, and is wired down to it with seven leads, its CS lead to the top GND rail (PROVISIONAL (BT-14)); +3V3 and GND rails run along the top and bottom; jumper paths are colour-coded by net, with a jumper table and part-lead holes below. UNVERIFIED: the OLED chip (SSD1306 or SH1106) and its pin order, so check the module before powering it, and the RGB lead order R-K-G-B. CLOCK IN is loop-back only, no external signals (no CD4049UB on the bench). MISSING (not owned): the RGB LED and tactile button (Q12) and the half-size breadboard itself.

Context

The MACROBRUTE project transforms an Arturia MicroBrute into a semi-modular instrument paired with a Eurorack expander. About 260 tracked files (263 on 2026-10-17): Pico MicroPython firmware (15 .py files: 14 modules plus the generated _effigy_constants.py), LPC2361 ARM7 C firmware skeleton (48 files), schematic docs (9 .md) and KiCad projects (breakout, expander), stripboard and diagram SVGs (83 SVGs repo-wide), panel SVGs, mod/bending guides, .mbf encryption cracked + firmware decrypted, and research docs.

Current status (2026-10-17): Design stage. This plan was reconciled against the project audit (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md), the back-feed and hum design note (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-backfeed-hum-design.md, cited as "BF") and the connection map (docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md, the authority for pins and wiring). The owner's own build plan comes after this redraft, so sections that still predate the decisions are marked STALE rather than redesigned. Firmware RE ~98% complete (43 SysEx commands, 107+ Ghidra labels). Pico firmware: firmware/pico/config.py is the canonical pin source. Stripboard layouts exist but several are stale (audit B16, S34). Touch test board designed (8 circuit bends, pending bench-test selection). Phase 0 bench validation is the next step — no physical build started yet.

Confirmed Decisions (owner answers 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17; reconciled 2026-10-17)

Source: audit sections 1a and 1b, BF, and docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md (the authority). Anything not proven stays UNVERIFIED.

Decision Detail
Expander HP OPEN: 17 HP or about 20 HP. The repo panel file panel/expander_17hp.svg is 87 mm wide with mounting holes 79 mm apart, both UNVERIFIED against the A-100 spec (audit S53, E-22). The owner measures the blank first; plan both layouts. Depth behind the panel UNVERIFIED (E-23).
Connector 2× shielded DB-9 (HD-15/VGA rejected: the cable shorts pins 6-8 to GND; no DB-25). Both mount on the MicroBrute rear panel, left of the Pitch/Gate section (owner decision a). Panel dimensions, free area and depth UNVERIFIED until the owner measures (audit E-20, E-21). DB-9 A = outputs; DB-9 B = UART TX, UART RX, Filter CV, VCA CV and grounds only. Pin maps: CM sections 2 and 3 (from BF 2.2 and 2.3).
Power Split. The expander is powered only from the rack (CP1A); the MicroBrute-side breakout only from the synth (TP70 +12 V, TP71 -12 V, TP72 GND). No supply rail crosses the DB-9 cable; only ground is shared.
Pico location Inside the expander (not the MicroBrute case). Board: Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350). Nothing here uses wireless.
OLED (primary) 1.3" 7-pin SPI (owner ruling, 2026-10-17; chip SSD1306 or SH1106 UNVERIFIED: read the module; module pin order UNVERIFIED) on SPI0, write-only: SCK GP2, MOSI GP3, DC GP4, RES GP5; CS tied to GND, no GPIO (PROVISIONAL, BT-14) — on the expander panel, powered from the Pico 3V3 (draw UNVERIFIED). Driver: firmware/pico/display.py (OLED_SPI; for SH1106: OLED_CHIP="SH1106", OLED_COL_OFFSET=2). A 1.3" module is larger than the 0.96" cutout, which bears on the open expander width. BF Q22.
OLED (strip) DROPPED (owner decision c). No I²C is used on the expander, and no I²C crosses the DB-9 cable.
OLED (alternatives) The owner's 1.3" 4-pin I²C module is wired into a TD-3: not available. The 0.96" SSD1306 (owner to confirm it has arrived) and the 16×2 1602 I²C LCD (separate driver) are alternatives only: an I²C display needs GP4/GP5, which are OLED DC/RES, so it requires re-pinning, not a drop-in.
MIDI paths (a) Pico ↔ LPC2361 UART bridge over DB-9 B pins 1 and 6 @ 115200 baud, XOR-checksummed frame; LPC-side UART is UART1 (P0.15/P0.16, pins 62/63), UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity check; (b) Pico USB-MIDI via micro-USB (TinyUSB MIDI class), not used while the DB-9 cables are connected (BF 4.3).
EFFIGY pair bus SHELVED (owner decision b): kept as an idea for another project; nothing is designed around it. GP2 and GP3 are now the main OLED's SCK and MOSI; GP11 is the gate input.
Hardware utilities Slew limiter, LFO, Sample & Hold (standalone rack utilities, rack power only, no synth cabling). Noise, mult and attenuverter stay out. S&H uses an LF398 (not owned) and a film hold capacitor (not owned).
Firmware utilities Clock divider (3 outputs, GP16/17/18), 4 programmable aux outputs (GP19/20/6/7) — replaces the dropped CD4024. Clock I/O on the expander only.
RGB LED Common-cathode on GP8/9/10 — R=clock tick, G=gate, B=mode (the old "pair" meaning is shelved). On the expander.
Touch mods 8 body-contact bends designed; bench-test in Phase 0 → pick 6
JF-33 delay Moved to spinoffs/jf33-eurorack/ — DIY PT2399 delay; not part of the canonical MACROBRUTE build
DSO138 scope Moved to spinoffs/dso138-desktop/ — desktop scope; not a Eurorack module
EFFIGY DSP SHELVED (see above). docs/MACROBRUTE_EFFIGY_BRIDGE.md and firmware/pico/effigy_bridge.py are archived as an idea.
Norns Shield Anticipated only, not designed. See docs/MACROBRUTE_NORNS_BRIDGE.md; its EFFIGY half is shelved and no I²C pins are reserved for it.
PSU Behringer CP1A Eurorack PSU: -12 V @ 1 A (pins 1-2), +12 V @ 1 A (pins 9-10), +5 V @ 0.5 A (pins 11-12), GND pins 3-8, pins 13-16 not used (CP1A QSG p15, p20). Whether the owner's bus slot carries +5 V: UNVERIFIED (BF BT-12). Pico VSYS takes rack +5 V through a Schottky OR diode + bulk + 100 nF; the 1N5817 is a 20 V part and is not owned (an owned BAT85 can stand in, BF 1.2). MicroBrute stock power untouched.
Migrated to MB panel Resonance CV (new jack); reuse MB's existing back-panel Sync In / Gate In / Audio In
Owned parts Every circuit uses parts marked Have in docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_BOM.md; anything else is flagged with an owned alternative (BF section 1).

Badge legend: each phase heading shows its state and reversibility. VERIFIED built and tested on this rig · UNTESTED designed, not yet built · DRAFT still in design. REVERSIBLE no irreversible changes to the synth · DESTRUCTIVE involves panel cuts or trace cuts — plan accordingly.

Phase 0: Bench Validation — non-destructive (Week 1) UNTESTED REVERSIBLE

Goal: Validate Pico firmware on breadboard, confirm the OLED module (1.3" 7-pin SPI baseline; read the chip marking, SSD1306 or SH1106, and the pin order, both UNVERIFIED, BF Q22), locate test points, and pass the gate checks on the MicroBrute that later phases depend on (LPC UART pins, TP83 level, synth rail margin, DB-9 geometry). Full procedures: docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_PHASE0_BOM.md.

Wiring reference

The breadboard layout for Phase 0 lives in schematics/pico_pinout.md and is rendered as two diagrams:

  • phase0_wiring_schematic.svg — flat schematic, elbow-routed nets, useful for understanding what connects to what.
  • phase0_breadboard.svg — top-down breadboard view, jumper paths colour-coded by net (amber=+3V3, green=GND, blue=SPI0 OLED, red=RGB drive, orange=button and encoder, violet=clock).

Both match firmware/pico/config.py. Pin map covered: one OLED on SPI0 — the main display is the 1.3″ 7-pin SPI OLED (chip SSD1306 or SH1106 and pin order UNVERIFIED), SCK GP2, MOSI GP3, DC GP4, RES GP5, CS lead to the GND rail (PROVISIONAL, BT-14; later mounted on the expander panel). GP11 (gate input) is not used in Phase 0. KY-040 encoder on GP14/GP15/GP13 (firmware enables Pin.PULL_UP on all three), tap button on GP12 (active-LOW, Pin.PULL_UP), RGB LED (common cathode) R/G/B on GP8/GP9/GP10 via 220 Ω, clock OUT on GP22, clock IN on GP21 (Pin.PULL_DOWN, IRQ on rising edge).

Tasks

  • ☐ Flash Pico firmware (tools/flash_pico.sh). Run test_hw.py first for per-peripheral diagnostics. Its OLED check draws a test frame through display.OLED_SPI (copy display.py and config.py first); a working frame with CS on GND passes BT-14.
  • ☐ Confirm the main OLED draws its boot splash. If the display is blank: check the module pin order against its silkscreen (UNVERIFIED), SCK/MOSI not swapped (D0 = SCK, D1 = MOSI), then VCC vs GND polarity; if the image is shifted by two columns, the chip is probably SH1106 (OLED_COL_OFFSET=2).
  • ☐ Breadboard integration per the diagrams above: OLED + KY-040 encoder + tap button + RGB LED + clock IN/OUT
  • ☐ Self-loopback test: jumper GP22 → 1 kΩ → GP21 to confirm the firmware clock generator and IRQ-driven clock-in count match
  • ☐ MicroBrute inspection: locate TPs, measure panel gaps, photograph PCBs — DONE (teardown photos taken)
  • ☐ LPC2361 ISP pin survey (visual only — locate P0.2, P0.3, P2.10 on PCB). This feeds the UART continuity gate below
  • ☐ Verify PL2303HX USB-TTL with serial loopback

Phase 0 gate checks on the MicroBrute (probe only, no soldering)

Full procedures, pass criteria and the owner's recording sheet: docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_PHASE0_BOM.md. Each result is recorded before the phase that depends on it starts.

  • ☐ LPC UART continuity probe (gate before any Phase 6 bridge work): LPC2361 LQFP-100 pins 62/63 (P0.15/P0.16), pins 98/99 (the ISP UART), and 6N138 output to pin 85 (P4.29, expected). Rear board CU17002, power off, continuity mode. Procedure from audit decision 7. Never probe pins 96/97 (VDD(3V3) and VSS)
  • ☐ TP83 logic level: measure the high and low level of the gate test point (audit E-09). A 5 V CD40106 is only guaranteed to trigger above 3.6 V
  • ☐ Synth rail margin: adapter label, TP70/TP71 against TP72, baseline for the Phase 2 loaded check (audit E-04)
  • ☐ D-sub neighbour geometry (BF BT-7): caliper the owner's DB-9 insert and confirm the row offset and neighbour table
  • ☐ Optional: CP1A +5 V on bus pins 11-12 (BF BT-12); PC817 isolated-UART alternative noted, not required (BF 3.9)
  • ☐ Bench tests BT-1 to BT-13 are listed in the Phase 0 BOM file (names only; definitions and pass criteria in BF section 6.2). They run when the matching hardware exists, not all in Phase 0

Phase 1: Breakout Board Build (Week 2-3) UNTESTED REVERSIBLE

Goal: Build the buffer-only breakout board on stripboard and verify all buffer channels. The Pico, RGB LED and its drivers live on the expander, not on this board (CM section 9, audit S12). Layout: schematics/breakout_layout.svg (generated from tools/generate_layouts.py). STALE: this layout and schematics/breakout_stripboard.md still hold the old Pico/J_PICO/VSYS/Q1-Q3 design and have template defects (audit B16, S34); do not build from them until regenerated. The IC list and headers in CM section 9 are the reference.

Tasks

  • ☐ Cut tracks, solder DIP sockets (U1 TL074, U2 TL072, U3 CD40106)
  • ☐ Power section, fed only from TP70/TP71/TP72 (no Pico, no VSYS): rail protection per CM 5.3 (open choice, audit C12: an owned BAT85 per rail or a 4.7-10 Ω series resistor), bulk from 2-4× owned 10 µF/63 V in parallel per rail, no ferrite beads. If a diode is used on -12 V its cathode goes to the TP71 / -12 V side and its anode to the breakout rail (audit B15). Test rails under load.
  • ☐ Insert ICs, decoupling caps, feedback jumpers, bias resistors
  • ☐ Test each buffer channel with audio source (4× TL074 unity-gain followers)
  • ☐ Gate stage: CD40106, TP83 → 10 kΩ → pin 1 with 1 nF to GND, no pull-up, two gates in series so A:1 follows TP83 polarity, then 1 kΩ to DB-9 A:1; unused inputs tied to GND. Local +5 V from an owned 78L05 off +12V_BRK. Provisional (BF 3.4); TP83 level UNVERIFIED (E-09). The Square output is DB-9 A:8 from a TL074 follower; the triangle is not on the DB-9 (body jack, CM 12A).
  • ☐ No RGB LED driver, no VCO circuit and no CD4049 level shifter on this board. The gate reaches the Pico through a 22k/33k divider on the expander (BF 3.5).
  • ☐ Connector headers (J_PWR, J_IN, J_OUT, J_CV_IN per CM section 9)
  • ☐ Bench test the breakout alone with a signal generator and a scope; the Pico is not connected to this board

Test Checkpoint

  • ☐ All 4 buffer channels pass signal (play audio → measure output)
  • ☐ Gate stage follows a test square wave with the correct polarity; with TP83 at 3.3 V the CD40106 at 5 V may not trigger (VT+ up to 3.6 V, UNVERIFIED level), see BF Q15
  • ☐ Rails measured with the board loaded (synth rail drop and current margin, audit E-04)
  • Gate: All buffer channels pass signal and the gate stage behaves

STOP if any buffer channel fails — debug before proceeding.

Goal: Drill the MicroBrute panels and mount the touch bolts, panel jacks/toggles and the 2× DB-9. The OLED, encoder, tap button and RGB LED are on the expander (Phase 4), not on the MicroBrute. Template: panel/microbrute_panel_template.svg covers the top panel only. No rear-panel template exists; draw one after the owner's caliper measurements (audit decision 6). Risk: MEDIUM — drilling is irreversible. Practice on scrap first.

Tasks

  • ☐ Print 1:1 drilling template, tape to panel, verify clearances
  • ☐ Practice on scrap material: jack holes, toggle holes, touch-bolt holes, and the DB-9 cut-outs
  • ☐ Touch bolts: 6× 6mm holes for brass M3 bolts (selected from Phase 1B testing)
  • Spacing: 18-20mm horizontal between bolts to avoid accidental multi-touch
  • Labels: PITCH, CRUNCH, WAH, DISTORT, HARMONIC, GATE
  • [ ] Wire touch bolts with safety resistors to PCB points (permanent solder)
  • [ ] DB-9: 2× cutouts on the rear panel, left of the Pitch/Gate section (where the Arturia "A" logo is), solder-cup connectors. All dimensions UNVERIFIED until measured (audit E-20, E-21); mounting-hole spacing 24.99 mm per the Spectrum Control drawing, owner's part unconfirmed. Shells to TP72 with a short lead at this end only; braid bonded here (CM section 11)
  • [ ] Wire DB-9 A (8 signals + GND) and DB-9 B (UART TX/RX, Filter CV, VCA CV, grounds; no supply, no I²C) to the breakout headers per CM sections 2 and 3. The UART wires are installed here but unused until Phase 6C (audit N17)
  • [ ] Interior cable routing, strain relief

Test Checkpoint

  • ☐ Touch bolts modify sound when touched (verify against Phase 1B results)
  • ☐ DB-9 connectors secure, no pin shorts
  • Gate: touch bolts modify sound, DB-9 signals measure correct

3.X: Phase 2 mod additions

While the MicroBrute case is open, add the 13 Phase 2 mods documented in docs/mods/macrobrute_mod_catalog.md (M02–M14). Recommended sequence (safest → most invasive):

Build group Mods Notes
Safe injects (no PCB cuts) M06 PWM CV, M09 PWM self-mod normalled, M03 sine extract, M11 9th touch bolt, M14 safe bias starve All tap high-Z nodes; only solder leads
Toggles M05 selfosc kill, M07 pitch starve, M10 brute extreme, M13 sync→env, M08 sub-harmonic enable SPDT/SPST in series with existing nets
Breadboard then install M02 active soft sync, M12 ARG audio-rate gate Both use LM393 — bench-test stability before committing
Most invasive M04 metalizer VCA (LM13700), M08 sub-harmonic divider (74HC74) Both need a small stripboard sub-PCB; cuts/inserts in audio path

Per-mod parts list and wiring detail: docs/mods/macrobrute_mod_catalog.md.

Gate: all Phase 2 mods bench-tested, then panel-installed; sound check on every mod; no regressions to Phase 1/3 baseline.

Phase 4: Expander Build (Week 6-10, parallel with Phase 3) UNTESTED REVERSIBLE

Goal: Build the expander: Pico, display and controls, clock I/O, firmware dividers and aux outputs, and the analog utilities (slew limiter, LFO, Sample & Hold); mount in the Eurorack panel and link to the MicroBrute through the 2× DB-9. Width OPEN: 17 HP or about 20 HP. Schematics: schematics/expander_circuits.md, kicad/expander/. STALE: both still describe the old scope (noise, attenuverter, mult, CD4024, 42 HP; audit S58, S59). The decided scope is in CM section 10.

Build Order (easiest → hardest, get sound early)

Order Circuit ICs Test Signal
1 Pico, display, encoder, tap button, RGB LED Pico + 1.3" 7-pin SPI OLED (chip UNVERIFIED; see Phase 0) Firmware runs from the rack +5 V (VSYS via the Schottky OR diode, BF 1.2)

Phase 5: System Integration (Week 10-12) UNTESTED REVERSIBLE

Goal: Full system test — MicroBrute + breakout + Pico + expander, all connected.

Integration Tests

  • ☐ Connect expander via DB-9 shielded cables

  • ☐ Touch bolts: verify all 6 panel bolts still function after permanent install

Ground Loop Audit

  • ☐ Measure DC offset between MB and expander GND
  • ☐ Listen for hum with headphones at max gain
  • ☐ If hum: work the fallback ladder in CM section 11 / BF 4.5 (the old "100 nF in series with the DB-9 GND pin" fix is withdrawn: it removes the DC ground reference, audit S23)
  • ☐ Verify star ground at TP72 and at the expander
  • ☐ The DB-9 ground conductors (A:9; B:2, 4, 7, 8, 9) must be the ONLY ground connection between systems
  • ☐ No USB cable on the Pico while the DB-9 cables are connected; flash and debug with them unplugged (BF 4.3)
  • ☐ Do NOT connect Eurorack chassis ground to MicroBrute chassis
  • ☐ Salvaged isolation transformer available for critical paths if needed

Pico Firmware Polish

  • ☐ Screensaver timeout (120s)
  • ☐ Boot RGB LED test sequence (already in leds.py)
  • ☐ Error handling for disconnected peripherals

Test Checkpoint

  • ☐ No ground loops, hum, or noise
  • ☐ Pico menu fully operational, values persist across reboot

  • Gate: Full system operational, clean audio, no ground hum

Phase 6A: LPC2361 ISP Setup (Week 12+) DRAFT REVERSIBLE

Goal: Physical connection to LPC2361 for firmware development. Status: Firmware RE ~98% complete via .mbf decryption path. ISP is for verification + future custom firmware.

Completed (via .mbf decryption)

  • ☑ Cracked .mbf XOR cipher (key: ArturiaminiBruteFirmware, start index 4)
  • ☑ Extracted Intel HEX → 52.6KB ARM binary (v1.0.4.114)
  • ☑ Ghidra project: 427 functions, 107+ labels, 43 SysEx commands mapped
  • ☑ MIDI dispatcher, DAC pipeline, NRPN protocol, sequencer timing all documented
  • ☑ UART0 (0xE000C000): one reference in the disassembly, inside the UART3 RX error path. The earlier "safe for the Pico bridge" claim is withdrawn (UNVERIFIED): stock MIDI uses UART3 (0xE007C000, init at 0x3D88), UART0 is the ISP port, UART1/UART2 had no literal references (not exhaustive) (audit B01, S06)
  • ☑ 68.6KB free flash available for custom code

Tasks

  • ☐ Solder PL2303HX wires to LPC2361 UART0 pads (P0.2 TX = pin 98, P0.3 RX = pin 99; the "separate pads near the QFP" claim in MACROBRUTE_TEST_POINTS_VERIFIED.md is UNVERIFIED, audit S09). Not pins 96/97: those are VDD(3V3) and VSS
  • ☐ Identify P2.10 (ISP enable) — jumper to GND for bootloader entry
  • ☐ Power cycle with P2.10 LOW, run: lpc21isp -detectonly
  • ☐ Check CRP level (likely CRP3 = locked → use .mbf decryption path instead)
  • Gate: Part ID detected OR CRP status confirmed

Phase 6C: Pico ↔ LPC2361 UART Bridge DRAFT REVERSIBLE

Goal: Bidirectional communication between Pico and MicroBrute CPU.

Tasks

  • ☐ Gate: the Phase 0 continuity check (UART pins 62/63 and 98/99, 6N138 output to pin 85) has passed and is recorded. Only then may the docs say a bridge UART is confirmed
  • ☐ Wire Pico GP0/GP1 → DB-9 B:1 / B:6 with 1 kΩ at each end → LPC2361 UART1: P0.16/RXD1 (pin 63) and P0.15/TXD1 (pin 62), UNVERIFIED until the continuity check. Fall back to the ISP UART (pins 98/99) only if those pins are taken and the ISP conflict is handled
  • ☐ No level shifter and no divider: both ends are 3.3 V (audit S30). Firmware rule: GP0 stays an input until GP1 has read high (BF 3.1). Bench checks BF BT-1 and BT-2; PC817-isolated alternative in BF 3.9
  • ☐ Custom LPC2361 code: init the chosen UART at 115200, accept queries from Pico

Phase 7: Advanced / Optional DRAFT

7A: EFFIGY DSP module pair-up — SHELVED

Owner decision b (2026-10-17): the EFFIGY I²C pairing is shelved as an idea for another project. No rear JST-XH header is fitted, GP2/GP3 are now the main OLED's SCK/MOSI and GP11 the gate input, and nothing is designed around it. docs/MACROBRUTE_EFFIGY_BRIDGE.md, firmware/pico/effigy_bridge.py and tools/sync_effigy_constants.py are archived as they are.

7B: Norns Shield ii bridge (anticipated, not designed)

Three-module chain Norns → MACROBRUTE → EFFIGY (the EFFIGY half is shelved, 7A). MACROBRUTE would host an ii-compatible target on a separate front-of-rack I²C bus (suggested address 0x60). See docs/MACROBRUTE_NORNS_BRIDGE.md — covers translator command split, ii address allocation, pull-up topology, hardware conflict (RP2040 has only 2 HW I²C peripherals — ii target needs PIO-based I²C on spare GPIOs).

7C: Additional touch plates via Pico ADC

  • ☐ Extend the 6 selected panel bolts with Pico ADC (GP26–28) for CV output
  • ☐ CD4051 multiplexed scanning if more than 3 channels needed
  • ☐ PWM → RC filter → CV output (reuses the aux-output PWM machinery)

  • Phase 0: Pico + OLED + encoder all work on breadboard
  • Phase 1: All buffer channels pass signal, gate stage behaves

Pi Pico GPIO Assignment

Superseded. The earlier table here (SPI OLED on GP16-20, CV outputs on GP10-13) predates the firmware and is removed (audit S04). The canonical source is firmware/pico/config.py; the table is mirrored in docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md section 1 and schematics/pico_pinout.md. Free pins: GP26-GP28 only (ADC-capable, not fault tolerant); GP2 and GP3 are the SPI main OLED and GP11 the gate input.

Test Point Signal Board Purpose

Power Distribution

Two independent chains; no supply crosses the DB-9 cable (only ground is shared).

  • Buy 20-50% extra of resistors, capacitors, and diodes — they're cheap and you'll lose some
  • TME has a Lithuanian language interface and excellent EU shipping
  • Combine orders to hit free shipping thresholds (Mouser €50, TME €50)
  • The OLED display is the most critical sourcing item — verify dimensions (75.5 × 19.35 mm PCB) before ordering
  • J-Link EDU Mini is worth it over cheap clones for JTAG work — much better software support
  • Keep the optional items (MCP4725 DAC, PT8211, copper tape) for future expansion

Document Version: 2.0 Project: MACROBRUTE

▶ Phase 0 Starter BOM docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_PHASE0_BOM.md

The minimum kit to validate the Pico-side hardware on a breadboard, without modifying the MicroBrute (the gate checks below only probe it, with no soldering). Wire it per schematics/phase0_breadboard.svg and run firmware/pico/test_hw.py — if every peripheral passes, you're ready for Phase 1.

If anything fails on the bench, fix it here. It will be 10× harder once this is mounted inside the synth.

Subtotal: ~$30 USD (varies by source / shipping), before the Have column: most of this kit is already owned (Pico, OLED, KY-040, resistor kit, jacks).

What you actually need

Qty Part Have? Notes ≈ USD
1 Raspberry Pi Pico Have Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350); nothing here uses wireless. A Pico without soldered headers needs headers soldered for the breadboard. $7
1 1.3″ OLED, SPI, 7-pin (chip SSD1306 or SH1106 and pin order UNVERIFIED: read the module) Have (owner ruling, 2026-10-17, BF Q22) The "main" display, SPI0 write-only: SCK GP2 (D0), MOSI GP3 (D1), DC GP4, RES GP5; the CS lead goes to the GND rail (PROVISIONAL, BT-14); power from the Pico 3V3. GP11 (gate input) is not used in Phase 0. Driver: display.py (OLED_SPI); for SH1106 also OLED_CHIP="SH1106", OLED_COL_OFFSET=2. The 4-pin I²C 1.3″ module is in a TD-3 (not available); the 0.96″ SSD1306 may not have arrived and is an alternative only (I²C would need re-pinning). $4
1 KY-040 rotary encoder module Have 5 pins (CLK, DT, SW, +, GND). On-board 10 kΩ pull-ups. $2
1 Tactile push button, 6 mm Missing (BF Q12) Single-pole momentary. $0.10
1 Common-cathode RGB LED, 5 mm Missing (BF Q12) Used as the status LED. $0.50
3 220 Ω resistor, ¼ W Have (kit; values to confirm, BF Q5) RGB LED current limiters (one per colour). —
2 1 kΩ resistor, ¼ W Have (kit; values to confirm) Clock IN/OUT series resistors for the loop-back test. Not input protection: CLOCK IN is loop-back only, no external signals (no CD4049UB on the bench). —
2 3.5 mm mono panel jacks (or PCB-mount equivalent) Have (25 owned, type unknown, BF Q8) Clock IN + Clock OUT. Bench-only. $1
1 Half-size breadboard (400+ tie points) Not on the owned list Big enough to span the Pico across the centre channel. $4
~30 Solid-core jumper wires, 22 AWG Not on the owned list Mix of M-M and M-F. Pre-cut sets are fine. $4
1 USB cable, micro-B → USB-A or USB-C Not on the owned list Whatever your computer accepts. For Pico flash + power. $2

The 0.91″ strip OLED is dropped and is no longer part of the kit (it stays a spare).

Optional but very helpful:

Qty Part Why
1 Multimeter (continuity + DC voltage) You almost certainly already own one. Critical for verifying jumper paths before powering up.
1 USB-serial adapter (CP2102 / FT232) Lets you watch Pico print() output in a terminal. Not required since the Pico's USB stays available, but nice for parallel debugging once the synth is wired.
1 Caliper (0.1 mm) For the D-sub geometry check below and the later rear-panel measurements.
1 Oscilloscope probe / scope For the TP83 level and the optional 31250-baud check on LPC pin 85. A meter alone gives the DC level of TP83 only.

What you do not need yet

Hold off on these until Phase 1+:

  • Stripboard, IC sockets, TL072 / TL074 / CD40106, BAT85 clamps, vactrol,

10 µF / 100 nF caps, rail-protection diodes — that's the Breakout Board BOM in the full doc.

  • Eurorack panel, M3 hardware, brass touch bolts, panel-mount jacks —

that's Panel Modifications (Phase 3).

  • Eurorack panel (17 HP or about 20 HP, width open), expander parts, ±12 V Eurorack PSU — that's

Expander Build (Phase 4).

  • 5-pin DIN MIDI sockets, 6N138 optocouplers — only matters when you

reach the MIDI Bridge phase.

If you order the full BOM in one go, you'll have a pile of parts you won't touch for weeks. The Phase 0 starter kit is deliberately a weekend's worth of parts.

Bench-validation checklist

After wiring the breadboard per schematics/phase0_breadboard.svg:

  • ☐ Pico powered from USB; on-board green LED is solid.
  • ☐ The main OLED powers up and draws its splash frame (test_hw.py's

OLED test draws through display.OLED_SPI; with CS on the GND rail this is bench check BT-14). If it stays blank, check the module pin order (UNVERIFIED), D0/D1 (SCK/MOSI), DC, RES and CS on GND, then VCC/GND (BF Q22).

  • ☐ Encoder rotation increments / decrements a counter on the OLED.
  • ☐ Encoder push button toggles the on-screen indicator.
  • ☐ Tap button (GP12) registers as a separate input.
  • ☐ RGB LED cycles red / green / blue when each colour is selected.
  • ☐ Looping Clk OUT (GP22) → Clk IN (GP21) with a single 1 kΩ in

series produces clean tick events on the OLED at the firmware's tap-tempo rate.

If all six pass, the breadboard part of Phase 0 is done. Then do the MicroBrute gate checks below before Phase 1 and record each result: they decide what the later phases may assume.

Common Phase 0 gotchas

  • Encoder jitter — the KY-040 module already has 10 kΩ pulls and

on-board caps but firmware also enables Pin.PULL_UP on GP13/14/15. That's intentional and fine. If you still see 2 ticks per detent, add the optional 100 nF + 10 kΩ RC filter shown in pico_pinout.md.

  • No second OLED and no I²C — the strip OLED is dropped and the main OLED is SPI, so there is no address and no I²C scan to run.
  • Common-anode RGB LED instead of common-cathode — they look

identical. With common-anode, "off" is +3.3 V on the GPIO and the LED is always lit until firmware drives the pin high. Verify the part with a multimeter (long lead = K = cathode for common-cathode).

  • Centre-channel jumpers across the Pico body — the Pico straddles

the breadboard centre channel. Jumpers from the encoder / tap to the Pico must route around the Pico, not over it; see the breadboard layout SVG for safe drop columns.

Phase 0 gate checks on the MicroBrute

These are probe-only checks on the open synth (no soldering). Source: audit docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md (decision 7, E-01 to E-05, E-09) and the back-feed and hum design note docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-backfeed-hum-design.md ("BF"). Datasheet pin numbers: docs/DATASHEETS.md. Record every result (a number or "not found") in the build log. Anything not measured stays UNVERIFIED in the docs.

G1. LPC bridge UART continuity (gate before any Phase 6 bridge work)

Rear board CU17002 "Rear Board B3", power off, multimeter in continuity mode. Pin numbers are LPC2361 LQFP-100 (data sheet Rev. 03, Table 3). Never probe pins 96 and 97: they are VDD(3V3) and VSS, not UART pins (the older docs were wrong).

  • ☐ 1. Locate the LPC2361 LQFP-100 (right of the P1_JTAG header) and count from the pin-1 dot.
  • ☐ 2. Probe pin 62 (P0.15 / TXD1) and pin 63 (P0.16 / RXD1) against nearby pads and vias. Record whether each goes to a pad that can take a wire, and whether it also goes to anything else (SPI to a shift register or DAC, an LED driver, a connector). The stock firmware uses SSP0/SPI, which shares these pins.
  • ☐ 3. Same for pin 98 (P0.2 / TXD0) and pin 99 (P0.3 / RXD0), and check the claim of "separate pads near the QFP" in MACROBRUTE_TEST_POINTS_VERIFIED.md (UNVERIFIED, audit S09, E-03). These are the ISP UART.
  • ☐ 4. Trace the 6N138 output (pin 6, 4.7 kΩ pull-up) to the LPC. Expected: pin 85 (P4.29, RXD3), the stock MIDI UART (UART3 per the disassembly; audit E-02).
  • ☐ 5. Optional, synth powered and a MIDI source connected: scope pin 85 for 31250 baud; check pins 62/63 and 98/99 idle at 3.3 V.
  • ☐ 6. Record the result. Only after it passes may a doc say UART1 (or UART0) is confirmed. Until then every doc keeps "UART1, P0.15/P0.16, pins 62/63, UNVERIFIED".

G2. TP83 logic level

  • ☐ Measure the high and the low level of TP83 (gate from the microcontroller, 100 kΩ source impedance, buffer needed): synth on, key pressed and released; scope with a 10× probe preferred (audit E-09, BF BT-5 first part).
  • ☐ Record. If the high level is below 3.6 V, a CD40106 powered from 5 V is not guaranteed to trigger (VT+ at VDD 5 V is 2.2 / 2.9 / 3.6 V min / typ / max, TI SCHS097F p5-p6) and the gate stage must be redesigned: owner question BF Q15. Do not tap the synth's +3V3ARM.

G3. Synth rail drop and current margin (TP70 / TP71)

  • ☐ Read the MicroBrute wall-adapter label (voltage, current, class II symbol; audit E-04, N06) and write it down.
  • ☐ With the synth on and idle, meter TP70 (+12 V) and TP71 (-12 V) against TP72 (GND). Record both. This is the baseline for the Phase 2 loaded check.
  • ☐ The breakout load estimate is about 35 mA typical / 60 mA worst case on +12 V and 15 / 30 mA on -12 V (audit E-04, UNVERIFIED). The Phase 2 acceptance is rails within about 100 mV of the unloaded baseline with no extra ripple on TP70/TP71, measured with the breakout connected, before the DB-9 is wired.
  • ☐ Do not load TP141 (the 5 V precision reference). TP56 "+5VNUM" and P4 pin 5 (+3V3ARM) are not supply taps (audit B09, E-05).

G4. D-sub neighbour geometry (BF BT-7)

  • ☐ Caliper the owner's DB-9 insert (or obtain the exact connector's drawing): pin numbering as moulded on the insert, row offset, flange width and height, hole spacing (the generic drawing says 24.99 mm, Spectrum Control p1), D-body width and height, body depth, solder-cup length, gender.
  • ☐ Confirm or correct the neighbour table in BF 2.1 (top row pins 1-5, bottom row pins 6-9, offset half a pitch: pin 6 between 1 and 2, 7 between 2 and 3, 8 between 3 and 4, 9 between 4 and 5). The DB-9 B map (each CV pin with only ground neighbours) depends on it.
  • ☐ Count the owned DB-9 connectors and note gender (BF Q9; 4 panel connectors are needed in total).

G5. Optional rack checks

  • ☐ CP1A bus slot: meter pins 11-12 for +5 V (BF BT-12, audit E-14). Note: the +5 V pins are 11-12, not 13-14 (pins 13-16 are not used on the CP1A).

Optional alternative: PC817 isolated UART (BF 3.9)

Not part of the decided design and not required in Phase 0. If BT-2 (UART back-feed) fails or the bridge can live at low baud, the owned PC817 (10-20, owner to confirm; photo label x20) can isolate each UART direction. It does not work at 115200 or 38400; 9600 is marginal and 4800 the realistic rate, all UNVERIFIED until BT-13. It also needs an MB-side collector supply (BF Q20). Read the rank mark on the owned part if you try it.

Bench tests BT-1 to BT-13 (names only)

Definitions, pass criteria and what each settles are in BF section 6.2. They run when the matching hardware exists.

ID Name
BT-1 UART edge rate at each receiver pin, real cable, 1k + 1k
BT-2 UART back-feed (each side off in turn, rails and pin current)
BT-3 CV back-feed (both CV outputs at maximum, synth off)
BT-4 CV depth with and without the 100k
BT-5 Gate: TP83 levels, CD40106 output, Pico GPIO node, S2 pin current
BT-6 Cable capacitance (LCR meter)
BT-7 DB-9 insert geometry (caliper) — also G4 above
BT-8 Shell and shield continuity (MB shell to TP72; expander shell to panel and rack 0 V)
BT-9 Hum and gate-to-Pitch crosstalk
BT-10 CD4049UB input clamp behaviour
BT-11 Clock IN overvoltage through the 100k and 4049
BT-12 CP1A bus slot +5 V on pins 11-12 — also G5 above
BT-13 PC817 UART baud and CTR rank (only if the alternative is considered)

Key facts verified from datasheets

(a) LF398 (TI SNOSBI3C, LF398/lf398-n.pdf)

  • PDIP-8 pinout (Pin Functions table, p3): 1 V+, 2 OFFSET ADJUST, 3 INPUT, 4 V-, 5 OUTPUT, 6 Ch (hold capacitor),

7 LOGIC REFERENCE, 8 LOGIC. (TO-99 uses the same numbering. SOIC-14 differs: it is a different pin map, so do not mix the two.) This settles the three conflicting pinouts in the docs: use the list above.

  • Supply: +/-5 V to +/-18 V operating (p1 features); absolute max +/-18 V (p4); +/-15 V nominal.

LF398-N temperature range 0 to 70 C (p4).

  • Logic input: TTL/CMOS compatible; differential logic threshold 0.8 / 1.4 / 2.4 V min/typ/max (p5). Logic

reference to logic differential must stay within the limits in p4 note (4); one logic pin must stay at least a threshold away from the other.

  • Hold capacitor: 0.01 uF is the characterised value (hold step 1 mV typ, 2.5 mV max for LF398-N, p7); acquisition to

0.1 % is 4 us at 1000 pF (10 V step) and 20 us at 0.01 uF (p5-p7). Leakage current into hold capacitor: 30 pA typ, 200 pA max for LF398-N at TJ = 25 C (p7); 100 pA max for LF198/LF298 (p5).

  • Droop: TI states "droop rates as low as 5 mV/min with a 1-uF hold capacitor" (p1). The sheet does not give a

single droop number for 1 nF; the figure follows from leakage (dV/dt = I / C): 30 pA / 1 nF = 30 mV/s typ, 200 pA / 1 nF = 200 mV/s max at 25 C (derived by us from p7, not stated by TI). Droop curve is Figure 4 (p9).

  • Dielectric: p15 section 9.1.1 recommends polystyrene, polypropylene or Teflon for low dielectric absorption;

mica and polycarbonate are called not nearly as good. COG ceramics also noted as low-DA. This confirms the docs' "1 nF ceramic is not for S&H".

  • The same sheet notes stray capacitive coupling of logic to the hold capacitor adds hold step (1 pF with a 5 V logic

swing and 0.01 uF adds 0.5 mV, p5).

(b) LPC2361 (NXP data sheet Rev. 03, LPC2361/lpc2361_62_ds-keil.pdf)

  • Package: LQFP100, 14 x 14 x 1.4 mm, SOT407-1 (p3; package outline p45). Part number LPC2361FBD100.
  • P0.2 / TXD0 = pin 98; P0.3 / RXD0 = pin 99 (Pin description table 3, p5). Alternate functions of P0.2 and P0.3 are

TXD0 and RXD0 only (no further alternates listed).

  • P0.15 / TXD1 / SCK0 / SCK = pin 62; P0.16 / RXD1 / SSEL0 / SSEL = pin 63 (p6). The reviewer is right (62/63).
  • The docs' "97/96" are power pins, not P0.15/P0.16: pin 97 is VSS (ground) and pin 96 is VDD(3V3) (p12).

Any probe or wire landed on 96/97 per the old docs would be on supply or ground.

  • I/O: 5 V tolerant pads with TTL levels and hysteresis (pad notes, p12-p13); input absolute max -0.5 to +6.0 V on

5 V tolerant pins only when VDD(3V3) is present, otherwise VDD(3V3) + 0.5 V (Table 4 limiting values, p33). VDD(3V3) 3.0-3.6 V (p33).

  • Caveat: this is the 2008 Rev. 03 document. NXP lists Rev. 5.1 (Oct 2013) and marks the part not recommended for

new designs; pin numbers above are from the older sheet and should be re-checked against Rev. 5.1 if it can be obtained. UM10211 Rev. 02 (LPC2361/lpc23xx_um_UM10211_rev02-keil.pdf) covers LPC2361/62 (added in this revision).

(c) TL074 / TL072 / CD40106B / CD4049UB / CD4051B

  • TL072, 8-pin PDIP (P package), TI SLOS080W Fig 4-5 p5: 1 1OUT, 2 1IN-, 3 1IN+, 4 VCC-, 5 2IN+, 6 2IN-, 7 2OUT, 8 VCC+.
  • TL074, 14-pin PDIP (N package), Fig 4-8 p8: 1 1OUT, 2 1IN-, 3 1IN+, 4 VCC+, 5 2IN+, 6 2IN-, 7 2OUT, 8 3OUT, 9 3IN-,

10 3IN+, 11 VCC-, 12 4IN+, 13 4IN-, 14 4OUT.

  • TL07x limits (p10-p11): supply abs max 36 V (+/-18 V) for the NS/PS-package and M variants and 42 V for "all other"

(TL07xH) variants; recommended supply 10-30 V (NS/PS/M) or 4.5-40 V (others). The table does not break out PDIP TL07xC separately, so for TL072CP/TL074CN treat +/-12 V operation (24 V total) as within both columns. Input clamp behavior: signal input current limited to +/-10 mA (50 mA for NS/PS/M), common-mode input abs max (VCC-) - 0.5 to (VCC+) + 0.5 V and differential up to VS + 0.2 V for "all other devices" (p10). Recommended input range (VCC-) + 4 V to (VCC+) + 0.1 V for those devices (p11), i.e. about 4 V below the positive rail is the linear limit for the H-class; check the C-class common-mode range in the electrical table before using inputs near the rails. Do not drive inputs beyond the rails.

  • CD40106B, 14-pin (TI SCHS097F p3): 1 A, 2 G (=NOT A), 3 B, 4 H (=NOT B), 5 C, 6 I (=NOT C), 7 VSS, 8 J (=NOT D), 9 D,

10 K (=NOT E), 11 E, 12 L (=NOT F), 13 F, 14 VDD. Supply 3-18 V recommended, abs max 20 V (p4). Inputs: abs max -0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V, +/-10 mA input current (p4): inputs above VDD are not allowed, so drive from a 5 V domain only when VDD >= 5 V or add a series resistor with clamp-current in mind.

  • CD4049UB, 16-pin (TI SCHS046L p3): 1 VCC, 2 G (out of A), 3 A, 4 H (out of B), 5 B, 6 I (out of C), 7 C, 8 VSS,

9 D, 10 J (out of D), 11 E, 12 K (out of E), 13 NC, 14 F, 15 L (out of F), 16 NC. Supply 3-18 V recommended, abs max 20 V VCC to VSS (p5-p6). Input above VCC is explicitly allowed: the description (p1) says the input high level (VIH) can exceed VCC when the device is used for logic-level conversion (high-to-low conversion; max input current 1 uA at 18 V over temperature, p1). The abs max table (p5) lists only +/-10 mA DC input clamp current and gives no separate input voltage limit, so keep the source current-limited (series resistor) and stay under the 18 V input/supply envelope. Note this differs from CD40106B/CD4051B, which have a VDD + 0.5 V input limit.

  • CD4051B, 16-pin (TI SCHS047O p3): 1 Y4, 2 Y6, 3 COM, 4 Y7, 5 Y5, 6 INH, 7 VEE, 8 VSS, 9 C, 10 B, 11 A, 12 Y3, 13 Y0,

14 Y1, 15 Y2, 16 VDD. Supply abs max 20 V (V+ to V-, referenced to VSS), DC input -0.5 to VDD + 0.5 V, +/-10 mA (p5). VEE is the analog negative rail; digital address/INH levels are referenced to VSS and need VDD - VSS adequate for the logic swing (check recommended-supply table in the sheet before using a 5 V VDD with +/-5 V analog).

(d) RP2040 / Pico / Pico W

  • GPIO is not 5 V tolerant. RP2040 datasheet Table 622 (p615): IOVDD abs max 3.63 V and voltage at IO pin abs max

-0.5 V to IOVDD + 0.5 V (about 3.8 V at 3.3 V). The datasheet nowhere states 5 V tolerance. ADC GPIO26-29 additionally have an internal reverse diode to the IOVDD (3V3) rail, so their input voltage must not exceed 3.3 V (Pico datasheet p20).

  • Output drive: selectable 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA (p616-p617, output voltage table). Maximum total current sourced by all GPIO + QSPI pins

is 50 mA; maximum total sunk is 50 mA (p617). No per-pin absolute-maximum figure is given beyond the 12 mA drive setting; treat that as NOT FOUND as a separate per-pin abs max.

  • ESD: 2 kV HBM (p615).
  • Pico (non-W) pin map (Pico datasheet p8): pin 36 = 3V3 (OUT), pin 37 = 3V3_EN, pin 39 = VSYS, pin 40 = VBUS, pin 35 = ADC_VREF,

pin 33 = AGND. 3V3 (pin 36) can power external circuitry; maximum output current depends on RP2040 load and VSYS voltage; the datasheet recommends keeping the load below 300 mA (p9). VSYS: 1.8 V to 5.5 V (p9, p12, Recommended operating conditions table). Pico W gives the same VSYS range and 300 mA guidance (Pico W datasheet p9, p13).

  • VBUS to VSYS goes through an on-board Schottky (D1) so VSYS = VBUS minus the diode drop (Pico datasheet p21); an external

supply into VSYS should be ORed via another Schottky (p22). This confirms the 1N5817 from the 5 V rail into VSYS is a valid arrangement.

(e) BAT85 and 1N5817

  • BAT85 (Philips data sheet 2000-05-25, BAT85/bat85-nxp-mirror-aau.pdf, p2-p3): VR 30 V, IF 200 mA continuous,

IFRM 300 mA, IFSM 5 A (10 ms), Tj 125 C; VF 240 mV at 0.1 mA, 400 mV at 10 mA, 800 mV at 100 mA; IR 2 uA at 25 V; Cd 10 pF; trr 4 ns. Package SOD68 (DO-34 glass axial), not SOT-23. As a BAT54S substitute it is a single diode (BAT54S is a dual series pair in SOT-23: 30 V, 200 mA IO, 300 mA IFRM, VF 400 mV at 10 mA, IR 2 uA at 25 V; Diodes DS11005 p1-p2). It can stand in where only one diode of the pair is used; it is a through-hole part.

  • 1N5817 is a 20 V part, not 40 V: VRRM 20 V (1N5818 = 30 V, 1N5819 = 40 V), IO 1.0 A, IFSM 25 A (Vishay 88525 p1; Diodes

DS23001 p2). Forward voltage at 1 A: 0.450 V max (1N5817), 0.55 V (1N5818), 0.60 V (1N5819) (Diodes p2). The BOM line "1N5817 Schottky diode (40V 1A)" is therefore wrong; a 40 V / 1 A part is the 1N5819. For a 5 V rail 1N5817 is adequate; use 1N5819 only if you want a 40 V rating. The owner's kit inventory (2026-10-17) lists 1N5819 x10; the actual part, its marking and a datasheet for it are UNVERIFIED (not saved under datasheets/; the series figures above come from the 1N5817-series sheet). The BOM's "0.3 V drop" applies at light load only; the Vishay forward-voltage curve (88525 Fig. 3, p2) gives the drop versus current.

(f) Behringer CP1A and Eurorack 16-pin header

  • CP1A (Quick Start Guide, Behringer_CP1A/QSG_BE_0720-ABO_CP1A_WW.pdf, Specifications page p20): two 16-pin (2 x 8, 2.54 mm)

box headers wired in parallel. +5 VDC @ 0.5 A (pins 11, 12); -12 VDC @ 1 A (pins 1, 2); +12 VDC @ 1 A (pins 9, 10); ground pins 3-8. External adapter 13 VDC, 3 A; consumption 35 W max (p20, p12). Pins 13-16 are marked "Not Used" in the pin-out (p15).

  • Pin 1 is -12 V and goes to the red stripe of the cable; the sockets are keyed and the supplied ribbons have tabs matching the gaps

(p15).

  • Doepfer A-100 (Doepfer_A100/a100t_e_technical_details.html and a100b_e.gif): 16-pin module bus connector, 2 x 8, from the lower right corner

of the board upward (each row is a pair of pins): -12 V, GND, GND, GND, +12 V, +5 V, CV, Gate. The 10-pin version, same orientation, is -12 V, GND, GND, GND, +12 V. This matches the CP1A order (pin 1 = -12 V, pins 3-8 = GND, pins 9-10 = +12 V, pins 11-12 = +5 V, pins 13-16 = CV/Gate). Doepfer states the coloured (red) wire of the ribbon marks -12 V and must point to the bottom of the bus board (page text, section on bus boards). Doepfer warns against polarised/boxed headers for A-100 modules (page text). The 16-pin version adds +5 V, CV and Gate. Doepfer PSU current ratings appear in the page text as a list of PSU models, not as a pin spec.

  • CP1A rated currents (+12 V 1 A, -12 V 1 A, +5 V 0.5 A) agree with the retail listing; the CP1A is not a PSU with 5 V at more than 0.5 A, so Pico +

OLEDs through a 1N5817 must stay well under that 0.5 A budget shared with all other +5 V consumers in the rack.

(g) DB-9 mechanical (D-sub shell size 9 / "E" shell)

  • Spectrum Control "Board and Panel Cutouts" (DB9_Dsub/spectrumcontrol_dsub_panel_cutouts.pdf, p1): panel cutout for shell size 9: mounting-hole

centre spacing A = 0.984 in (24.99 mm); cutout width C = 0.777 in (19.74 mm); cutout height E = 0.440 in (11.18 mm); mounting holes 0.125 in (3.18 mm) dia, two holes. Row/contact pitch 0.109 in (2.77 mm); PCB-mount hole spacing 0.984 in (25.00 mm).

  • Winford recommended panel cutout (DB9_Dsub/winford_dsub_panel_cutouts.pdf, p1): DB9: mounting holes 0.98 in apart, 0.125 in dia (2 places), cutout 0.81 x 0.45 in

with R0.15 corners, maximum panel thickness 0.062 in. (Winford and Spectrum cutout width differ: 0.81 vs 0.777 in. Use the larger Winford cutout if the connector's own drawing is unavailable; confirm against the actual connector.)

  • Switchcraft EHDB9 adapter drawing (DB9_Dsub/switchcraft_ehdb9.pdf, p1) for reference: hole spacing 0.945 in (24 mm), cutout 0.748 in (19 mm) wide, flange width about 1.22 in (31 mm)

reference. This is a different (adapter) part: do not use its numbers for a bare DB-9 flange.

  • Flange outer width / height of a bare DB-9 shell (the nominal 30.81 mm / 1.213 in figure): NOT FOUND in the downloaded documents (only an adapter-drawing

reference of about 31 mm); get the specific connector's manufacturer drawing before cutting.

Findings that contradict project docs

  1. 1N5817 is rated 20 V, not 40 V (BOM line 9): see (e).
  2. LPC2361 P0.15/P0.16 are pins 62/63; pins 96/97 are VDD(3V3)/VSS: see (b).
  3. CD40106B inputs may not exceed VDD + 0.5 V (CD4049UB inputs may exceed VCC): see (c).
  4. RP2040 GPIO is not 5 V tolerant (IOVDD + 0.5 V abs max): see (d).
  5. LF398 PDIP-8 pinout is V+ 1, OFFSET 2, IN 3, V- 4, OUT 5, Ch 6, LOGIC REF 7, LOGIC 8: see (a).
