2. DB-9 A and DB-9 B final pin maps

2.1 Neighbour geometry (UNVERIFIED)

Standard D-sub 9 layout, as numbered on the connector insert: top row pins 1-5, bottom row pins 6-9, offset by half a pitch. Pin 6 sits between 1 and 2, 7 between 2 and 3, 8 between 3 and 4, 9 between 4 and 5. Direct neighbours:

Pin 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9
Neighbours 2, 6 1, 3, 6, 7 2, 4, 7, 8 3, 5, 8, 9 4, 9 1, 2, 7 2, 3, 6, 8 3, 4, 7, 9 4, 5, 8

The downloaded D-sub drawings give contact pitch 0.109 in (2.77 mm) and mounting-hole spacing 24.99 mm (Spectrum Control p1) but not the row offset for the owner's part. The geometry stays UNVERIFIED until BT-7 (caliper or the exact connector's drawing). Male and female faces are mirror images; always use the numbers moulded into the insert.

2.2 DB-9 B (Digital + CV, expander to and from MicroBrute)

Rule applied: the UART pair at one end, each high-impedance CV pin surrounded only by ground pins, no CV pin next to a digital pin, grounds interleaved.

Connector face (insert numbering):

   top row     [1 UART TX]-[2 GND]-[3 VCA CV]-[4 GND]-[5 FILTER CV]
   bottom row        [6 UART RX]-[7 GND]-[8 GND]-[9 GND]

Check against the neighbour table: UART TX (1) touches 2 GND and 6 RX; UART RX (6) touches 1 TX, 2 GND, 7 GND. VCA CV (3) touches 2, 4, 7, 8, all ground. Filter CV (5) touches 4 and 9, both ground. No CV touches a digital pin or the other CV. Filter CV, the most sensitive input (summing node, audit H-4), takes pin 5: the corner farthest from the UART.

Why not the alternatives: r5's and r3's maps were built around I2C on the cable, which is now off (audit section 1a c, d). Placing both CVs on 5 and 9 (also "at the far end") would make them neighbours of each other and give pin 9 only two ground neighbours; the 3/5 placement guards each CV on every side.

Pin Signal Direction Series R Protection Wire colour
1 UART TX (Pico GP0 to LPC P0.16 / RXD1, LQFP pin 63) Expander to MB 1k at the Pico (expander board) + 1k at the LPC (MB board) Pico firmware keeps GP0 high-impedance until GP1 reads high (section 3.1). LPC UART choice UNVERIFIED (audit B01). White
2 GND - - Guard; TP72 star and expander star Black
3 VCA CV in (to TP10, per CM) Expander to MB 10k at the expander output + 100k at the MB board BAT85 to +12V_BRK and from -12V_BRK at the node after the 100k; 1 nF to GND Purple
4 GND - - Guard Black
5 Filter CV in (to TP26, per CM) Expander to MB 10k at the expander output + 100k at the MB board As pin 3 Blue
6 UART RX (LPC P0.15 / TXD1, LQFP pin 62, to Pico GP1) MB to expander 1k at the LPC (MB board) + 1k at the Pico (expander board) GP1 is a fault-tolerant RP2040 pin (section 3.1) Yellow
7 GND - - Guard Black
8 GND - - Guard Black
9 GND - - Star return Black

Freed pins: compared with the old CM map (1 TX, 2 RX, 3 SDA, 4 SCL, 5 Filter, 6 VCA, 7 +12 V, 8 -12 V, 9 GND), four pins are freed (the two I2C and the two rail pins). All carry ground. No signal is justified on them: r2's MB_ALIVE sense line is unnecessary because the Pico can see that the LPC is powered from the UART RX idle level (section 3.1), and a ground-sense line is kept only as a fallback-ladder option (section 4.5). Five ground conductors also lower the return impedance for the CV and UART currents.

Series resistors sit on the board side of each connector (soldered at the solder cup or the first board pad), never in the cable (r5 7.2). Both ends get one on the UART so either board survives a cable fault on its own.

Consequences for other documents (Task 5, not done here): the UART moves from B:1/B:2 to B:1/B:6 and the CVs from B:5/B:6 to B:5/B:3. firmware/pico/config.py mentions DB-9 pin numbers only in comments (r5); those comments and the CM tables change together.

2.3 DB-9 A (Outputs, MicroBrute to expander)

A has 8 signals and 1 ground: no pin can be interleaved, only reordered. The order is kept as in CM:76-86. Justification: no reviewer proved a crosstalk or ground problem with it. r5's re-order (N21) was offered as optional with its benefit marked UNVERIFIED by r5 itself; every A line is driven from a low impedance (op-amp follower or stock buffer) through a small series R, so capacitive coupling is expected to be small. The one weak spot is the Gate (pin 1) next to Pitch (2) and VCF (6). The re-order stays an owner option (Q14) to be decided by the BT-9 crosstalk measurement.

Connector face (insert numbering):

   top row     [1 GATE]-[2 PITCH]-[3 ENV]-[4 LFO]-[5 MIX]
   bottom row        [6 VCF]-[7 SAW]-[8 SQUARE]-[9 GND]
Pin Signal (MB source) Direction Series R Protection Wire colour
1 Gate (TP83 via 2x CD40106) MB to expander 1k at the CD40106 output (MB board) Expander: 22k / 33k divider into Pico GP11, a fault-tolerant GPIO (section 3.5; PROVISIONAL (BT-14), CM 12G); gate jack tapped before the divider. Provisional. White
2 Pitch CV (stock rear Pitch buffer) MB to expander 220 ohm at the MB board (new; was "direct") Low-impedance source UNVERIFIED (E-16) Yellow
3 Envelope (TL07x follower) MB to expander 1k after the feedback tap (audit S36, R3-15) - Orange
4 LFO (TL07x follower) MB to expander 1k after the feedback tap Source TP21 meaning UNVERIFIED (E-17) Green
5 VCO Mix (TP30, TL074 follower) MB to expander 1k in, 1k out - Blue
6 VCF out (TP19, TL074 follower) MB to expander 1k in, 1k out - Purple
7 Saw (TP94, TL074 follower) MB to expander 1k in, 1k out Peak level UNVERIFIED (E-19) Red
8 Square (TP93, TL074 follower) MB to expander 1k in, 1k out Peak level UNVERIFIED (E-19) Brown
9 GND - - TP72 star and expander star Black

Expander side of A: lines 2-8 go to panel jacks with no expander IC on them. If any A line is later normalled into an expander circuit (slew, S&H), it enters through at least 100k (section 3.6).

Pitch series value (audit conflict C2: r5 1k vs r3 100-220 ohm): 220 ohm is chosen. The back-feed into an unpowered receiving module is set by that module's own input resistor (typically 100k, UNVERIFIED), so 1k adds no back-feed protection, while it costs about 1 % scale into a 100k input (r3). 220 ohm still isolates the cable capacitance from the stock buffer.

3. Back-feed analysis per cable line

Datasheet limits used:

  • LPC2361 (Rev. 03): standard pins 62, 63, 98, 99 are 5 V tolerant pads (footnote [1], p5-p6, p12). Table 4 (p33) gives -0.5 to +6.0 V for 5 V tolerant pins "only valid when the VDD(3V3) supply voltage is present", and VDD(3V3) + 0.5 V for "other I/O pins". The limit for a 5 V tolerant pin with VDD absent is therefore not specified; this note treats it as at most 0.5 V (the "other I/O pins" figure at VDD = 0). VIH 2.0 V min, VOH VDD - 0.4 V at 4 mA, pull-up current 15-85 uA (Table 5, p34; read for this note). The datasheet gives no injection-current figure for an unpowered pad: the actual current is UNVERIFIED.
  • RP2040: VPIN abs max IOVDD + 0.5 V, and Table 622's scope names both Standard and Fault Tolerant IO (Table 622, p615); VIH 2.0 V at IOVDD 3.3 V, pull-up and pull-down 50-80 kohm, input leakage 1 uA (Table 625, p616-p617; read for this note). GPIO0-22 are "Digital IO (FT)": "very little current flows into the pin whilst it is below 3.63 V and IOVDD is 0 V" (Table 614, p613; read for this note); their reset state is pull-down (Table 615, p613-p614). GPIO26-29 are not FT and have a diode to IOVDD (Pico datasheet p20). The two statements conflict for an unpowered chip: any voltage above 0.5 V on a pin of an unpowered RP2040 exceeds the Table 622 absolute maximum, and only the Table 614 FT sentence says it is tolerated. Every S2 case below where a pin of the unpowered RP2040 sits above 0.5 V is therefore labelled "exceeds Table 622 abs max, relies on Table 614 FT, provisional", and BT-2 / BT-5 measure the pin current, not only the rail.
  • CD4049UB: TI SCHS046L contradicts itself: p1 says VIH can exceed VCC; section 8.2.2 (p17) says inputs have clamp diodes to VCC and must stay below VCC (read for this note). This note treats the input as clamped to VCC.
  • CD40106B: inputs -0.5 to VDD + 0.5 V, +/-10 mA (p4); VT+ at VDD 5 V 2.2 / 2.9 / 3.6 V min / typ / max (p5-p6; read for this note).
  • BAT85: VF 240 mV at 0.1 mA, 400 mV at 10 mA (p2-p3).
  • TL07x: input current limit +/-10 mA, inputs must stay within the rails (TI SLOS080W p10).

Decision on audit conflict C2 (one table): UART 1k at both ends (r5) rather than r2's 4.7k or r3's 1-2.2k at the Pico end only. CV: 10k at the expander (r5) plus 100k on the MB side (r2 and r3's "100k or more", replacing r5's 1k). Gate: 1k at the source (r3) and a divider on the expander (this note, section 3.5). Reasons are in each subsection.

3.1 UART TX (B:1, Pico GP0 to LPC RXD1) and UART RX (B:6, LPC TXD1 to Pico GP1)

State UART TX (Pico drives) UART RX (LPC drives)
S0 No source. No source.
S1 (expander on, synth off) Risk: Pico TX idles high (3.3 V) into an LPC pin treated as rated to 0.5 V when unpowered (p33, see above). Fix: firmware rule, GP0 stays an input (high-impedance, reset pull-down) until GP1 has read high; with the LPC off, GP1 is pulled low by its own pull-down, so GP0 never drives. Backstop if firmware fails: 2k total limits any current to below (3.3 - 0.6) / 2k = 1.35 mA, assuming a clamp to VDD exists (UNVERIFIED; the datasheet does not say). LPC unpowered: no source. GP1 reads low (pull-down).
S2 (synth on, expander off) Pico off, so no Pico source. The LPC's P0.16 (RXD1) pin, if left with its reset pull-up under stock firmware (15-85 uA, p34; reset default UNVERIFIED), pulls the line toward 3.3 V into the unpowered GP0 through 2k. The current is bounded by the pull-up (at most 85 uA) and GP0 is FT; the pin voltage can still exceed 0.5 V: exceeds Table 622 abs max, relies on Table 614 FT, provisional. LPC TX (bridge firmware, Phase 6) idles high, or the LPC pin pull-up (15-85 uA, p34) under stock firmware, into unpowered GP1. Exceeds Table 622 abs max (pin up to 3.3 V vs 0.5 V), relies on Table 614 FT ("very little current" below 3.63 V with IOVDD = 0, p613), provisional. LPC VOH cannot exceed VDD 3.3 V. Backstop: 2k limits a worst-case clamp current to below 1.35 mA. BT-2 measures the pin current.
S3 Normal. If the LPC starts second, GP1 goes high, and only then does the Pico enable GP0 as UART TX. Normal. GP1's pull-down to the LPC's 4 mA push-pull high gives a clean high through 2k.

Firmware rule (to add in a later firmware task; no firmware change here): GP0 stays an input until the bridge is enabled and GP1 has read high continuously for a debounce time (value is a firmware choice); it returns to input when GP1 stays low (LPC powered off). Caution: a UART break sent by the LPC (line held low for longer than a character) looks the same as "LPC off" and would trip this rule. The "stays low" timeout must be longer than any break the bridge protocol uses, or the bridge protocol must not use breaks. Until the Phase 6 bridge firmware exists, the UART lines are wired but unused (audit N17), so GP0 never drives.

Value justification (1k + 1k = 2k per line):

  • Edge rate: bit time at 115200 baud is 8.68 us. Cable capacitance is UNVERIFIED (E-13); the audit's working figure is about 150 pF for 1 m plus pins. RC = 2k x 150 pF = 0.30 us; 10-90 % rise = 2.2 RC = 0.66 us, 7.6 % of a bit, inside the BT-1 pass criterion of 0.9 us (about 10 % of a bit). At 300 pF (about 3 m at 100 pF/m) it is 1.32 us, which fails BT-1; for such a cable either shorten it or lower the resistors to 680 ohm at each end (1.36k x 300 pF x 2.2 = 0.90 us) and repeat BT-2, since a lower R raises any back-feed current. r2's 4.7k at one end gives 1.55 us at 150 pF, already outside BT-1.
  • Drive current: peak charging current at most 3.3 V / 2k = 1.65 mA, inside the 4 mA rating of both drivers (LPC p34, RP2040 default 4 mA drive). DC load is only receiver leakage (3 uA LPC, 1 uA RP2040), so the high level at the receiver stays at the driver's VOH, above both VIH = 2.0 V figures.
  • Fault: a cable conductor shorted to ground limits each driver to 3.3 V / 1k = 3.3 mA.
  • Back-feed: with the firmware rule and the FT receiver, the series R is a backstop, not the primary protection. BT-2 sets the acceptance: the unpowered side's 3V3 rail below about 0.3 V.
  • No divider, no level shifter: both ends are 3.3 V and LPC VIH is 2.0 V (p34); the old "1k + 2k divider OR CD4049" note is deleted (audit S30).

3.2 Why no MB_ALIVE line

The UART RX line already tells the Pico whether the LPC is powered (GP1 high with the bridge firmware running, low otherwise). A separate sense line would need a GPIO and a freed pin and would itself cross the cable. With the stock firmware the LPC pull-up versus the RP2040 pull-down gives an undefined level, which is harmless because GP0 is not used before the bridge firmware.

3.3 Filter CV (B:5) and VCA CV (B:3), expander to MicroBrute

Circuit per line: expander driver (op-amp output, up to about 10 V; source circuit not yet chosen) -> 10k on the expander board -> cable -> 100k on the MB board -> clamp node: BAT85 anode to node, cathode to +12V_BRK; BAT85 anode to -12V_BRK, cathode to node; 1 nF (owned) to GND -> existing injection point (TP26 for Filter CV, TP10 for VCA CV, per CM; whether the stock 220k / 100k resistors sit after these points is UNVERIFIED, E-18).

State Current path and size
S0 No source.
S1 Expander CV (up to 10 V) through 110k into the upper BAT85 and the unpowered +12V_BRK rail: at most (10 - 0.24) / 110k = 89 uA (BAT85 VF at 0.1 mA, p2-p3). Negative CV mirrors into -12V_BRK. The same 110k bounds any current into the synth's own injection path.
S2 The MB node (TP26 / TP10 voltage UNVERIFIED) through 110k into the unpowered expander op-amp output: under 0.11 mA for any node voltage within +/-12 V.
S3 Normal. Clamps conduct only for a fault above the breakout rails.

Deviation from the plan's back-feed rule: for the CV lines the rule ("no current can flow into an unpowered IC's input protection diodes") is reduced, not met. In S1 up to 89 uA still flows into the unpowered +12V_BRK (or -12V_BRK) rail, and the same 110k path feeds the synth's own injection path (TP26 through the stock 220k, and TP10) while the synth is off. CV back-feed is bounded, not zero: the design limits the current; it does not remove it. Acceptance is BT-3 (unpowered rails below about 0.3 V). Owner option (Q19): a firmware mute that holds both CV outputs at 0 V until the Pico sees the synth powered (GP1 high, section 3.1) would make the S1 current zero in normal use; it needs a firmware change and the CV source circuit to support a defined 0 V output.

Why these values: with r5's 1k on the MB side, the S1 current is about (10 - 0.24) / 11k = 0.89 mA, which r2 and r3 warn can partly power the breakout op-amps. 100k cuts it by ten. The 10k at the expander isolates the op-amp output from the cable capacitance and limits a cable short to about 1 mA. Cost: the extra 100k reduces the CV depth if the synth's own 220k / 100k is in series after the injection point (to about 0.69 for Filter and 0.5 for VCA in that case; UNVERIFIED until E-18 and BT-4). If the depth is too small, reduce the MB-side resistor to 47k (S1 current about 0.17 mA) and repeat BT-3. The 1 nF with 100k gives a 0.1 ms time constant (about 1.6 kHz corner), which removes edge pickup without slowing control-rate CV; r3's 10 nF is not owned and would cut the corner to about 160 Hz.

Rail-diode note: whether the injected S1 current stays on the breakout rails or reaches the synth's TP70 / TP71 depends on audit conflict C12 (series diode or series resistor on the breakout rails). BT-3 measures both.

3.4 Gate A:1 on the MicroBrute side and the 5 V supply

Provisional (audit recommendation, owner has not confirmed):

  • TP83 -> 10k series -> CD40106 pin 1, 1 nF (owned) from pin 1 to GND, no pull-up (audit B14). CD40106 pins 2 -> 3, pin 4 -> 1k -> A:1, so A:1 follows TP83 polarity (audit S33). Unused CD40106 inputs (5, 9, 11, 13) tied to GND (audit S34).
  • The breakout needs 5 V only for this CD40106 (the strip OLED is dropped). Supply: owned 78L05 from +12V_BRK (dropout 1.7 V typ, TI SLVS010X device tables; quiescent current 3.8 mA, p1). Dissipation about (11.7 - 5) V x 4 mA = 27 mW.
  • Open condition: the CD40106 at VDD 5 V needs TP83 above VT+ (3.6 V max, p5-p6). If TP83 is 3.3 V logic (E-09 UNVERIFIED), triggering is not guaranteed and this stage must be redesigned (Q15); do not tap the synth's +3V3ARM (audit B09).

3.5 Gate A:1 into the Pico: no 5 V net reaches a GPIO

Provisional (audit recommendation, owner has not confirmed), with one justified change: the audit recommends a CD4049UBE on Pico 3V3 as the level shifter. Because the CD4049UB datasheet itself says its inputs have clamp diodes to VCC (p17), a 5 V input to a 3.3 V-powered 4049 would push current into the Pico 3V3 rail, and in S2 into the unpowered rail. A resistive divider into a fault-tolerant RP2040 GPIO avoids both:

A:1 -> (gate panel jack tapped here) -> 22k -> node -> 33k to GND; node -> Pico GP11 (FT; GATE_IN in config.py). DECIDED-PROVISIONAL (owner ruling, 2026-10-17): the OLED CS pin is tied to GND to free GP11; PROVISIONAL until BT-14 (section 5).

  • High level: 5 V x 33k / (1k + 22k + 33k) = 2.95 V at a 5.0 V CD40106 supply; above RP2040 VIH 2.0 V and below 3.63 V (FT limit) and IOVDD + 0.5 V = 3.8 V. The 78L05 output tolerance was not read for this note; a +/-5 % supply would give 2.80-3.09 V (UNVERIFIED margin, BT-5).
  • No 5 V net touches a GPIO: the highest node voltage is the divided value. The validator rule (plan Task 8) sees a DIV endpoint.
State Current path
S0 None.
S1 Cable side is the unpowered CD40106 output; the 33k pulls the node low; no expander-side pull-up exists (r2: keep every gate pull-up on the MB side), so nothing flows toward the synth. GPIO reads gate off.
S2 CD40106 high into an unpowered FT pin: Thevenin source 2.95 V through 13.6k. Exceeds Table 622 abs max (2.95 V vs 0.5 V on an unpowered RP2040), relies on Table 614 FT ("very little current", p613), provisional. Worst case if it behaved like a clamp: (2.95 - 0.6) / 13.6k = 0.17 mA. BT-5 measures the pin current.
S3 Normal. Edge: 13.6k into the pin capacitance (a few pF) is far faster than any gate.

3.6 A outputs (A:2 to A:8)

State Current path
S0 None.
S1 MB followers unpowered. Expander jacks are passive, so the expander drives nothing into the MB. A rack module output wrongly patched into an expander output jack would drive the MB follower output through 1k; this is misuse, not a design path.
S2 MB followers (about +/-5 V typical, peaks UNVERIFIED E-19) through 1k (220 ohm on pitch) into whatever rack input is patched, which is unpowered: limited by that module's input resistor (typically 100k, UNVERIFIED) to about 0.1 mA. No expander IC is on these lines. If an A line is normalled into an expander circuit, use at least 100k at that input so S2 current is at most about 0.1 mA, far below the TL07x 10 mA input limit (p10).
S3 Normal.

3.7 Clock jacks on the expander

Both clock jacks and the Pico are in the rack domain; no clock wire crosses to the synth (audit N08). The synth states do not apply; the relevant extra state is the Pico on USB with the rack off.

  • Clock IN: jack -> 100k pull-down to GND at the jack -> 100k series -> CD4049UB section (VCC = Pico 3V3) -> second section -> GP21 (r3, audit S46). A +10 V input pushes at most (10 - 3.3 - 0.6) / 100k = 61 uA into the 4049's VCC clamp, which the powered 3V3 rail absorbs; a -10 V input pushes 94 uA through the VSS clamp, far under the +/-10 mA DC clamp rating (p5). The RP2040 pin only ever sees the 4049 output (0-3.3 V). With the Pico on USB and the rack off, the source module is off.
  • Clock OUT: GP22 -> CD4049UB section -> second section -> 1k -> jack. The buffer takes any mis-patch fault instead of the RP2040, whose per-pin injection limit is NOT FOUND in the datasheet (DATASHEETS (d)). Whether the 4049 output tolerates a mis-patched +/-10 V through 1k (about 6 mA) is UNVERIFIED (Q16). With the rack off and the Pico on USB, the output drives an unpowered rack input through 1k plus that input's own resistor.
  • These four sections use one of the three owned CD4049UBE packages.

3.8 Per-line summary (for the connection map and the Task 8 validator)

Line Source Destination Series R Protection Powered-side assumption
B:1 UART TX Pico GP0 LPC P0.16 RXD1 (pin 63) 1k expander + 1k MB Firmware: GP0 high-Z until GP1 high Pico never drives into an unpowered LPC
B:6 UART RX LPC P0.15 TXD1 (pin 62) Pico GP1 1k MB + 1k expander GP1 fault tolerant; pull-down LPC may drive while Pico is off: exceeds Table 622 abs max, relies on Table 614 FT, provisional (BT-2)
B:5 Filter CV Expander op-amp TP26 10k expander + 100k MB 2x BAT85 to +/-12V_BRK, 1 nF Either side may be off
B:3 VCA CV Expander op-amp TP10 10k expander + 100k MB 2x BAT85 to +/-12V_BRK, 1 nF Either side may be off

A:2 Pitch Stock pitch buffer Jack 220 ohm MB - -
A:3-A:8 MB followers Jacks 1k MB >= 100k into any expander circuit Synth may drive while rack is off
Clock IN Rack jack GP21 100k 2x CD4049UB on 3V3, 100k pull-down Rack domain only
Clock OUT GP22 Rack jack 1k 2x CD4049UB on 3V3 Rack domain only

3.9 Alternative: PC817-isolated UART (documented option, not the decided design)

The decided UART (3.1) stays as written; it is provisional because it relies on the RP2040 FT sentence and on an unpowered LPC pad. This section evaluates the owned PC817 (10-20 owned, owner to confirm) as a replacement for both UART directions. Datasheet: Sharp PC817X Series, sheet D2-A03101EN (datasheets/PC817/73758.pdf, read for this note); a second Sharp sheet (OP18002EN, PC817XxNSZ1B) gives the same IC, fc, tr and tf rows (its cover page states CTR 50-400 % instead of 50-600 %). The owned parts come from an assortment: maker, CTR rank mark and whether they meet the Sharp figures are UNVERIFIED.

Datasheet figures used (Ta = 25 C):

  • LED: IF abs max 50 mA, VR abs max 6 V (p4); VF 1.2 V typ, 1.4 V max at IF 20 mA (p4); about 1.1 V at 3-5 mA (Fig. 7, p7, typical curve, reference only).
  • CTR: IC 2.5-30 mA at IF 5 mA, VCE 5 V, i.e. CTR 50-600 % (p4); ranks A-D from 4-8 mA up to 15-30 mA (p5). No minimum is given at any other IF; "while operating at IF < 1.0 mA, CTR variation may increase" and IRED output degrades by about 50 % over 5 years (p9).
  • Speed: fc 80 kHz typ at VCE 5 V, IC 2 mA, RL 100 ohm (p4); tr 4 us typ / 18 us max, tf 3 us typ / 18 us max at VCE 2 V, IC 2 mA, RL 100 ohm (p4). Fig. 13 (p8, "for reference and not for guarantee") shows tr and tf rising with load resistance: about 20 us each at RL 1k and about 50-75 us at 10k; read at RL 4.7k by log interpolation, about 40-50 us. Fig. 15 (p8) puts the -3 dB point near 20-30 kHz at RL 1k and a few kHz at 10k (reference only).
  • Dark current ICEO at most 100 nA at VCE 50 V (p4).
  • Drivers: LPC2361 IOH / IOL 4 mA at VOH = VDD - 0.4 V / VOL = 0.4 V, VIL 0.8 V (Table 5, p34). RP2040 VOL at most 0.5 V and VOH at least 2.62 V at the selected 2 / 4 / 8 / 12 mA drive, VIL 0.8 V, total IOVDD current 50 mA (Table 625, p616-p617).

Topology (chosen so that polarity is kept, no supply crosses the cable and the B map does not change):

  • One PC817 per direction, at the receiver end. The driver GPIO drives the LED directly: driver TX pin -> 560 ohm on the driver board -> cable -> PC817 LED anode on the receiver board; LED cathode to the receiver board's ground star, returning over the shared cable grounds.
  • Output as an emitter follower: collector to the receiver's own supply, emitter to the receiver's RX pin with 4.7k to the receiver's ground. LED on (TX high, the idle state) gives RX high, so the UART is not inverted.
  • B:1 carries the Pico-to-LPC LED drive, B:6 the LPC-to-Pico LED drive. The ground pins stay as in 2.2. The 1k series resistors of 3.1 are not used (the 560 ohm takes their place); a cable short to ground draws at most about 3.9 mA from the driver.

LED current (the driver sources it, TX high = LED on): IF = (VOH - 1.1) / 560. LPC: VOH at least 2.9 V (p34) gives at least 3.2 mA. RP2040: VOH at least 2.62 V at the 4 mA setting (p617) gives at least 2.7 mA. Either way at most (3.3 - 1.1) / 560 = 3.9 mA, within the 4 mA figure of both drivers. Because UART idle is high, each LED is lit whenever its driver is idle, so each side spends about 3-4 mA continuously while the bridge runs, and the LEDs age faster than with a short duty cycle (p9).

Output level: high needs IC x 4.7k above VIH 2.0 V, i.e. IC at least 0.43 mA; the follower then saturates near the receiver supply. Assuming CTR at least 50 % at IF 2.7 mA (UNVERIFIED: the minimum is only specified at 5 mA, though the typical CTR curve, Fig. 6 p6, is higher at 3 mA than at 5 mA), IC is at least 1.35 mA new and 0.68 mA after the 50 % degradation (p9): margin about 1.6x. Low is dark current only (100 nA x 4.7k = 0.5 mV). A 1k load would need IC 2 mA for VIH, i.e. CTR about 75 % new and 150 % after degradation at IF 2.7 mA, which only rank B or higher would cover (rank figures are at 5 mA, p5; owned rank UNVERIFIED). 4.7k is therefore the load that works on the guaranteed figures.

Maximum baud: working criterion (this note, not a datasheet rule): each edge at most about 25 % of a bit, so the receiver's mid-bit sample sees a settled level.

  • 115200 (bit 8.68 us): does not work. Even at RL 100 ohm, which this circuit cannot use, tr and tf are up to 18 us (p4), longer than two bits.
  • 38400 (bit 26 us): does not work. Edges of about 20 us at 1k and 40-50 us at 4.7k (Fig. 13) are as long as or longer than a bit.
  • 19200 (bit 52 us): not expected with the 4.7k load (edges near a whole bit); possibly with a 1k load and a rank B-D part (edges about 40 % of a bit): UNVERIFIED.
  • 9600 (bit 104 us): marginal with 4.7k (edges about 40-50 % of a bit): UNVERIFIED, bench check BT-13.
  • 4800 (bit 208 us): expected to work with 4.7k (edges about 25 % of a bit), on reference curves only: UNVERIFIED until BT-13.

The Fig. 13 curves are for VCE 2 V and IC 2 mA in the linear region; in this circuit the transistor saturates at about 0.7 mA, where turn-off can be slower. All baud figures above are UNVERIFIED until BT-13 is done on the owned parts.

Back-feed, per power state: S1 (synth off): GP0 drives the Pico-to-LPC LED, which sits on the MB board and returns to ground; no IC pin is on that path. The unpowered LPC RX pin sees the phototransistor emitter with the collector on the unpowered MB supply, so there is no source on the LPC side. The LPC-driven line (B:6) connects only to the unpowered LPC pin through 560 ohm and the LED, which the Pico side does not drive. S2 (Pico off): the mirror image. No GPIO of an unpowered chip is driven above 0 V by the other system in any state, so the Table 622 / Table 614 conflict (3.1) and the unpowered LPC pad limit (Table 4, p33) no longer apply to the UART. The firmware rule of 3.1 is no longer needed for protection, but GP1 still reads low when the LPC is off, so it can stay as the "LPC alive" sense (with the same UART-break caution).

What each side's supply must provide:

  • Pico side: 3-4 mA from GP0 for the TX LED (sourced through IOVDD, inside the 50 mA total), and at most 3.3 V / 4.7k = 0.7 mA through the RX phototransistor from Pico 3V3.
  • MB side: 3-4 mA from the LPC TXD1 pin for the RX LED (from the LPC's own supply through its pin), and a collector supply for the TX phototransistor, at most 0.7 mA. The MB board has no 3.3 V rail of its own. Options: (a) a resistor tap on the synth's +3V3ARM, which audit B09 rejects for the gate stage and the owner would have to accept here; (b) the Provisional 78L05 (5 V): RXD1 (pin 63) is a 5 V tolerant pad, but -0.5 to +6.0 V is "only valid when VDD(3V3) is present" (Table 4, p33), so it depends on the 78L05 not coming up before the LPC's 3.3 V (sequencing UNVERIFIED); (c) common-emitter output with the LPC's internal pull-up (15-85 uA, p34) and no rail, which inverts the signal and is far too slow (about 40-220k equivalent). None is free of a new owner decision (Q20).

Ground: in this topology the LED currents return over the shared cable grounds, so the UART does not break any ground path. Full galvanic isolation of the UART would need each LED's return on its own conductor (2 more pins). On DB-9 B that leaves 3 ground pins for 2 CVs; by the neighbour table (2.1) pin 5 is the only CV position with only-ground neighbours, so the second CV would have to sit next to a UART return. And the synth and rack grounds stay joined by A:9 and the remaining B grounds, which the CV, gate and audio lines need, so isolating the UART alone gives no hum benefit (4.1). Not recommended.

Consequences for the DB-9 B map: none in the recommended topology (B:1 and B:6 change from logic lines to LED drive lines, about 3-4 mA DC while idle instead of near zero). Parts: 2x PC817, 2x 560 ohm, 2x 4.7k, all owned (resistor values Q5).

Verdict: the PC817 UART removes UART back-feed in every power state and needs only owned parts, but it does not work at 115200 or 38400; 9600 is marginal and 4800 is the realistic rate, both UNVERIFIED until BT-13. It costs an MB-side collector supply (Q20). It is worth taking only if BT-2 fails or the bridge can live with 4800-9600 baud.

4. Hum design

4.1 Ground topology

  • Exactly one ground connection between the synth and the rack: the cable ground conductors (A:9; B:2, B:4, B:7, B:8, B:9), six conductors in two cables, all running between the same two star points. Strictly they form small loops (between the conductors inside each cable, and between the two cables); keeping both cables bundled and short keeps that loop area small, so they are not expected to pick up mains hum the way a second, separately routed ground would (r5 F-05). Measured by BT-9.
  • MicroBrute side: every cable ground pin and the breakout ground go by their own short wires to the TP72 star (TPV:27), not through the breakout's ground strip (audit N13). The breakout takes power only from TP70 / TP71 / TP72.
  • Expander side: every cable ground pin, the Pico GND and all expander circuit grounds meet at one star point where the rack 0 V enters at the 16-pin header.
  • No other synth-to-rack path: no separate clock cable (audit N08), no chassis or panel bond between the two cases, and the USB rule below.
  • The earth status of the two adapters (class II or not) is UNVERIFIED (audit N06); if either is earthed, mains earth is part of any loop.
  • Outside this design: both systems' audio outputs going to the same mixer or interface form a loop through the audio cables (r2). The cable design cannot cut that loop; the ladder in 4.5 handles it.

4.2 Shield termination (resolves audit conflict C8)

Rule: each cable's braid is bonded to its connector shell at the MicroBrute end only, and that MB-side panel connector shell is wired with a short lead to TP72. At the expander end the braid is cut back and insulated inside the hood, and the expander panel connector's shell is isolated from the aluminium panel with insulating shoulder washers (Missing, Q10). The shield never carries signal return; returns stay on the ground pins.

Why the MicroBrute end: it matches the existing CM rule and two of the three reviewers (r3, r5; r2 preferred the expander end). The shield then drains into TP72, the node where every cable return already meets, instead of into the expander panel and rack rails, whose bond to rack 0 V is unknown. The MB rear panel appears to be plastic (r5, IMG_6973; UNVERIFIED), so the MB shell does not touch another ground. A molded off-the-shelf cable bonds the braid at both hoods (r2 P-D3, r5 F-06): it must be modified or built. Shell-to-panel continuity on both ends is checked in BT-8 (E-15). If the owner rejects washers, the fallback is r2's rule (bond at the expander end, cut at the MB end), tried in ladder step 3.

4.3 USB ground

Rule: no USB cable on the Pico while the expander is rack-powered and the DB-9 cables are connected. Flash and debug the Pico with the DB-9 cables unplugged. Reason: the Pico micro-USB ties expander ground to the computer, and the MicroBrute's own USB to the same computer then closes a loop through the cable ground (audit S25). No USB isolator is owned. USB and rack 5 V at the same time is electrically safe for the Pico (on-board VBUS Schottky, Pico datasheet p21-p22); the rule is about hum only. Consequence: runtime USB-MIDI from the Pico (CM:67-70) cannot be used with the cables connected without an isolator (Q17).

4.4 Pin interleaving

DB-9 B: the UART pair sits at the pin-1 end; each CV pin has only ground neighbours (section 2.2). DB-9 A: no free pin; order kept (section 2.3). Both cables are run together and kept short to keep the loop area between the two cable grounds small. Maximum cable length: 1 m working figure (audit S38, r3), UNVERIFIED until BT-6 measures the cable capacitance and BT-1 the UART edges.

4.5 Fallback ladder (owned parts only, in order of cost)

Do each step only if hum or noise is still measured after the previous one (BT-9). The "100 nF in series with the ground pin" fix in the current docs is wrong (it removes the DC ground reference for CV, gate and UART; audit S23) and is not part of this ladder.

  1. No parts: confirm the baseline. USB unplugged (4.3); no clock cable; cables bundled and short; both adapters on the same mains strip; measure with each cable unplugged in turn to locate the loop.
  2. No parts: re-wire any ground that does not go to its star by its own lead (4.1); confirm no case-to-case contact.
  3. No parts: swap the shield bond to the expander end (r2's rule) and compare; keep whichever measures lower. In the swapped arrangement the braid is bonded at the expander hood; because the expander panel shell is isolated by the washers (4.2), wire that expander shell with a short lead to the expander star (rack 0 V); cut the braid back and insulate it inside the MB-end hood, and leave the MB shell's lead to TP72 in place or remove it (compare both).
  4. Owned resistor kit plus two BAT85 (conditional): on the expander, break the ground bundle from the expander star with 10 ohm, bypassed by 100 nF (owned) in parallel and two anti-parallel BAT85 so fault current has a path. This keeps the DC reference (r2 step 4, r3 H-1). Condition: all 10 owned BAT85 are already allocated (section 1.2), so this step can only be built from BAT85 if two are freed by taking the series-resistor option on the breakout rails (audit C12, Q3). Since the owner's kit has 1N4148 (25+) and 1N5819 (x10), the anti-parallel pair can instead be two owned 1N4148 or 1N5819 (provisional; the forward voltage differs from BAT85, so the checks below matter more). Without the diodes, 10 ohm in parallel with 100 nF still keeps the DC reference, but a fault current between the systems then has only the 10 ohm path (it would burn the resistor): flagged, not recommended. Recheck BT-2, BT-3 and BT-5 afterwards: the gate, CV and UART references now ride on up to the BAT85 forward voltage.
  5. Owned op-amps (TL072) and resistors: dedicate one B ground pin (for example B:8) as a no-current ground-sense wire from TP72 and use it as the reference of difference-amplifier receivers on the expander's audio inputs (r2 step 3). Needs matched resistors (1 % parts are not owned, Q5).
  6. Owned isolation transformer on the single worst audio line only, after its characterisation (E-29). It passes no DC, so never on CV, gate or UART (r2, r3).

5. GPIO note

With I2C off the cable and EFFIGY shelved, GP2, GP3 and GP11 were free when this note was written. Update (owner rulings, 2026-10-17): GP2 and GP3 are now the SPI main OLED's SCK and MOSI, and GP11 is the gate input (OLED CS tied to GND), so only these Pico pins are free:

GPIO Physical pin Type (RP2040 datasheet) Note
GP26 31 Digital IO / ADC0, not FT, diode to IOVDD (Pico p20) PWM slice 5A is shared with GP10 (LED_MODE) (audit S02).
GP27 32 Digital IO / ADC1, not FT -
GP28 34 Digital IO / ADC2, not FT -

Rule: any input that can see a signal from the cable or a jack while the Pico may be unpowered goes on an FT pin (GP0-22), not on GP26-28.

Gate input pin: DECIDED-PROVISIONAL (owner said "whichever is better"; ruling 2026-10-17). The OLED module's CS pin is strapped permanently to GND (single device on the SPI bus, common practice), which frees GP11 (fault tolerant) for the gate mirror of A:1 (section 3.5; GATE_IN = 11, direction IN). The module's behaviour with CS tied low is UNVERIFIED: bench check BT-14. Fallback if BT-14 fails: CS back on a GPIO, and the gate input on GP27 or GP28, either accepting the S2 clamp current (about 0.17 mA worst case by the section 3.5 arithmetic, (2.95 - 0.6) V / 13.6k; check with BT-5) or behind a series diode or a 3V3-powered buffer.

ID Check Pass criterion Settles
BT-1 Scope the UART edge at each receiver pin with the real cable and 1k + 1k. 10-90 % rise at most 0.9 us (about 10 % of a bit at 115200). UART series R, cable length
BT-2 UART back-feed: S1 with the Pico running, measure LPC +3V3ARM (P4 pin 5) and the B:1 pin; S2 with the LPC bridge firmware idling (and again with stock firmware), measure Pico 3V3 (pin 36), the GP1 and GP0 pin voltages, and the pin current: the voltage across the receiver-end 1k (1 mV = 1 uA), or a uA meter in series with the pin. Unpowered rail below about 0.3 V and pin current in the "very little" range (record it; propose under 10 uA as the working limit, UNVERIFIED since the datasheet gives no number). If not, raise the receiver-end resistor to 2.2k and repeat BT-1, or take the PC817 alternative (3.9). RP2040 FT behaviour, LPC unpowered pad (E-11)

▶ project audit docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-16-project-audit.md

Date: 2026-10-16 Branch: project-review-diagram-redesign Method: five independent read-only reviews (r1 to r5) plus the doc-vs-firmware checker run on the real docs, merged here. Nothing was changed by the reviewers. Nothing is built yet; docs and firmware are design-stage.

1. Scope and decided facts

Scope: Pico pins and buses plus the LPC bridge UART (r1), power architecture (r2), analog and protection circuits plus DB-9 pin correctness (r3), expander scope and doc structure (r4), DB-9 pin budget and rear-panel fit (r5).

Decided facts (binding; docs that contradict them are findings):

  • Split power. The Eurorack expander is powered only from the rack (CP1A). The MicroBrute-side breakout is powered only from the synth (TP70 +12 V, TP71 -12 V, TP72 GND). No supply rail crosses the DB-9 cable; only shared ground. DB-9 B pins 7/8 become free.
  • Two DB-9 connectors (A = outputs, B = digital + CV inputs), mounted on the MicroBrute rear panel in the Arturia "A" logo area, to the left of Pitch/Gate. No DB-25.
  • The expander gains a standalone LFO and Sample and Hold (rack-only, no synth cabling) in addition to slew limiter, clock I/O, firmware dividers and 4 aux outs. Noise, mult and attenuverter stay out.
  • Owned parts only. Parts not on the owned list are flagged with an owned alternative.
  • Back-feed protection: series resistors on the digital lines so an unpowered side is never parasitically powered.
  • No hum: ground and shield strategy must be consistent and not rely on a series capacitor in the ground.
  • firmware/pico/config.py is the canonical Pico pin source.

Conventions: CM = docs/MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md, BP = docs/MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md, BOM = docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_BOM.md, TPV = docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_TEST_POINTS_VERIFIED.md, CR = schematics/CIRCUIT_REVIEW.md, PCB = schematics/breakout_pcb.md, SB = schematics/breakout_stripboard.md, LAY = schematics/breakout_layout.svg. "svg text" means the cite is text-element order, not a line number. Source column gives the report (r1 to r5) and its own finding ID. Anything marked UNVERIFIED was marked so by the reporting reviewer and is not upgraded here.

Counts: 17 Blockers (2.1), 76 Should fix (2.2), 24 Nice (2.3), 16 conflicts (section 3), 9 owner decisions (section 4). Raw checker output is in Appendix A.

1a. Decisions (owner, 2026-10-17)

Recorded from the plan's "DECIDED (owner answers, 2026-10-17)" line and the owner's follow-up messages. These override the recommendations in section 4 where they differ.

1b. Datasheet findings (docs/DATASHEETS.md)

The datasheets collected in docs/DATASHEETS.md settle or narrow these items. Page numbers are PDF page numbers as given in DATASHEETS.md. Anything the datasheets did not prove stays UNVERIFIED.

The docs' "97/96" are power pins: pin 97 = VSS, pin 96 = VDD(3V3) (p12). 3. Conflicts between reviewers

Each conflict states the contradiction and the evidence that would settle it.

C1. DB-9 B pin map (r5 vs r2 vs r3).

  • r5 (sections 2.2 and 7.1): 1 VCA CV, 2 UART RX, 3 UART TX, 4 GND, 5 Filter CV, 6 GND, 7 SDA, 8 SCL, 9 GND (three grounds; the freed pins carry I2C).
  • r2: B:7 becomes an "MB_ALIVE" sense line (breakout spare CD40106 inverter to expander) and B:8 a second ground return or MB_GND_SENSE for a difference-amp receive; r2's back-feed table also keeps the current numbering (B:1 TX, B:2 RX, B:3/B:4 I2C, B:5/B:6 CV in).
  • r3 (H-3): B:1 TX, B:2 RX, B:3 SDA, B:4 SCL, B:5 GND, B:6 GND, B:7 Filter CV, B:8 VCA CV, B:9 GND (CVs on freed pins, flanked by guard grounds).
  • All three keep the D-sub half-pitch neighbour geometry as an UNVERIFIED assumption.
  • Settles it: (i) the datasheet or a caliper check of the exact connector confirming neighbour geometry; (ii) a decision whether any freed pin carries a signal (MB_ALIVE) or only ground; (iii) a scope or bench crosstalk measurement of Filter CV/VCA CV next to the chosen digital neighbour; (iv) the firmware GPIO budget (C9), since MB_ALIVE needs a Pico input that does not exist today.
  • Status (2026-10-17): superseded. With I2C and supplies off the cable (section 1a c, d) none of the three maps applies; the final map is in the back-feed and hum design note, section 2. Neighbour geometry still UNVERIFIED.

C2. Series resistor values.

  • r5 (7.2): UART 1k at both ends of each line; I2C 100-220 ohm at both ends; CV 10k at the expander output plus existing 1k and BAT85 at the MB; DB-9 A inputs on the expander at least 10k.
  • r2: UART 4.7k at the Pico end of TX and at the LPC end of RX; gate 10k; audio/CV 1k+1k; CV in at least 100k; no series R on I2C (instead own bus with gated pull-ups).
  • r3 (C.1): UART 1k-2.2k at the Pico end of both lines (plus 1k at the LPC end if accessible); I2C 220-470 ohm both ends; gate 1k at the CD40106 output; pitch 100-220 ohm; CV in keep 100k+ ("do not use 1k"); clock IN 100k; clock OUT 1k. r3 gives ranges; it is not silent on values.
  • Also: r3 R3-14 wants 2.2-3.3k I2C pull-ups for long cable; r5 says 4.7k is fine for 1 m and up to about 2 m; r5 notes I2C series R above a few hundred ohms breaks the low level (3 mA x 1k = 3 V).
  • Settles it: bench test with each side off in turn (parasitic voltage on the other side's rail under about 0.3 V per r5); LPC2361 and RP2040 datasheet clamp and Ioff behaviour (UNVERIFIED by all three); a measured cable capacitance with an LCR meter; the 115200-baud edge check with the chosen R and about 150 pF.
  • Status (2026-10-17): one table chosen in the design note section 3 (UART 1k at both ends per r5; CV 10k at the expander plus 100k on the MB side per r2/r3); I2C rows are moot. Values stay subject to the bench tests named there.

C3. Source of 5 V and place of the level shifter (r2 vs r3, r5 on the strip OLED).

  • r2: synth has no verified 5 V; generate a breakout-local 5 V with the owned 78L05 from +12V_BRK; move the CD4049 to the expander on Pico 3V3.
  • r3 (R3-10): the 5 V to 3.3 V stage is documented (CM:298) but not built anywhere; MB side has no 3V3; place the 4049 on the expander powered from Pico 3V3 with 1k series from A:1. r3 does not address where the CD40106's 5 V comes from; PCB/SB/CR keep "+5V" with no source.
  • r5 (F-08): power the strip OLED from "MB-side 3V3 (or 5V after F-08 checks)". r2 says the only 3V3 on the MB side is P4 pin 5 (+3V3ARM, the LPC's own supply) and warns against tapping it.
  • r2 P-E3 and r4 S14 for the expander: drop the expander 78L05 and use rack +5 V.
  • Settles it: scope/meter the MB at TP56 (+5VNUM), P4 pin 5 and TP141 for voltage and ripple (TPV marks TP56 as "per original doc" only); read the synth schematic for the +3V3ARM current margin; confirm the 78L05 dropout and dissipation at the actual +12V_BRK (r2: about 0.17 W at 25 mA); decide what the breakout actually needs 5 V for (CD40106 only, OLED, vactrol).

C4. Strip OLED supply and bus. r2: OLED from the local 5 V with module pull-ups removed, own SoftI2C bus and gated pull-ups. r5: OLED from MB 3V3, one 4.7k pair at the Pico end, shared bus. r3: 220-470 ohm series on both ends, convert via a 4049 if the module pulls up to 5 V. Settles it: measure the module's SDA-to-VCC resistance and its idle SDA voltage; measure VDD on the module with the synth off and the Pico running (r2: accept under about 0.5 V). Status (2026-10-17): moot. The strip OLED is dropped (section 1a c).

C5. Is "rear panel" the correct face (r5 vs the decided facts). r5 found the "MICROBRUTE" name and the Arturia "A" logo on the top panel in every repo photo (IMG_6964, IMG_6972), lower-left of the Pitch/Mod wheels, while the Kensington slot is on the rear. The decided facts and BP:291-292 use "rear panel". r5 could not open the 4 DNG files. Settles it: an owner photo of the rear face, square-on, with a scale, and a statement of which face is meant; the caliper list in decision 6.

C6. Stock MIDI UART (r1 vs r5/mbf_analysis).

  • r5 (F-10) and docs/research/mbf_analysis.md:210 treat the stock MIDI UART as 0xE0010000 (UART1?).
  • r1's disassembly: MIDI is UART3 at 0xE007C000; UART1 and UART2 have no literal references (not exhaustive: a run-time-built base would not show). r1 also notes mbf_analysis.md:445 itself says "0xE007C000, NOT UART0" and that CM 12D and CM 5.4 conflict.
  • Settles it: Ghidra check that nothing writes UART1/UART2 registers via a computed base; continuity probing on pins 62/63, 98/99, 85 (section 5, E-01).
  • Status (2026-10-17): partly settled by the LPC2361 datasheet (pin numbers 62/63, 98/99 confirmed, section 1b). Which UART the stock firmware uses and which pins are free stay UNVERIFIED.

C7. Ownership source. r2 cites a BOM "Component Inventory (Purchased)" section with status "Have"; r3 and r5 state docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_BOM.md has no Have/Need column and that the owned list is in CM:485-511 (r5: CM:482-512). Settles it: check which file holds the list and add a single inventory table.

C8. Which end the shield ties to and the pin-9 policy. r2 (ladder step 2): braid to ground at the expander end only, A:9 audio return and B:9 digital return meeting at TP72 on the MB and at the rack 0 V on the expander, with a B:8 ground-sense difference-amp. r5 (F-05,F-06): braid and shell to the MB end only, cut the bond at the expander hood, A:9 and B:9 both to TP72 and to one expander star. r3 (H-2): MB-side per the docs, with insulating washers at the expander end. Settles it: continuity of the shell to the panel on both ends, a measured hum with each option, and the owner's decision on cable construction. Status (2026-10-17): one rule chosen in the design note section 4 (braid and shell bonded at the MicroBrute end only, to TP72). Shell-to-panel continuity (E-15) stays UNVERIFIED.

C9. GPIO budget for r2's proposals. r1 proves all of GP0-22 are used and only GP26-28 are free. r2 proposes SoftI2C on GP26/GP27 for the strip OLED, an I2C_PU_EN GPIO, an MB_ALIVE input, and (P-F4) a gate-mirror input: five or more GPIOs against three. r1 F2 also notes GP26 PWM shares a slice with GP10. Settles it: a pin allocation in config.py that fits (for example drop the dedicated strip bus, or drop MB_ALIVE). SUPERSEDED (owner ruling 2026-10-17): main OLED is the 7-pin SPI module on SPI0 GP2/3/4/5/11; free pins GP26-28 only. Status (2026-10-17): resolved by the owner (section 1a g): 6 spare pins; r2's SoftI2C, I2C_PU_EN and MB_ALIVE are not needed.

C10. U2 part. r2 recommends 2x TL074 (owned x4); r3 recommends 2x TL072 (owned x6) with sections allocated U2A env, U2B LFO, U2C triangle, V-to-I. Settles it: a single section count and the owned stock after the decision on whether the vactrol driver stays on the breakout (r3 R3-12). Update 2026-10-17: owner has both parts in stock (TL074C ×4, TL072IP ×6); the count and split are chosen at breakout layout.

C11. TP83/gate path. r2: if TP83 is 3.3 V feed it straight via 10k to a Pico GPIO; if 5 V keep the CD40106 on local 78L05 and shift on the expander. r3: remove the pull-up, and if 3.3 V use a 3V3-powered CD40106 on the MB side, which r2 says does not exist. Settles it: bench-measure the TP83 high level and the CD40106 VT+ at the supply used.

C12. Rail protection on the MB side. r2: series 4.7-10 ohm resistor or a PPTC (not owned) instead of the 1N5817; keep 1N5817 on the expander. r3: BAT85 (owned) on MB rails, real 1N5817 for the Pico VSYS path. Settles it: choose by owned parts and the measured MB rail drop (S19).

C13. Locus of the -12 V diode error. r3 (R3-07) locates the backwards diode in SB:78 and LAY:688-689; r2 (P-C2) locates it in TROUBLESHOOTING:66-73 and says CR:12 is correct. The two do not contradict (different files) but together they show the polarity is wrong or confused in three places. Settles it: one drawn polarity (cathode toward the -12 V header) and an end-to-end check in the build.

C14. PCB/stripboard source of truth. r3 treats LAY as the correct geometry and SB as wrong (B16); SB and PCB differ on U2 (S17), board size and U1 position. Settles it: regenerate SB from LAY after the fixes in S34, then re-parse.

C15. I2C frequency and cable length. r1 F5 says code runs I2C0 at 400 kHz; docs say 100 kHz; r5 calculates 100 kHz with 4.7k is fine to about 2 m (UM10204 limits, from memory, UNVERIFIED); r3 says use 2.2-3.3k pull-ups and keep 30 cm-1 m. Settles it: measured cable capacitance and a scope of rise time at the chosen pull-up. Status (2026-10-17): moot for the cable (no I2C on the DB-9). The doc/code frequency mismatch (S05) stays as a local doc fix.

C16. 4049 input behaviour. r2 and r3 both say CD4049UB inputs may exceed VDD but that is UNVERIFIED; r5 warns the 4049 must not be used as a buffer because its input diode to VDD clamps a driven signal when its own rail is down; r3 says a 4049 input has a diode to VSS only. These are three unverified claims about one part. Settles it: the CD4049UB datasheet absolute maximum ratings and input structure (E-10). Status (2026-10-17): partly settled. TI SCHS046L p1 says VIH may exceed VCC; section 8.2.2 (PDF p17) says inputs have clamp diodes to VCC and must stay below VCC. The sheet contradicts itself; design treats the input as clamped (design note). Bench test E-10 stays.

4. Decisions needed from the owner

Each item lists the audit's recommendation first.

  1. DB-9 B final pin map and what freed pins carry.
  • Recommendation: r5's map (1 VCA CV, 2 UART RX, 3 UART TX, 4 GND, 5 Filter CV, 6 GND, 7 SDA, 8 SCL, 9 GND), because it gives Filter CV two ground neighbours and keeps all supplies off the cable. It renumbers UART and I2C in config.py comments (lines 32-42), CM 19-23 and the pin tables; it does not change code.
  • Alternatives: r3's H-3 map (CVs on 7/8 flanked by grounds, digital on 1-4 unchanged); r2's use of 7 as MB_ALIVE and 8 as ground-sense (requires a Pico GPIO, conflict C9).
  • Also decide the DB-9 A order (N21) and whether pins 7/8 may carry any signal or only ground.
  1. Series R values per line (back-feed protection).
  • Recommendation: adopt one table. Start from r5 7.2 (UART 1k at both ends; I2C 100-220 ohm; CV 10k at the expander output) and r3's 100k clock IN, subject to the bench check that the unpowered side stays under about 0.3 V with each side off. Hold off on r2's 4.7k until the check runs.
  1. 5 V source for the breakout.
  • Recommendation: breakout-local 78L05 (owned x4) from the filtered +12V_BRK (r2), and no tap on the synth's own 5 V/3V3. Move the CD4049 to the expander on Pico 3V3 (r2, r3). Confirm first that the breakout needs 5 V at all (CD40106 only, if the TP83 level allows a direct Pico input).
  1. Strip OLED supply.
  • Recommendation: do not feed the module 5 V while its pull-ups can reach the Pico GPIOs. Inspect the module's pull-ups first (multimeter SDA-to-VCC), remove them, keep one 4.7k pair at the Pico end, and power it from the breakout-local rail chosen in item 3. Choose between shared I2C0 and a separate bus once the GPIO budget (C9) is settled.
  1. Expander size (17 HP vs about 20 HP) given LFO + S&H.
  • Recommendation: 20 HP (101.3 mm, 6 columns) if the blank is not locked in, since it also gives room for LFO CV in, a second pot, LEDs and silkscreen (r4). 17 HP is feasible but tight (5-column layout, 12-14 mm knobs, no LFO CV in). First measure the owner's blank: width (the repo panel is 87 mm), mounting-hole spacing (79 mm in the file), and depth behind the panel for the Pico sub-board, 2 DB-9 and the stripboards.
  1. Rear-panel face and measurements.
  • Recommendation: confirm which face is meant (conflict C5), then take these measurements with calipers (r5 section 3.5), 0.1 mm, unit open, power off, USB and PSU unplugged:
  1. W_total (rear face outer width), H_face (from the bottom lip to the underside of the top-panel lip), and T_panel (panel wall thickness at the intended spot).
  2. X positions from the left outer edge: left and right edges of every existing feature (tuning pot hole, Kensington slot, Pitch, Gate, Pitch out jack, other jacks), giving the free width L_free.
  3. Z positions from the bottom edge: bottom and top of the free area (including any raised logo, moulding step or screw boss) and the top and bottom lips.
  4. Surface: flat or moulded; any texture or ribs inside the panel in the area (photograph; rib height and spacing).
  5. Depth: from the inside face of the panel to the first obstacle behind it (rear PCB edge, jacks, pots, screw posts, wiring), at three or more points with a depth rod.
  6. Connector: flange width and height, hole spacing centre to centre, hole diameter, D-body outer width and height, body depth behind the flange, solder-cup length, nut or jackscrew height outside.
  7. Hole-to-hole distance of the case screws nearest the area, and the PCB mounting posts behind the panel.
  • Procedure: unit face down, rear toward you, all X from the same reference, each value three times (mean), square-on photos with a ruler, tape the printed 1:1 template on before drilling, and drill a scrap piece first. No rear-panel template exists (panel/microbrute_panel_template.svg covers the top panel); draw one after the measurements. Targets from r5 (all UNVERIFIED): side by side needs about 71 mm free width and 20 mm height; stacked needs about 36 mm height and 39 mm width; about 25 mm clear depth with angled wires, 35 mm straight. The owner's "24.5 x 11 mm" cut-out figure is suspect: measure the D body and add 0.2-0.3 mm.
  1. LPC bridge UART.
  • Recommendation: keep UART1 (P0.15/P0.16) as a working assumption marked UNVERIFIED; do not trust any "UART0 is free" claim. Evidence from r1: the stock firmware uses UART3 for MIDI, UART0 appears only in a one-off read, UART1/UART2 have no references, P0.15/P0.16 share pins with SSP0/SPI that the firmware uses, and P0.2/P0.3 are the ISP port.
  • Add this continuity check to the Phase 0 checklist (docs/hardware/MACROBRUTE_PHASE0_BOM.md) as a gate before any Phase 6 bridge work, on the rear board (CU17002 "Rear Board B3"), power off, multimeter in continuity mode: (1) locate the LPC2361 LQFP-100 (right of P1_JTAG, TPV:339-341) and count from the pin-1 dot; (2) probe pin 62 (P0.15) and pin 63 (P0.16) against nearby pads and vias: continuity to a pad that can take a wire, and whether the pin goes to anything else (SPI to a shift register or DAC, LED driver, connector); (3) same for pin 98 (P0.2) and pin 99 (P0.3), and check the "separate pads near the QFP" claimed at TPV:348; (4) trace the 6N138 output (pin 6, 4.7k pull-up) to the LPC; expected pin 85 (P4.29, RXD3); (5) optionally, with the synth powered and a MIDI source, scope pin 85 for 31250 baud, and check pins 62/63 and 98/99 idle at 3.3 V; (6) record the result. Only after it passes may the docs say UART1 (or UART0) is confirmed.
  1. Parts not owned and their owned alternatives.
  • Owned (from CM:485-511 via r2/r3/r5): TL074C x4, TL072IP x6, CD4051 x2, CD40106 x3, BF245C x5, LDR04 x4, BAT85 x10, 78L05 x4, 100 nF x20, 1 uF x5, 1 nF ceramic x5, 10 uF/63 V x10, 100k pots x4, 3.5 mm jacks x25, Pico WH, three OLEDs, HW040, DB-9 connectors (count UNVERIFIED: x2 in this list, "several" per the owner on 2026-10-17; gender and flange UNVERIFIED), CD4049UBE x3, isolation transformer.
  • Recommendation by part: BAT54S, use BAT85 (2 per clamp, 4-6 of 10); 2N3904, delete the LED drivers (S12) and use an op-amp V-to-I stage for the vactrol (S37); 1N5817, BAT85 on MB-side rails and a real 1N5817 only for the Pico VSYS path (or r2's series R); 100uF/25V, 2-4x 10uF/63V in parallel per rail; ferrite bead, 10R + 10uF or omit; LF398 and a film hold cap, buy (no equivalent owned; r3 notes a CD4051 + TL072 + film cap alternative with unverified charge injection); 10M resistors, 1M; SMBJ12CA and BAT46, omit; PPTC and BZX84C3V3, skip; LM7805, not needed (78L05 is owned); CD4024, dropped; resistors, ferrites, shielded cable, hoods, insulating washers, JST-XH, Thonkiconn, 1 Mohm pots, 16-pin keyed header: not on the owned list, confirm or add to Still Need. DB-9 count needed (2 panel jacks per side plus cable ends) is UNVERIFIED.

▶ Glossary docs/MACROBRUTE_GLOSSARY.md

Acronyms, part codes, and project-specific terms that appear across the manual. Skim this once if you're new to the synth-DIY / Eurorack world — the rest of the manual leans on these without re-defining them.

Project parts of speech

Term What it means
MACROBRUTE This whole project — modified MicroBrute plus its expander (17 or about 20 HP, open), treated as one instrument.
MicroBrute (MB) The stock Arturia MicroBrute analog mono synth this project starts from.
Breakout (board) The small buffer-only stripboard mounted inside the MB that taps test points, buffers signals, and exposes them via 2× DB-9 connectors on the rear panel. Powered only from the synth (TP70/TP71/TP72).
Expander The Eurorack module (17 or about 20 HP, open) that pairs to the MB through the DB-9 cable. Self-contained — runs only from the rack's ±12 V / +5 V supply; nothing is powered over the DB-9.
Touch bolt An exposed brass bolt on the panel that, when touched, completes a circuit-bend (changes pitch / timbre / gating). The 6 selected ones are documented in touch_bend_specs.md.
Test point (TP) A pre-existing solder pad on the MB rear PCB. Numbered TP1–TP124 in Arturia's reference; this manual uses ~18 of them. See MACROBRUTE_TEST_POINTS_VERIFIED.md.
Mod ID (M01…M14) The 14 curated panel/electronic mods, indexed in macrobrute_mod_catalog.md.
Spinoff An idea that was researched but moved out of the canonical project. Currently: the JF-33 analog delay rebuild and the DSO138 oscilloscope. They live in spinoffs/.

MicroBrute architecture

Term What it means
Steiner-Parker filter The MB's voltage-controlled filter topology — multimode, distinctive snarl, will self-oscillate at high resonance.
Brute Factor The MB's signature feedback knob — routes the audio output back into the filter input for distortion / drive.
Metalizer The MB's wavefolder — adds harmonics by folding the wave around a CV-controllable threshold.
VCO / VCF / VCA Voltage-controlled oscillator / filter / amplifier — the three classic analog synth blocks the MB is built from.
LFO Low-frequency oscillator (the modulation source — typically 0.04 to 40 Hz).
ADSR / envelope Attack-Decay-Sustain-Release amplitude envelope generator.
CV Control voltage — the analog modulation signal standard. MB uses 0–5 V; Eurorack typically uses ±5 V or 1 V/oct for pitch.
Gate A binary on/off signal that triggers the envelope (typically 0 V off, 5 V on).

Connectors + pinouts

Term What it means
DB-9 The 9-pin D-sub connector used between the MB and the expander. Two of them: DB-9 A carries the 8 outputs + GND; DB-9 B carries UART TX/RX, Filter CV, VCA CV and grounds. No supply and no I²C cross the cable.
HP "Horizontal pitch", the Eurorack panel-width unit. 1 HP = 5.08 mm. The expander is 17 HP (≈ 86 mm) or about 20 HP (≈ 101 mm); width is open.
GP / GPIO General-purpose I/O pin on the Pico. GP4 = GPIO 4.
TP / TP-N See "Test point" above. Always followed by a number (TP70 = +12 V, TP72 = GND, etc.).
JF-33 / DSO138 Spinoff parts no longer in the canonical build. Search "spinoffs" if you care.

Components by part code

Part What it is
TL072 / TL074 JFET-input op-amps (dual / quad). Used for buffering MB test-point taps and Eurorack-side reception.
CD40106 Hex Schmitt-trigger inverter. Used for clean gate squaring and as the LFO core in the expander.
CD4051 8-channel analog multiplexer. Owned x2, but it has no role in the decided design.
CD4024 7-stage binary counter. Dropped: the clock dividers /2, /4, /8 are firmware.
CD4049UBE Hex inverting buffer used for the expander's clock IN/OUT buffers on Pico 3V3. Its inputs clamp to VCC (TI SCHS046L p17), so it is not used as the gate level shifter.
74HC74 Dual D flip-flop. Used in the M08 sub-harmonic divider.
LM358 / LM393 Op-amp / comparator pair. LM393 (open-collector comparator) is used for M02 active soft sync and M12 audio-rate gate.
LM13700 Dual operational transconductance amplifier (OTA). Used in M04 Metalizer VCA.
LF398 Sample-and-hold IC for the expander S&H module (not owned; needs a film hold capacitor).
78L05 / 78L09 Three-terminal +5 V / +9 V linear regulators in TO-92 packages.
2N3904 NPN small-signal transistor. Owned (kit, 10+, card contents UNVERIFIED) and not needed by the decided design (LED drivers deleted, vactrol driven by a TL072 stage, noise dropped).
1N4148 Small-signal silicon switching diode (~0.7 V drop, fast). Used as clamp / mixer diode. Owned (kit, 25+, card contents UNVERIFIED).
1N5817 Schottky diode, 20 V / 1 A (not 40 V), not owned. Intended for the Pico VSYS path; an owned 1N5819 or BAT85 can stand in.
1N5819 Schottky diode, 40 V / 1 A. Owned (x10, kit; the part and its datasheet are UNVERIFIED). May serve where a 1N5817 was wanted (provisional).
BAT54S Dual Schottky in SOT-23. Not owned; two owned BAT85 take its place as the CV-input clamp to ±supply rails.
Vactrol Optocoupler made from an LED + LDR (light-dependent resistor) pair sealed in a black package. Used for smooth, click-free resonance modulation.
MPR121 Capacitive touch sensor IC (12 channels, I²C). Optional alternative to direct touch bolts on GPIO; not owned, and no Pico pins are free for it now (I²C would need 2 of GP26-28).

Microcontrollers + protocols

Term What it means
Pico Raspberry Pi Pico (any variant with the standard 40-pin layout; RP2040 electrical facts quoted here come from the RP2040 datasheet and were not checked against Pico 2/RP2350). The owner says the variant does not matter (Pico, Pico H, WH, 2, 2H, 2WH share the 40-pin layout); nothing here uses wireless. RP2040 (Pico 1 family): 133 MHz, 264 KB SRAM, 2 MB Flash. Runs MicroPython in this project.
LPC2361 The MicroBrute's stock CPU. ARM7TDMI core, 72 MHz, 128 KB Flash, 34 KB SRAM. Custom firmware build is optional.
RP2040 The chip on the Pico (used interchangeably with "Pico" when context is clear).
MicroPython Subset of Python that runs on microcontrollers. Used for all Pico firmware in this project.
UART Asynchronous serial protocol. Used for Pico ↔ LPC2361 bridge (115 200 baud) and for MIDI (31 250 baud).
I²C Two-wire synchronous serial bus (SDA + SCL). Not used in this build: the main OLED is SPI, no I²C crosses the DB-9, and the rear Daisy Seed (EFFIGY) expansion is shelved.
SPI Synchronous serial bus with a clock (SCK), data out (MOSI), optional data in (MISO) and a chip select (CS). The main OLED uses Pico SPI0 write-only (SCK GP2, MOSI GP3) plus DC GP4 and RES GP5; the module's CS pin is tied to GND (PROVISIONAL, BT-14).
PIO RP2040's Programmable I/O — small state machines that handle precise timing-critical I/O without the CPU. Used for the clock-out generator.
PWM Pulse-width modulation. Used for LED brightness and for low-resolution analog CV output (filtered to DC).
ADC Analog-to-digital converter. Pico has 4 channels @ 12-bit.
DAC Digital-to-analog converter. The LPC2361 has a 10-bit DAC; the Pico does not (uses PWM-as-DAC).
ISP In-System Programming — the LPC2361's bootloader-mode UART flashing protocol. Used to flash custom firmware without JTAG.
CRP Code Read Protection — a one-way fuse on the LPC2361 that, if blown, prevents firmware readback. The stock MB has CRP enabled; custom firmware loads regardless.
JTAG Hardware debug interface (5-pin connector). The MB has it populated but unused in this project — printf-over-UART is the debug path.
TinyUSB The USB device-class library on the Pico that exposes it as a USB-MIDI device to the host computer.
MIDI / DIN MIDI / USB-MIDI Standard music-control protocol (31 250 baud serial). The 5-pin DIN port is on the LPC2361 path; the micro-USB port on the Pico is a separate USB-MIDI device.

Build / process terms

Term What it means
Phase 0 / Phase 1 / … The 7 sequential build phases (see MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md). Phase 0 is non-destructive bench work; Phase 3 is the irreversible panel-cutting step.
Stripboard Perfboard with horizontal copper strips already etched on the back. Cheaper than a custom PCB; cut tracks with a 3 mm drill twisted by hand.
Track cut A break deliberately made in a stripboard's copper strip — drawn as a red X in the layouts. Always verify with a multimeter.
Eurorack The dominant modular-synth format (3U panels, ±12 V power, 3.5 mm jacks, 1 V/oct CV). The expander is a Eurorack module.
Brute Factor See "MicroBrute architecture" above.
Star ground A grounding scheme where every ground wire returns to one central point, instead of daisy-chaining. Used here at TP72.
Decoupling cap A small (typically 100 nF ceramic) capacitor placed between an IC's power pin and ground, within ~10 mm of the pin. Filters supply noise.
Bias resistor A high-value (typically ≥1 MΩ) resistor that sets the DC operating point of an op-amp input when there's no DC path through the signal source.
Inline series resistor A resistor placed in series on a signal path — used here as input protection (limits fault current) and as part of summing networks.
▶ Troubleshooting & Common Pitfalls docs/MACROBRUTE_TROUBLESHOOTING.md

Real failure modes, organized by phase. Most of these come from schematics/CIRCUIT_REVIEW.md, docs/firmware/lpc2361_investigation_guide.md, and the Phase 0 bench-validation notes — collected here so you can spot them before they bite.

If you hit something not on this page, check the original review docs; they go deeper on the analog circuits.

Phase 0 — Bench validation (Pico + breadboard)

The OLED shows nothing

The main display is the 1.3″ 7-pin SPI OLED on SPI0, write-only: SCK GP2 (module D0), MOSI GP3 (D1), DC GP4, RES GP5; the module's CS pin is tied to GND (PROVISIONAL, BT-14). SPI has no address and no scan; the driver is display.py (OLED_SPI), and test_hw.py's OLED test draws a test frame through it.

Fix: check the module pin order against its silkscreen (UNVERIFIED; the common order is GND, VCC, D0, D1, RES, DC, CS), that D0/D1 are not swapped, that RES is driven high after reset and CS really is on GND, then VCC and GND. If CS on GND does not work (BT-14 fails), move CS back to a GPIO and set OLED_CS to it (connection map 12G). If the picture is shifted by two columns or shows a stripe at the edge, the chip is probably SH1106 (UNVERIFIED): set OLED_CHIP="SH1106" and OLED_COL_OFFSET=2 (BF Q22).

KY-040 encoder reports two ticks per detent

The KY-040 module has on-board 10 kΩ pull-ups and the firmware enables Pin.PULL_UP on GP13/14/15. That's intentional — without it the rotational A/B sequence is too noisy on long jumper wires. Two-ticks-per-detent usually means contact bounce on a worn or cheap encoder.

Fix: wire the optional 10 kΩ + 100 nF RC filter shown in schematics/pico_pinout.md (Hardware Debounce section). Adds ~1 ms of lag, kills the bounce.

RGB LED is always lit — pin LOW makes it brighter

You probably have a common-anode RGB LED instead of common-cathode. They look identical; only the long-lead position is different (CC: long lead = cathode = GND; CA: long lead = anode = +3V3). With CA wired into a CC firmware, pulling the GPIO LOW lights the LED.

Fix: verify the part with a multimeter (diode-test mode + the long lead will be the common one). Either swap to a CC LED or invert the firmware duty cycle in firmware/pico/leds.py.

Centre-channel jumpers cross the Pico body

The Pico straddles the breadboard centre channel along its long axis. A straight vertical drop from a top-edge pin to a bottom-row peripheral pierces the Pico body. Use the drop columns shown in schematics/phase0_breadboard.svg — the ones in the gap between the Pico and the encoder/RGB blocks.

Pico won't enumerate after firmware copy

If main.py raises an exception at boot, the Pico sometimes won't expose the USB MicroPython filesystem. Hold BOOTSEL when plugging in to enter the RP2 bootloader, then reflash MicroPython. Your main.py is preserved on the FAT partition.

Phase 1 — Breakout board build

-12V rail measures +12V (or vice versa)

The protection diode on the -12V rail (an owned BAT85 or 1N5819, or a 1N5817 if one is bought) must be installed with the cathode toward the TP71 / -12 V header side and the anode toward the breakout rail (audit B15). The old text here said the opposite. Installed the wrong way round, the diode blocks the normal -12 V current and the V- pins float near 0 V.

Fix: check the band orientation on each diode before powering up. The band marks the cathode: it goes to the -12 V (TP71) side. Multimeter diode-test mode: probe red on the plain (anode) side and black on the band (cathode) side, you should read the Schottky forward drop (BAT85 about 0.24 V at 0.1 mA, 0.4 V at 10 mA).

TL074 outputs sit at +12V (or -12V) when no signal applied

The +IN pin is floating. The MicroBrute test points are AC-coupled at the tap, so each op-amp +IN needs a DC bias path to GND.

Fix: add 10 MΩ from each +IN pin to GND (rows 8/10 in the breakout layout). Sets the operating point at 0 V, doesn't load the high-impedance test point. See CIRCUIT_REVIEW.md §2.

Ferrite beads (FB1/FB2) burning hot

Ferrite beads are not part of the decided breakout power chain (they are not owned; audit S20 and decision 8). If you did fit them, a bead's rating is an impedance at 100 MHz, not a DC resistance, and cheap ones run hot at full op-amp current. Omit the beads, or use 10 Ω in series with 2-4× 10 µF in parallel where filtering is wanted (CM 5.3).

TL074 audio sounds clipped or distorted at line-level

TL074 output current = 50 mA max. Driving a 600 Ω headphone = ~10 mA at line level — fine. Driving a 32 Ω earbud = ~50 mA = at the edge. Driving a 8 Ω speaker = blown op-amp.

Fix: ensure the breakout's outputs only feed line-level inputs. If you need to drive headphones, use the TL072 follower at the destination, not the TL074 directly.

Phase 2 — Internal wiring

Static pop / click when touching breakout board

ESD discharge through ungrounded fingers into the bias-resistor input. Won't damage CMOS in the breakout (BAT54S clamps it) but it will pop the audio output.

Fix: wear an antistatic wrist strap when working on the open synth, or touch the chassis ground (TP72) before each session. Also: the touch bolts are deliberately exposed — those will pop too, by design.

Audio bleeding from one buffered output into another

Ground loop. TP72 is the MicroBrute-side star ground. Every DB-9 ground pin and the breakout ground go to TP72 by their own short wires, not through the breakout's ground strip and not via the MicroBrute's own ground rail.

Fix: verify your wiring against MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md section 11. The rule is load-bearing: the DB-9 ground conductors (A:9; B:2, 4, 7, 8, 9) are the ONLY ground connection between the synth and the rack.

Test-point voltage on a multimeter is "noisy" / unstable

That's fine — most TPs are AC signals (waveform taps, LFO, etc.) and your multimeter is averaging them poorly. Probe with an oscilloscope, not a multimeter, for anything that's an audio or modulation signal. Use the multimeter only for DC checks (TP70/71/72 = ±12V/-12V/GND).

Phase 3 — Panel modifications (irreversible)

Drilled hole is the wrong size for the jack/toggle

Always measure the thread of the part, not the body. A "6 mm" jack typically has 6 mm threads but a 7 mm body — the panel hole needs to be 6.2–6.3 mm so the threads pass with clearance.

Fix: test-fit every part against a scrap of identical panel material before drilling the synth. The provided panel/microbrute_panel_template.svg shows tested hole diameters — print at 1:1 and pinprick the centres.

Panel paint chips around the drilled hole

You drilled too fast or used a worn bit. The MicroBrute panel is anodized aluminum, brittle on the surface.

Fix: mark the centre with a punch. Drill in stages: 2 mm pilot → 3 mm → 5 mm → final size. Keep RPM low (300-500), feed slow, use a sharp HSS bit. A drop of cutting fluid helps.

Touch bolt makes no sound when touched

Most likely either (a) you've isolated it with a track cut you didn't mean to make, (b) the series safety resistor is too high (try 1 kΩ–10 kΩ range), or (c) the bolt isn't electrically connected to anything bendable (a "ground" bolt has nothing to bend — it just provides the return path).

Fix: with a multimeter on continuity, probe between the bolt and the TP it's supposed to bend. You should see your safety resistor's value. If you see open circuit, the wire's broken or the track's cut.

Phase 5 — System integration (DB-9 cable)

Audio sounds different through the expander vs. direct from synth

Expected: the A outputs are buffered on the MicroBrute side, and the expander jacks are passive. Sound should be ~indistinguishable. If you hear hum, work through the fallback ladder in MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md section 11 (BF 4.5), in order, and measure after each step.

Fix: the shield rule is one end only: the braid is bonded to its connector shell at the MicroBrute end, that shell is wired with a short lead to TP72, and at the expander end the braid is cut back and insulated and the panel shell is isolated from the aluminium panel (insulating shoulder washers, BF 4.2). A molded off-the-shelf cable bonds the braid at both hoods and must be modified. The ground conductors are terminated at both ends. The older advice here to pick the expander end is replaced; swapping the bond to the expander end is ladder step 3, to be tried only if hum persists. Never connect USB to the Pico while the DB-9 cables are connected.

Eurorack modules see noise / tick on +12V rail

The CP1A or other PSU is shared between expander + other Eurorack modules. The expander's digital section (LFO Schmitt trigger) injects edges onto +12V if not decoupled.

Fix: add 100 µF electrolytic + 100 nF ceramic across +12V/GND on the expander board, near the noisy IC. The breakout has these by design; expander often forgets them.

Firmware (Pico + LPC2361)

Pico USB-MIDI doesn't show up on the host

The TinyUSB stack inits during the first 100 ms of boot. If your host opens the device too fast, it can race.

Fix: unplug, wait 2 s, replug. If still nothing, check usbmidi.py is imported in main.py and the host has USB-MIDI class drivers (built into macOS, Windows, modern Linux).

LPC2361 ISP entry hangs at "Synchronized?"

Two probable causes: (a) the LPC isn't actually in ISP mode (P0.14 must be LOW at reset — the rear ISP header pulls this), or (b) baud-rate mismatch.

Fix: verify ISP mode pin with a scope or LED. Use 115 200 baud first (the LPC's ISP supports auto-baud but the host has to send the magic "?" sync at the right rate). See lpc2361_investigation_guide.md.

CRP fuse blown on the LPC2361 — can't read out original firmware

Expected — Arturia ships with CRP1 enabled. You can still flash new firmware (writes work), you just can't dump the existing image back out. The decrypted .mbf binary in firmware/ (recovered from Arturia's update file) is your reference.

Pico ↔ LPC2361 UART bridge sees garbage characters

Three things to check, in order:

  1. TX/RX crossed? Pico GP0 (TX) → DB-9 B:1 → LPC P0.16 (RXD1, pin 63);

Pico GP1 (RX) ← DB-9 B:6 ← LPC P0.15 (TXD1, pin 62). It's a cross — tx-to-rx, not tx-to-tx. The LPC UART is UART1, UNVERIFIED until the Phase 0 continuity check passes; if the check found those pins taken, the bridge may use the ISP UART (pins 98/99) instead.

  1. Common ground? Both processors must share GND. Verify TP72 (LPC

side) reads continuous to GND on the Pico side through the cable ground pins. Check the 1 kΩ series resistors at both ends and that the Pico keeps GP0 as an input until GP1 reads high (BF 3.1).

  1. Baud rate? Both ends configured for 115 200 8-N-1. Mismatch shows

up as repeating but garbled bytes (right framing, wrong content).

When in doubt

  • Re-read the relevant phase in MACROBRUTE_BUILD_PLAN.md. It's

written linearly — the gotcha is often called out two paragraphs after the step you're on.

  • Check MACROBRUTE_CONNECTION_MAP.md. The canonical wiring

reference. If your wiring disagrees with it, your wiring is wrong.

  • Check MACROBRUTE_GLOSSARY.md if a term in an error message looks

unfamiliar.

  • Open an issue / write it down for next time. If you hit a

pitfall not on this page, that's worth a note in docs/research/.

If the synth still works when you unplug everything you've added, you've succeeded — the project is incremental on purpose, and the stock MicroBrute should be untouched throughout Phases 0–2.
